For every transition t, delivery δ and outcome r: the passthrough tag ends with r on t and δ exactly when r is completion with no token.
For every tag x: isPT x holds exactly when x is the passthrough tag.
For every call k on an input i that gives no action: if the call returns an instance x, the definition of x carries the passthrough tag.
For all retrievals k and j: pt k equals pt j, and isPT holds of pt k.
quotes: *When* a transition fires under the built-in passthrough action, the action *shall* complete with no output token and *shall not* fail.
The identity predicate *shall* accept the built-in passthrough action and reject every other action, including `fork()` ([CORE-052]) and a hand-written action that produces no token.
*When* a transition is built without an action, the built transition *shall* carry the built-in passthrough action.
Every retrieval of the built-in passthrough action *shall* yield the same instance, which the identity predicate accepts.
assumes: The model is the tuple (interp, isPT, B, pt). An action is read as its identity tag (Act, Reference/Build.lean): the built-in passthrough or another action named by an opaque id; this is the tag CORE-020, CORE-042 and CORE-043 carry on a built transition (TransDef). interp tag is the action relation (ActionRel, Spec/GlossaryAction.lean) the tag names; the reference is Act.interp I, the passthrough tag naming refPassthrough and other x naming I x, for every table I of other actions. isPT is the identity predicate on tags; the reference is Act.isPassthrough, the predicate the CORE-043 compile check reads (refCompile). B is CORE-020's transition builder (TBuilder); the reference is refTransBuild. pt k is the tag the k-th retrieval of the built-in returns (Rust passthrough(), Java TransitionAction.passthrough(), TypeScript passthrough(), Python libpetri.passthrough); the reference is refRetrievePassthrough.

Two actions are the same instance exactly when their tags are equal. A runtime action is an object compared by reference (Rust Arc::ptr_eq, rust/libpetri-core/src/action.rs:75-77; Java ==, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionAction.java:65-67; TypeScript ===, typescript/src/core/transition-action.ts:32-34); a fresh closure per retrieval is a fresh tag (CORE_051_forbids_freshPerRetrieval). Python's built-in is the enum member BuiltinAction.Passthrough, mapped to Rust's singleton (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:238-243), so Python carries the tag itself; a Python callable that produces nothing is another action. Python exposes no identity predicate; line 2 is read there through the Rust one the compile check calls.

An explicitly bound null or undefined is not an action and is outside the model: the model's only absent action is TransIn.action = none, Rust cannot express a null action, and Python's builder raises TypeError on one (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:276-287). Java's Transition.Builder.action(null) and TypeScript's action(null) store it (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Transition.java:367-370, typescript/src/core/transition.ts:222-225); the identity predicate rejects it, so CORE-043's check passes such a transition and every firing then fails. That acceptance is recorded as a Java and TypeScript builder defect (RD-06 in spec/runtime-defects.md: the setter should reject null as Python does), not read as 'built without an action', and line 3 is not weakened for it.

Line 1 reads the first sentence at the level of the action: on every transition and delivery the passthrough tag completes, with no token, and has no other outcome, so it never fails (rust/libpetri-core/src/action.rs:86-88 returns Ok(()), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionAction.java:80-81 returns a completed future, typescript/src/core/transition-action.ts:24 is async () => {}; Python runs Rust's Passthrough, rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:238-243). A passthrough that copies its input token to every output place is fork() (CORE-052): it agrees with passthrough on a sink and violates line 1 on a transition with an output place (CORE_051_mutant_sinkOnly_killed); a passthrough that fails violates it on every delivery (CORE_051_forbids_failing). That a firing under the passthrough tag deposits nothing is line 1 with CORE-050's line 2 (core051_fire_nil), and that a transition built without an action deposits nothing when a firing ends with its action is line 3 on top (core051_default_fire_nil).

The body's 'consumes input tokens' describes the firing, not the action: what a firing consumes is CORE-030's and EXEC-010's, whatever its action. 'Completes immediately' (AC1) is line 1 for 'completes'. 'Immediately' (no task dispatch, the action runs inline on the orchestrator thread) is a claim about thread placement, kind Q: the Lean model has no threads, so no Lean block states it, and it is checked by tests (CONC-011 AC1, 'Passthrough actions execute inline without task dispatch').

Line 2 reads 'recognisable by identity' as an exact characterisation over tags: the predicate accepts the built-in and rejects every other tag, whatever that action does. An extensional predicate that also accepts a hand-written action producing no token violates it (CORE_051_mutant_acceptsBuiltin_killed). fork() is rejected because its tag is not the passthrough tag: on a one-place self-loop that delivers one token, an action satisfying CORE-052 emits a copy of it, while line 1 allows the passthrough tag no token there, so the tag of every fork satisfying CORE-052 differs from the passthrough tag and line 2 rejects it (core051_fork_ne); at the example table, other fork names the reference fork refFork (core051_reference_fork). Every predicate satisfying line 2 is Act.isPassthrough (core051_isPT_eq), so CORE-043's check, stated over action = passthrough, reads the same nets under any such predicate.

Line 3 reads the body's 'This is the default action for transitions without explicitly bound actions' at build time: a transition built without an action carries the built-in (rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:256, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Transition.java:247, typescript/src/core/transition.ts:152, and Python's builder rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:421-424, None => passthrough()). Line 3 is conditional on a successful build; that a transition given no action builds at all is CORE-020's line 4, and with it such a transition exists and carries the built-in (core051_default_builds). A builder that requires an action fails every build without one, satisfies line 3 vacuously, and is rejected by CORE-020's line 4 (core051_requiredAction_joint). Binding later (bindActions) is CORE-042's, which keeps the tag of an unbound transition. A builder whose default is a hand-written no-op behaves the same at every firing and violates the line (CORE_051_mutant_behaviouralDefault_killed): CORE-043's check would then miss an output-declaring transition left at the default.

Line 4 reads 'a stable singleton rather than a fresh closure per call' and the first half of AC3: every retrieval yields one instance and the predicate accepts it. A retrieval whose first call returns the built-in and whose later calls return fresh actions violates it (CORE_051_mutant_firstRetrieval_killed), and so does one that returns a fresh action on every call (CORE_051_forbids_freshPerRetrieval). By line 2, line 4 says every retrieval is the passthrough tag (core051_pt_eq). Python's retrieval is the module constant libpetri.passthrough (python/libpetri/model.py:23, the enum member BuiltinAction.Passthrough), so every access yields the same instance and line 4 holds there by construction.
AC1 (passthrough action completes immediately) is line 1 for 'completes'; 'immediately' is left to tests (CONC-011 AC1) as above.
AC2 (no output tokens are produced) is line 1: the only outcome is completion with no token.
AC3 (repeated retrieval yields the same instance, and an identity predicate accepts the built-in and rejects every other action, including fork()) is lines 4 and 2, with core051_fork_ne for fork().

The test derivation (fire a sink transition with passthrough and see no output token; retrieve the built-in twice and see identity) is CORE_051_nonvacuous: the reference action firing of a sink under the passthrough tag deposits nothing, two retrievals are equal and accepted, and the predicate rejects fork() and a hand-written no-op.

requirements.title: Fork Action
requirements.statement:
fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] val Fork ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),
    (∀ (i : N) (x : T),
        core052_soleInput t i →
          δ.inputs i = [x] →
            ∃ e,
              Fork t δ = Except.ok e ∧
                ∀ (p : N),
                  List.map val (EmittedTo e p) = if OutputArc t p then [val x] else []) ∧
      ((¬∃ i, core052_soleInput t i) →
          (∀ p ∈ inPlaces t, δ.inputs p ≠ []) → ∃ msg, Fork t δ = Except.error msg) ∧
        ∀ (i : N) (x y : T) (ys : List T),
          core052_soleInput t i →
            δ.inputs i = x :: y :: ys →
              (∃ msg, Fork t δ = Except.error msg) ∨
                ∃ e,
                  Fork t δ = Except.ok e ∧
                    ∀ (p : N),
                      List.map val (EmittedTo e p) = if OutputArc t p then [val x] else []
requirements.scope: all implementations (the built-in fork action; Python rides on the Rust action)
reading: For every value projection val and every fork action function Fork, for every transition t and every delivery δ:

for every place i and token x, if i is the sole input place of t (the input places of t, as a set, are {i}) and δ delivers exactly [x] from i, then Fork t δ completes with an emission e such that, for every place p, the values of the tokens e sends to p are [val x] if t's output spec names p and [] otherwise;
if t has no sole input place (it has none, or two or more) and every input place of t delivered at least one token in δ, then Fork t δ fails with some message;

for every place i and tokens x, y, ys, if i is the sole input place of t and δ delivers x :: y :: ys from i (x the oldest), then Fork t δ either fails with some message or completes with an emission e such that, for every place p, the values of the tokens e sends to p are [val x] if t's output spec names p and [] otherwise.
quotes: A built-in fork action that copies a single input token value to all declared output places.

*When* the fork action runs for a transition with exactly one input place and the firing consumed exactly one token from that place, the action *shall* complete with one token carrying that token's value in every place the output spec names and with no token in any other place.
*If* the transition does not have exactly one input place, *then* the fork action *shall* fail.

*When* the firing consumed two or more tokens from the single input place, the fork action *shall* either fail or complete with one token carrying the oldest consumed token's value in every place the output spec names and with no token in any other place.

**Divergence:** when the firing consumed two or more tokens from the single input place, the fork action copies the oldest consumed token to every output place in Java, Rust and Python and fails in TypeScript.

**Note:** The fork action writes every place the output spec names, so on an output spec `Xor(a, b)` with two different places it writes both, and an executor with output validation enabled rejects its completion ([IO-015], [EXEC-021]).
assumes: The fork action is read as an action function (ActionFn, Spec/GlossaryAction.lean): from the transition and the delivery δ (the consumed tokens per input place in consumption order, oldest first, and the read tokens per read place) to a completion with an emission (places and tokens, in emission order) or a failure. It reads nothing else, so a function, not a relation. Where the tokens it completes with go is CORE-050's line 2 (the firing deposits exactly them, AF := refActionFire with the action ActionFn.rel Fork).

Values, not tokens: val x is the value a token carries (CORE-003's projection; none for a unit token when V is an Option). Every runtime deposits a new token with a fresh created_at carrying the consumed value (Rust epoch_now in the output path, Java and TypeScript ctx.output), so lines 1 and 3 compare (EmittedTo e p).map val with [val x]. A fork that emits the consumed token itself (refFork) and one that emits a new token with the same value (CORE_052_allows_freshStamp) both satisfy them; a fork that emits another value violates them (CORE_052_forbids_otherValue).

'Exactly one input place' is a set condition (core052_soleInput): the input places are the places of t's input arcs, read and reset arcs excluded. Java and TypeScript count the declared input places (ctx.inputPlaces()); Rust counts input_place_names, the keys of the consumed-input map, which are the input places that delivered a token. The two counts agree on every delivery in which each input place delivered at least one token, and every firing is such a delivery (IO-002, IO-004 AC1: every input arc requires at least one token). Line 2 is stated for those deliveries only, so a fork that counts as Rust does satisfies the block (CORE_052_allows_rustCount). Lines 1 and 3 need no such premise: the sole input place delivered there. A transition with two input arcs on one place is rejected when it is built (CORE-030) and is covered by the set reading either way.

'Every place the output spec names' is OutputArc (glossary: Output arc; IO-017's set): every place of the spec, Xor alternatives, the Timeout child and ForwardInput targets included (Rust output_place_names over allowed_outputs, Java Transition.outputPlaces, TypeScript ctx.outputPlaces()). A transition without an output spec names no place, so fork completes with no token there. Lines 1 and 3 compare per place, not as a list: Rust iterates a HashSet of output places, so the emission order is not fixed and the block does not fix it.

Line 1 has three parts, each with a wrong fork that meets a plausible weaker reading: every output place gets a copy (the fork that writes only the first output place meets 'tokens only in output places, carrying the value', CORE_052_mutant_onlyOutputs_killed); exactly one copy (a fork that writes two copies meets the old AC2, 'produces the input value to all output places', CORE_052_mutant_ac2Literal_killed_double); and nothing elsewhere (a fork that also writes back to its input place meets the same reading, CORE_052_mutant_ac2Literal_killed_echo). AC2 is reworded to state the three parts.

Line 2 includes zero input places: AC1 says 'requires exactly one input place', and all three runtimes fail on any count other than one (rust/libpetri-core/src/action.rs Fork::run_sync, java TransitionAction.fork, typescript transition-action.ts fork), with the message 'Fork requires exactly 1 input place, found n'. AC3 said 'more than one input place' and is reworded to 'not exactly one' under ruling D20 (R-CB6). A fork that completes with no token on a transition without input places meets AC3's old wording and violates line 2 (CORE_052_mutant_ac3Literal_killed); a fork that accepts two input places and copies the first violates it too (CORE_052_forbids_acceptTwo). The message text is not stated.

Ruling D50 (a): line 1 is stated for a firing that consumed exactly one token from the sole input place, and the batch case (two or more, from an Exactly(n), All or AtLeast input) is left undecided between the runtimes' two behaviours: Java and Rust copy the oldest consumed token (Java ctx.input returns the first token of the batch, Rust's fork reads input_raw, which takes the first token), Python rides on Rust, and TypeScript fails (ctx.input throws on a count other than one). Both satisfy the block (CORE_052_reference, CORE_052_reference_strict) and differ on a batch (CORE_052_batch_undecided); the spec records which runtime does which in its Divergence note. Line 3 changes no runtime and picks neither: it only excludes what neither runtime does and what the headline 'copies a single input token value' excludes, a fork that copies every token of the batch and one that copies the newest (CORE_052_mutant_noBatch_killed_all, CORE_052_mutant_noBatch_killed_newest). AC4 states line 3.

The same option (exactly-one premise, batch undecided) is taken for input() in CORE-060. The runtimes' batch behaviour differs between the two in Rust and Python, where fork reads input_raw (the oldest token) and input() reports an error, so the two Divergence notes put Rust on different sides. A delivery of no token from the sole input place does not arise from a firing (IO-002, IO-004 AC1); both readings fail on it and the block says nothing of it.

Consequence with CORE-050 and IO-015 (core052_xor_never_fires), the Note: fork writes every place of the spec, so on Xor(a, b) with a ≠ b its emission fills no output branch and no reference action firing ends with the fork action; the executor's output validation rejects the completion (EXEC-021). Under the validation skip of CONC-026 the completion is not checked, which is CONC-026's. The block does not restate this; it follows from line 1 and refActionFire.

That every output place must accept the input value's type (Java's javadoc) is CORE-003's compatibility, owed by the net's author; a null value is propagated as a value like any other. That fork is a built-in with a constructor (fork() in each language, BuiltinAction in Python) is API shape. Whether it runs synchronously (Rust is_sync) is CONC-011's.

AC1 (requires exactly one input place) is line 2 with line 1's premise. AC2 (exactly one token carrying the input value in each output place and none elsewhere) is line 1. AC3 (throws or errors if the transition does not declare exactly one input place) is line 2. AC4 (on two or more consumed tokens, fails or copies the oldest as in AC2) is line 3. The test derivation (fork with one input and three outputs; all three receive the same value) is CORE_052_nonvacuous: on And(Place 1, And(Place 2, Place 3)) the reference fork completes with 7 in places 1, 2 and 3, and the reference action firing deposits them.

requirements.title: Transform Action
requirements.statement:
fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] val X ↦
  (∀ (f : TransformFn N T V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T)
      (e : List (N × T)),
      X f t δ (Except.ok e) →
        ∃ w v, f t δ (Except.ok (w, v)) ∧ TransformCopies val t w v e) ∧
    (∀ (f : TransformFn N T V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T)
        (w : List (N × T)) (v : V),
        f t δ (Except.ok (w, v)) →
          (∃ x, val x = v) → ∃ e, X f t δ (Except.ok e) ∧ TransformCopies val t w v e) ∧
      ∀ (f : TransformFn N T V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (m : String),
        X f t δ (Except.error m) → ∃ m', f t δ (Except.error m')
reading: Let X be the transform: X f is the action built from the host's function f; f t δ (ok (w, v)) says that one call of f, handed the transition t and the delivery δ, may return v after writing w through the context, and f t δ (error m) that one call may fail; val reads the value a token carries.

For every function f, transition t, delivery δ and emission e: if the action X f, handed t and δ, completes with e, then some single call of f on that same t and δ wrote w and returned v, and in every place the output specification of t names e holds the tokens w sent there followed by exactly one token carrying v, and in every other place exactly the tokens w sent there.

For every function f, transition t, delivery δ, writes w and value v that some token carries: if one call of f, handed t and δ, may write w and return v, then X f, handed t and δ, may complete with an emission of that shape for w and v.
For every function f, transition t, delivery δ and message m: if the action X f, handed t and δ, fails with m, then some call of f on that same t and δ fails.
quotes: *When* a transition fires under the transform action, the action *shall* call its function with the transition context of that firing, and *shall* complete or fail with the outcome of one such call.

*When* the function returns a value, the transform action *shall* complete with the output tokens the function wrote through the context, followed in every place the output spec names by one token carrying that value.
assumes: The model is the pair (val, X). X is the transform combinator: from the host's function f (TransformFn: a relation from the transition and what the firing delivered to the outcome of one call, either the tokens the function wrote through the context and the value it returned, or a failure) it gives the action X f (ActionRel, Spec/GlossaryAction.lean; glossary: Action). val : T → V reads the value a token carries, so tokens are compared on their values, never on their identity or creation stamp: the stamp of a copied token is the host's (CORE-011), and Rust stamps each copy at its own output call (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs output_raw). The witness is refTransform val.

The function is a relation, not a function, because it may read the world: one delivery may give more than one value, or a value on one call and a failure on another. That is what makes 'one such call' a line: a transform that calls the function once per output place may copy a different value to each place (CORE_053_mutant_perPlace_killed), and a transform whose emission is the writes of two calls is no single call's writes.

How many times the function is called beyond the call that accounts for the outcome is not observable in a relational model, and a transform that makes an extra call and discards its result is not excluded: the first sentence says which call the outcome comes from, not how many calls are made.

Line 1 reads both sentences from the completion's side: the function is called on the transition context of the firing (the transition and the delivery the action was handed; CORE-050 line 1 makes that the firing's delivery), and the completion is one call's writes followed by the copies. Its accessors (input, inputs, inputToken, read, output) are CORE-060 to CORE-063's. A transform that hands the function an empty context (CORE_053_forbids_blind), that drops what the function wrote (CORE_053_forbids_dropWrites), that puts the copy before what the function wrote (CORE_053_forbids_copiesFirst), that writes only the first output place (CORE_053_forbids_firstOnly) or that copies once per occurrence of a place the output specification names twice (CORE_053_forbids_rawList) violates it.

Line 1 is stated per place (EmittedTo): the order of the copies across places is not stated. Rust iterates a hash set of the output places, Java and TypeScript iterate the transition's output place set; each place receives exactly one copy, after what the function wrote there, which is what the marking sees (EXEC-020 appends per place in emission order).

Line 2 reads the second sentence's 'shall complete' from the side of the call: a call of the function that returns a value gives a completion. A transform that never ends, with neither a completion nor a failure, holds of lines 1 and 3 alone (CORE_053_mutant_soundOnly_killed). The premise that some token carries v holds in every runtime (any value can be put in a token) and keeps the line true at every model type.

Line 3 reads 'complete or fail with the outcome of one such call' and the second sentence's 'shall complete' from the side of a failure: the transform fails only when a call of its function on the same transition and delivery fails, so a transform that may fail after its function returned, such as a copy loop whose output call can fail, violates it (CORE_053_mutant_noFailLine_killed). The failure's message is not compared. Rust's function returns a value and has no failure channel, and its copy loop names only declared output places, so its output call does not fail there and the Rust transform never fails; Java and TypeScript catch the function's exception and fail the action, as the reference does with the call's message.

Whether a failing call must make the transform fail, and how a failure is handled, are EXEC-030's. The function's own writes are output calls through the context, so which places they may name is CORE-062 and CORE-063's: when every write list the function returns is built by output calls of a context that meets CORE-062 line 1, the transform writes through that context (refTransform_throughCtx), and an action that writes through a context whose output calls append only on output places deposits only in output places (ctx_deposits_outputs, core053_deposits_outputs). The execution context of CORE-064 is not modelled.

The place set is the glossary's output arc (OutputArc: every place the output specification names, all branches of an XOR, the child of a Timeout, the destination of a ForwardInput), the same set every runtime hands the context (rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs all_places; Java Transition.outputPlaces; TypeScript TransitionContext.outputPlaces). On a specification with more than one output branch the copies fill every branch, so the completion fills no single branch and the firing ends with no completion of the action (IO-015, EXEC-021; core053_xor_never_fires). The markdown's note under CORE-053 says so for the reader.

In the joint model a firing that ends with the completion of the transform deposits that completion (CORE-050 line 2), so it deposits one call's writes followed by one copy per output place (core053_firing_copies).
AC1 (the function receives the transition context) is line 1: the call that accounts for the completion is a call on the transition and the delivery the action was handed (CORE_053_forbids_blind).

AC2 (the return value is produced to all output places) is lines 1 and 2: every completion carries one token with the returned value in every place the output specification names, and every returned value gives such a completion (CORE_053_forbids_firstOnly). transform(place, fn), transformFrom and transformAsync are API shape, not encoded.

The test derivation (a transform that doubles an integer input; all outputs receive the doubled value) is CORE_053_nonvacuous: the doubling function on a delivery of 7, under AND(Place 1, Place 2), completes with 14 in place 1 and 14 in place 2, and the reference action firing deposits both; besides, a function that fails makes the reference transform fail, so the premise of line 3 is met.

requirements.title: Produce Action
requirements.statement:
fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] value produce ↦
  (∀ (p : N) (v : V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),
      OutputArc t p → (∃ x, value x = v) → ∃ r, produce p v t δ r) ∧
    (∀ (p : N) (v : V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T)
        (r : Except String (List (N × T))),
        OutputArc t p → produce p v t δ r → ∃ x, r = Except.ok [(p, x)] ∧ value x = v) ∧
      (∀ (p : N) (v : V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),
          ¬OutputArc t p → ∃ r, produce p v t δ r) ∧
        ∀ (p : N) (v : V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T)
          (r : Except String (List (N × T))),
          ¬OutputArc t p → produce p v t δ r → ∃ m, r = Except.error m
requirements.scope: the built-in produce action of Java, TypeScript and Rust (the Python binding exposes no produce built-in)
reading: For every value projection value and every produce action family produce (produce p v is the built-in action that produces the value v to the place p), every place p, value v, transition t and delivery δ:
if the output specification of t names p and some token carries v, produce p v ends on t and δ in some way;

if the output specification of t names p, every way produce p v ends on t and δ is a completion with the emission [(p, x)] for a token x whose value is v: exactly one output token, in p, and no token in any other place;
if the output specification of t does not name p, produce p v ends on t and δ in some way;
if the output specification of t does not name p, every way produce p v ends on t and δ is a failure.
quotes: *When* the built-in produce action of a place and a value runs on a transition whose output spec names that place, the action *shall* complete with exactly one output token, which carries that value and goes to that place, and with no output token in any other place.
*If* the built-in produce action of a place and a value runs on a transition whose output spec does not name that place, *then* the action *shall* fail.
assumes: The model is the pair (value, produce). value : T → V reads a token's value; T is the queue model's token identities, each carrying its value and its creation timestamp. produce p v is an action (ActionRel, Spec/GlossaryAction.lean): a relation from a transition and the delivery to how the action ends, completing with an emission (places and tokens, in emission order) or failing with a message. The value is fixed: on every transition whose output spec names p, whatever the delivery, every completion of produce p v carries v (line 2), so every such firing produces the same value. The witness is refProduce value, the single output call output(p, v) on the reference context refCtx (core054_ctxProduce), which mirrors the three runtimes (rust/libpetri-core/src/action.rs:165-168, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionAction.java:179-184, typescript/src/core/transition-action.ts:89-93: one ctx.output call, then completion).

ActionRel records the ways an action ends, not whether every run ends: an action that ends on some runs and not on others is the relation of its endings, so a run that does not end is outside this block, and lines 1 and 3 rule out only an action that has no way to end at all. The three runtimes end after the one output call (Rust run_sync returns, Java returns a completed future, the TypeScript async function returns or throws).

The block states the value, not the token: line 2 fixes the place and the value of the one token, and the token's creation timestamp is out of scope for this block. That an output token carries the epoch clock reading at its output call is CORE-035 AC2 and CORE-011, whose executor line is the W11 block; a produce action that builds its token once and hands that same token to every firing (the Java metadata overload ctx.output(Place, Token), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:295) meets this block and is for that line to reject. The runtimes stamp at the output call (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:401-416, created_at from the epoch clock). The premise of line 1 that some token carries v holds of every runtime's token type, which carries any value of its type; it is there because the block is stated over an abstract token type.

'A transition whose output spec names that place' is OutputArc t p (glossary: Output arc; CORE-035, IO-017). On a place the output specification does not name, the output call reports an error and leaves no entry behind (CORE-062 AC5, CORE-063 AC3), and lines 3 and 4 say the produce action passes that error on: it fails, and it never completes, so it cannot complete with no token (refProduce_undeclared). Every runtime does so: Rust returns the error with ?, Java throws IllegalArgumentException from the output call and the TypeScript output call throws inside the async action. A transition with no output specification names no place, so the produce action of any place fails on it. Whether the one-token emission is a deposit the output specification offers is the firing's question (IO-015, CORE-050 line 3): on Place p it is (core054_fires), on And(Place p, Place q) it is not and validation fails the firing (EXEC-021).

Line 1 says that the action ends on a declared place, so an action that never ends there violates it (CORE_054_mutant_noComplete_killed: lines 2 to 4 hold of it). Line 2 says what every way of ending on a declared place is, so an action that fails there violates it (CORE_054_forbids_fails), and so do one that writes two tokens (CORE_054_forbids_twoTokens) and one that writes the token it consumed instead of the value (CORE_054_forbids_echo). 'Exactly one output token in that place and none in any other' is stronger than AC1's 'the place receives a token with the value': an action that writes the value to every output place meets the AC1 reading and violates line 2 (CORE_054_mutant_ac1_killed). Line 3 says that the action ends on an undeclared place (CORE_054_mutant_noEndUndeclared_killed: an action that never ends there meets lines 1, 2 and 4). Line 4 says that every way it ends there is a failure (CORE_054_mutant_swallowSometimes_killed: an action that fails on some runs and completes with no token on others meets lines 1 to 3), and an action that always swallows the error and completes with no token violates it (CORE_054_forbids_swallow).

The produce action writes through the context: every emission it completes with is a buffer built by successful output calls (refProduce_throughCtx), so CORE-062's and CORE-063's context lines and ctx_deposits_outputs apply to it.

AC1 (the specified place receives a token with the fixed value) is lines 1 and 2 at the action, and at the firing through CORE-050: on a transition whose output specification is Place p, an enabled firing ends with the completion of produce p v (core054_fires), and every firing that ends with it deposits exactly one token of value v in p and nothing elsewhere (core054_emits). Lines 3 and 4 have no acceptance criterion of CORE-054; they are CORE-062 AC5 and CORE-063 AC3 at the produce action.

The test derivation (produce action with value "hello" to place P; P receives "hello") is CORE_054_nonvacuous: on a transition consuming one token from place 0 and producing to Place 1, the reference action firing under refProduce for the value "hello" deposits one token carrying "hello" in place 1, and on place 2, which the transition does not name, the reference action fails.

requirements.title: Context Input Access
requirements.statement:
fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] value C ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),
      ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,
        δ.inputs p ≠ [] → C.inputs t δ p = some (List.map value (δ.inputs p))) ∧
    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (p : N) (x : T),
        p ∈ inPlaces t → δ.inputs p = [x] → C.input t δ p = some (value x)) ∧
      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (p : N) (x : T),
          p ∈ inPlaces t → δ.inputs p = [x] → C.inputToken t δ p = some x) ∧
        ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),
          ∀ p ∉ inPlaces t,
            δ.inputs p = [] →
              C.inputs t δ p = none ∧ C.input t δ p = none ∧ C.inputToken t δ p = none
requirements.scope: the transition context of every implementation; line 3 and the inputToken part of line 4 only where the context gives access to tokens: Java and TypeScript
reading: For every value projection value and every context C, every transition t, every delivery δ (the tokens the firing consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read) and every place p:
if p is an input place of t and δ delivered at least one token from p, inputs on t, δ and p returns the values of the tokens δ delivered from p, in the order δ delivered them;
if p is an input place of t and δ delivered exactly one token x from p, input on t, δ and p returns the value of x;
if p is an input place of t and δ delivered exactly one token x from p, inputToken on t, δ and p returns x itself;
if p is not an input place of t and δ delivered no token from p, inputs, input and inputToken on t, δ and p each report an error.
quotes: *When* an action calls `inputs(place)` on an input place of its transition, the call *shall* return the values of the tokens the firing consumed from that place, in the order the firing consumed them ([EXEC-010]).
*When* an action calls `input(place)` on an input place from which the firing consumed exactly one token, the call *shall* return the value of that token.

*Where* the transition context gives access to tokens (Java, TypeScript), *when* an action calls `inputToken(place)` on an input place from which the firing consumed exactly one token, the call *shall* return that token, with its creation timestamp.

*If* an action calls `inputs(place)`, `input(place)` or `inputToken(place)` (where it exists) on a place that does not resolve to an input place of its transition ([MOD-031]), *then* the call *shall* report an error ([CORE-063]).
What `input(place)` and `inputToken(place)` return when the firing consumed more than one token from the place is not specified; an action reads a batch with `inputs(place)`.
assumes: The model is the pair (value, C). C is a transition context (Ctx, Spec/GlossaryContext.lean): its accessors inputs, input and inputToken take the transition, the delivery and a place, and return none when the call reports an error. A delivery (Delivered, Spec/GlossaryQueue.lean) is what the firing hands its action: the tokens it consumed from each input place, in the order consumed, and the tokens its read arcs read. Tokens are the queue model's token identities T, each carrying its value and its creation timestamp; value : T → V reads a token's value, so input (a value) and inputToken (the token, with its timestamp) are told apart. The witness is the reference context refCtx.

The block is a function of the delivery, not of the marking: line 1 keeps the order in which the firing delivered the tokens, and which tokens the firing consumes, and in which order, is not CORE-060's. For an input that is not a correlated input of a ν-net match specification it is EXEC-010's: the oldest tokens of the place, in queue order. core060_inputs_oldest derives that for any context that satisfies CORE-060 and any queue firing relation that satisfies EXEC-010, and core060_input_oldest gives the value of the oldest token for input on an arc that consumes one token. A correlated input (NU-020) takes the matched tokens of the chosen name, oldest first among them, and can pass over an older token of another name, so for it the delivered tokens are not the oldest of the place. The block holds for whatever delivery that firing makes; the two joint theorems do not reach it, because the queue firing relation of EXEC-010 carries no match specification (ruling D16).

Lines 1 and 4 range over the deliveries a firing makes at the place: line 1 takes an input place from which the delivery holds at least one token, line 4 a place that is not an input place and from which the delivery holds none. Every firing meets both premises: each input arc requires and consumes at least one token (IO-002, IO-004 AC1), and a firing consumes through its input arcs only. A delivery that breaks them is made by no firing, and the block makes no claim on it.

The premises accept the Rust and Python check, which is key presence in the map of delivered tokens, not membership in the input places: Rust's input and inputs answer from self.inputs.get(place_name) (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:278-302), the backends insert a key only when they push a token (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/bitmap_backend.rs:785-808), and Python copies those keys (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs:329-365). That context, core060_keyedCtx, satisfies CORE-060 (CORE_060_allows_keyed), and on every delivery that holds tokens from exactly the input places it answers as refCtx at every place (core060_keyed_agrees).

Line 1 compares lists: the values in the order delivered, with their repetitions. A context that returns them in reverse order meets the reading 'inputs returns all consumed values' as a multiset and violates line 1 (CORE_060_mutant_anyOrder_killed).

Lines 2 and 3 carry the premise that exactly one token was delivered from the place (ruling D50 (a), clash core-c#1). With more than one, the runtimes differ: input reports an error in Rust (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:278-287), TypeScript (typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:114-123) and Python (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs:207-217), and Java returns the value of the oldest token (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:164-168, against its own javadoc at :162, a recorded defect, RD-09 in spec/runtime-defects.md); inputToken returns the oldest token in Java (:190-194) and TypeScript (typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:133-138). The block leaves the case open: CORE_060_batch_undecided shows two contexts that both satisfy it and differ there, on input and on inputToken. A firing never consumes zero tokens from an input place (IO-002 and IO-004 AC1: every input arc requires at least one token), so 'other than one' is 'more than one' at a firing. No line claims anything on an input place with an empty delivery, which no firing makes: lines 2 and 3 need exactly one token, line 1 at least one.

A context whose input always reports an error, so that an action must use inputs, meets the reading 'input returns a consumed value when it returns one' and violates line 2 (CORE_060_mutant_soundOnly_killed). A context whose inputToken re-mints the token with the same value and another timestamp meets the reading 'inputToken returns a token with the consumed value' and violates line 3 (CORE_060_mutant_valueOnly_killed): the metadata the token carries is the consumed token's own.

A context is a function of the transition, the delivery and the place, so a context that keeps state across firings is modelled as a different context at each firing. Java's precompiled executor reuses one context per transition and clears its token store before each firing (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:2320-2324); a context that kept the tokens of the previous firing ahead of its own violates lines 1 to 3 (CORE_060_forbids_staleStore).

Line 3, and the inputToken part of line 4, are scoped to the implementations whose context gives access to tokens (ruling D50 (a), clash core-c#2): Java's and TypeScript's inputToken. The Rust and Python contexts expose values only (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:278-327, python/libpetri/_libpetri.pyi), so line 3 has no accessor there; Rust's take_inputs empties the context and serves the executor, not an action. The Lean line is the same under every scope.

Line 4 reads 'results in an error' as 'the call reports an error' (none): Rust returns an error, Java and TypeScript throw, Python raises. A place that is not an input place includes a read place (no place is both, ruling D15), an output place and a place of no arc of the transition. A context that answers such a place with the empty list meets the reading 'an undeclared place has no consumed values' and violates line 4 (CORE_060_mutant_emptyList_killed). So does one that keeps the consumed and the read tokens in one store and serves a read place through inputs (CORE_060_forbids_sharedStore), or through an inputToken that lost its input-place guard (CORE_060_forbids_unguardedToken): TypeScript's context and Java's precompiled executor keep one such store (typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:114-160, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:2341-2347), so each accessor depends on its own guard. The read accessor is CORE-061's, the output accessor CORE-062's, and the three error lines together are CORE-063's.

The error sentence names the place the call resolves to (MOD-031), and the block reads every place that way: after instancing or port binding, Java and TypeScript map a declared place the action names to the composed place first (MOD-031, W8). A type mismatch between the place and the value (Rust's downcast error) is API shape and not modelled: V is one type of values. Further accessors (Java's inputTokens, Rust's input_raw and input_tokens_raw) are not part of the block.
AC1 (input(place) returns the single consumed value) is line 2, under the exactly-one premise of ruling D50 (a).
AC2 (inputs(place) returns all consumed values, for multi-token cardinality) is line 1.
AC3 (inputToken(place) returns the token with metadata, including its timestamp) is line 3, scoped to Java and TypeScript.
AC4 (accessing an undeclared input place results in an error) is line 4.

The test derivation (fire a transition consuming 3 tokens, verify inputs() returns 3 values) is CORE_060_nonvacuous: the reference firing of a transition whose input arc takes exactly 3 tokens delivers the 3 oldest, and the reference context returns their 3 values, in queue order.

requirements.title: Context Read Access
requirements.statement:
fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] value C ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (p : N) (x : T),
      ReadArc t p →
        δ.inputs p = [] → (δ.reads p).head? = some x → C.read t δ p = some (value x)) ∧
    ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (p : N),
      ¬ReadArc t p → δ.reads p = [] → C.read t δ p = none
requirements.scope: the transition context of every implementation
reading: For every value projection value and every context C, every transition t, every delivery δ (the tokens the firing consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read) and every place p:
if p is a read place of t, δ consumed no token from p and the first token δ read at p is x, read on t, δ and p returns the value of x;
if p is not a read place of t and δ read no token at p, read on t, δ and p reports an error, whether or not p is an input place of t.
quotes: *When* an action calls `read(place)` on a read place of its transition, the call *shall* return the value of the token the read arc read from that place, the oldest token the place holds ([EXEC-012]).
The call consumes nothing: by [EXEC-012] the firing leaves the read token in the place, unless the transition also has a reset arc there, which drains the place ([EXEC-013]).

*If* an action calls `read(place)` on a place that does not resolve to a read place of its transition ([MOD-031]), *then* the call *shall* report an error, also when the place is an input place of the transition.
assumes: The model is the pair (value, C). C is a transition context (Ctx, Spec/GlossaryContext.lean): its accessor read takes the transition, the delivery and a place, and returns none when the call reports an error. A delivery (Delivered, Spec/GlossaryQueue.lean) is what the firing hands its action: the tokens it consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read, per place. Tokens are the queue model's token identities T; value : T → V reads a token's value. The witness is the reference context refCtx.

The block is a function of the delivery, not of the marking. Which token a read arc reads is not CORE-061's but EXEC-012's: the head of the read place, after input consumption and before reset draining. core061_read_head derives, for any context that satisfies CORE-061, any pair (Build, Q) that satisfies EXEC-012 and whose Q satisfies EXEC-010, that on a firing of a transition with no input arc and read arc on one place read returns the value of the oldest token of the read place, and that the firing leaves the queue of a read place that is not a reset place as it was, followed by the tokens it deposits there (identity and order). That is the clause 'the oldest token the place holds' of the first quoted sentence. The second quoted sentence states EXEC-012 line 2 as a consequence for the action and is not a line of this block: it is the 'without consuming it' of AC1 and the 'token still in place' of the test derivation, and its exception names EXEC-013, under which a reset arc drains the place. The context itself is a function and consumes nothing.

The premises 'δ consumed no token from p' (line 1) and 'δ read no token at p' (line 2) are a property of the firing, not of the context: a firing delivers read tokens only at the read places of its transition and consumed tokens only at its input places (core061_ByArcs). The reference queue firing has it (core061_refQFire_byArcs, from qDelivered_reads_off and qDelivered_inputs_off), and every runtime builds its delivery that way. EXEC-010's line 3 (no consumed token from a place that is not an input place) and EXEC-012's line 7 (no read token from a place that is not a read place) state it for every executor, so every queue firing relation that meets both delivers by arcs (core061_byArcs_of). Under them the third quoted sentence holds at every firing (core061_read_off, from EXEC-012 alone), and the first does through core061_read_head.

Line 1 takes the first token read at the read place, from a delivery that holds no consumed token there. At a firing of a transition that builds both premises are what the firing gives: every token a firing delivers at a read place is the head of its queue (EXEC-012 line 1), so the first is the only value there is, and a transition with two read arcs on one place gets the head twice; and no read place is an input place (ruling D15), so under core061_ByArcs the firing consumed no token from it. On a delivery no firing makes, with two different read tokens at one place, line 1 still asks for the first: that is a deliberate choice, and every runtime takes the first entry (Rust tokens[0], rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:337-347; Java's and TypeScript's TokenInput, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TokenInput.java:70-76). A context that answers the last read token agrees with refCtx at every firing and is rejected only on such a delivery. The premise that the delivery holds a read token at the read place holds at every firing, because a transition fires only while its read places are marked (CORE-032). On a read place from which the delivery holds no token, which no firing makes, the block makes no claim; refCtx and every runtime report an error there (Rust 'No tokens for read place', Python 'read place ... is empty', Java and TypeScript TokenInput.get).

Java and TypeScript keep the consumed and the read tokens in one store (rawInput), filled with the consumed tokens first and the read tokens after them (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java:1671-1699, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:2323-2345, typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts:1055-1075, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:1080-1116), and read checks its guard requireRead and then answers the first entry of that store at the place (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:235-239, typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:156-160). That context, core061_guardedSharedCtx, satisfies CORE-061 (CORE_061_allows_guardedShared), because line 1 takes a delivery with no consumed token at the read place, and at every firing of a transition that builds, under core061_ByArcs, it answers read as refCtx at every place (core061_guarded_agrees). Without the premise, line 1 would reject it on a delivery no firing makes (core061_strict_rejects_guarded). The same store served through a read without its guard is forbidden (CORE_061_forbids_sharedStore).
A context whose read always reports an error meets the reading 'read returns a read value when it returns one' and violates line 1 (CORE_061_mutant_soundOnly_killed).

Line 2 reads 'results in an error' as 'the call reports an error' (none): Rust returns an error, Java and TypeScript throw, Python raises. 'An undeclared read place' is any place that is not a read place of the transition: an input place, an output place, or a place of no arc of the transition. A context with one allowed set for inputs and reads, which answers read on an input place with the value of a consumed token, meets the reading 'read reports an error on a place the transition does not declare at all' and violates line 2 (CORE_061_mutant_anyDeclared_killed). No place is both an input place and a read place of a transition that builds (ruling D15, EXEC-012), so the two lines never meet on one place at a firing.

Line 2 accepts the Rust and Python check, which is key presence in the map of read tokens, not membership in the read places: Rust's read answers from self.reads.get(place_name) (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:337-347), the backends insert a key only when they push a read token (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/bitmap_backend.rs:823-832, rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:866-877), and Python copies those keys (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs:226-236, :367-381). That context, core061_keyedCtx, satisfies CORE-061 (CORE_061_allows_keyed), and on every delivery that holds read tokens at exactly the read places it answers read as refCtx at every place (core061_keyed_agrees). It is correct only under core061_ByArcs, which is why that property is named above.

The third quoted sentence is word for word the second quoted sentence of CORE-063, and line 2 is the same formula as CORE-063's line 2. CORE-061 is the requirement that states the rule, as its AC2; CORE-063 depends on CORE-061 and collects the error lines of CORE-060 to CORE-062, so the citation runs from CORE-063 to CORE-061 and not back.

The error sentence names the place the call resolves to (MOD-031), and the block reads every place that way: after instancing or port binding, Java and TypeScript map a declared place the action names to the composed place first (MOD-031, W8), and Python falls back through its local name map. A type mismatch between the place and the value (Rust's downcast error) is API shape and not modelled: V is one type of values. Further accessors (reads(place) in Java, TypeScript, Rust and Python, Rust's read_tokens_raw) are not part of the block.
AC1 (read(place) returns the read value without consuming it) is line 1, with 'without consuming it' from EXEC-012 line 2 through core061_read_head.
AC2 (accessing an undeclared read place results in an error) is line 2, and at a firing core061_read_off.

The test derivation (fire a transition with a read arc, verify read() returns the value, verify the token is still in place) is CORE_061_nonvacuous: a reference firing of a transition with an input arc on place 0 and a read arc on place 1, which holds 7 then 8, delivers the token of value 7 at place 1, the reference context returns 7, the firing leaves 7 and 8 in place 1, and read on the input place 0 and on the output place 2 reports an error. CORE_061_joint_example derives the same answers through core061_read_head and core061_read_off from EXEC-012's reference pair.

requirements.title: Context Output Access
requirements.statement:
fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] _value C ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (e : List (N × V)) (p : N) (vs : List V),
      OutputArc t p → C.output t e p vs = some (e ++ List.map (fun v ↦ (p, v)) vs)) ∧
    ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (e : List (N × V)) (p : N) (vs : List V),
      ¬OutputArc t p → C.output t e p vs = none
requirements.scope: the transition context of every implementation, except output calls made after the firing has ended with the timeout outcome
reading: For every value projection value, every context C, every transition t, every buffer e (the places and values the action declared before the call, in order), every place p and every list of values vs:
if p is an output place of t, the output call on t, e, p and vs succeeds and returns e followed by one entry (p, v) for each v in vs, in the order of vs;
if p is not an output place of t, the output call on t, e, p and vs reports an error, whatever vs is, the empty list included.
quotes: *When* an action calls `output(place, value)` on an output place of its transition, the call *shall* declare one token carrying `value` on that place, after every token the action declared before.

*When* an action calls the bulk form with a sequence of values on an output place of its transition, the call *shall* declare one token per value on that place, in the order of the sequence, after every token the action declared before.
*When* an action calls the bulk form with no values on an output place of its transition, the call *shall* declare no token and return successfully.

*If* an action calls `output(place, value)` or the bulk form on a place that does not resolve to an output place of its transition ([MOD-031]), *then* the call *shall* report an error and declare no token, also when it passes no values ([CORE-063]).
These four sentences do not govern an output call made after the firing has ended with the timeout outcome ([IO-013]); such a call declares no token that the firing deposits.
assumes: The model is the pair (value, C), as in CORE-060, so that the context blocks CORE-060 to CORE-063 share one signature; the value projection value plays no part in the output lines. C is a transition context (Ctx, Spec/GlossaryContext.lean). Its output accessor takes the transition, the buffer of places and values the action has declared so far in the firing, a place and the values of one call, and returns none when the call reports an error and some of the new buffer otherwise. The single form output(place, value) is the call with the one value [value]; every language shape of the bulk form (Java varargs and Iterable, TypeScript rest parameters, Rust and Python output_many) is the call with the values in iteration order. A value list is finite and fully known: a value source that fails part way (a Python iterable that raises, a Rust iterator that panics) is outside the block. The witness is the reference context refCtx.

Java API shape: the single form is the overload a call resolves to. Java declares output(Place<T>, T), the varargs output(Place<T>, T...) and output(Place<T>, Iterable<? extends T>) (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:281 and :350). On a place whose token type is a supertype of a collection type, such as Place<Object>, a call output(place, value) whose value has a static type that is an Iterable resolves to the Iterable overload (JLS 15.12.2: the first phase, without varargs, already matches it with T = Object), so it declares one token per element, not one token carrying the collection. The block reads such a call as the bulk call it resolves to, with the elements in iteration order; a caller that wants one token holding the collection casts the value to the place's type. The built-in transform and fork pass a value of static type Object and so take the single form (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionAction.java:104-107). This is the shape of the Java API (kind N), not a runtime defect, and no line is weakened for it.

An output place is a place the transition's output spec names (OutputArc: the glossary's Output arc, IO-017's allPlaces), so the targets of ForwardInput nodes and the places of a Timeout child are output places. Every runtime checks the place against that set: Rust require_output (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:462-473), Java requireOutput (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:323-324 and :351-352), TypeScript requireOutput (typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:196-198 and :227-233), Python require_output (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs:247-260). The place an action names is the place the call resolves to, as the fourth quoted sentence says (MOD-031): after instancing or port binding, Java and TypeScript map a declared place to the composed place first (MOD-031, W8).

Declaring a token is appending it to the firing's emission buffer. When the buffer enters the marking (at completion, or earlier through a flush) is EXEC-020's and ruling D17's, and that a firing that ends with the completion of its action deposits exactly that emission is CORE-050's. core062_deposits_outputs joins the two: for an action that writes through a context satisfying CORE-062 (ThroughCtx), every place a reference action firing deposits in is an output place of the transition.

The block does not govern an output call made after the firing has ended with the timeout outcome (IO-013), as the fifth quoted sentence says; the markdown lists IO-013 and IO-017 (the output places) among the dependencies. After it, Java and TypeScript detach the action's collector, and an output call on an output place still returns normally but its token is counted and dropped (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:362-372, typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:236-250); line 1 does not describe those calls, and IO-013 says that no output of such an action is deposited.

Line 1 compares lists: the new entries come after the old buffer, one per value with its repetitions, in the order of the values. A context that writes the values of one call in reverse order meets the reading 'one token per value, as a multiset' and violates line 1 (CORE_062_mutant_bulkAnyOrder_killed). A context that puts the new entries ahead of the earlier ones meets the reading 'the buffer holds the earlier and the new tokens' and violates line 1 (CORE_062_mutant_bufferAnyOrder_killed). A context that collapses repeated values meets the reading 'every value gets a token' and violates line 1 (CORE_062_mutant_eachValue_killed).

Line 2 reads 'results in an error' as 'the call reports an error and declares nothing' (ruling D63 (a)): Rust returns an error, Java and TypeScript throw, Python raises. Whether the firing then fails depends on whether the action lets the error out (EXEC-030), which is not this block's. A context that answers an undeclared place by silently producing nothing meets the reading 'producing to an undeclared place yields no token' and violates line 2 (CORE_062_mutant_silentDrop_killed). A context with one allowed set for the input and the output places is forbidden (CORE_062_forbids_arcPlaces).

A call that reports an error returns none and so leaves the buffer as it was: the type of the output accessor has no room for a failed call that changed the buffer, so the clause 'declare no token' of the fourth sentence and the 'no partial output' of AC3 are carried by the type, not by a line, and no wrong context of this type can append a prefix and then report an error. Their observable content is core062_error_declares_nothing: a buffer built by successful calls, so also by an action that catches the error and goes on, holds no entry on a place that is not an output place. A bulk call names one place, so a check made per value fails on the first value before anything is appended, and the only case in which checking once up front (AC3) and checking per value differ is the call with no values on an undeclared place. Every runtime checks before it iterates (the four locations above), so that call is an error: line 2 says so for the empty list too. A context that checks per value meets the reading 'every token produced to an undeclared place is an error' and violates line 2 (CORE_062_mutant_perValue_killed); core062_empty_undeclared shows that this call is the one difference between the bulk form and the single form repeated.

The stamp of a declared token is not this block's: V holds values, and the buffer carries no creation timestamp. That an output token carries the current reading of the epoch clock is CORE-035 AC2 (with TIME-015 and CORE-011, whose executor line is the W11 block), and both runtime shapes meet it: Rust's output_many reads the clock once for the whole call (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:448), Java and TypeScript read it for each value as it is added; either way the stamps of one call are current readings and do not decrease. No block relies on one stamp per value. A value source that fails part way leaves open whether the tokens it yielded before failing stay in the buffer: AC3's 'no partial output' is about the undeclared-place error only, and the markdown is silent on such a source. Producing a ready-made token (Java's output(Place, Token), TypeScript's outputToken) is not in the spec and not part of the block. The method names and signatures per language are API shape (kind N), recorded in AC2 and not in the formula.
AC1 (output(place, value) declares a single token on the given output place) is line 1 with one value: core062_single.

AC2 (a bulk form produces one token per value in iteration order; the language shapes) is line 1: core062_bulk_repeated shows that on an output place the bulk call is the single call repeated once per value, in order. The language shapes are API shape (kind N), recorded in the AC and not in the formula.

AC3 (the bulk form validates the place exactly once and reports an error before appending any token if the place is not declared) is line 2 for every list of values, with the reading of none above: no partial output (core062_error_declares_nothing), and an error also for the empty call. 'Exactly once' is the cost of the check (quality), not encoded beyond that.

AC4 (an empty bulk call is a no-op and returns successfully) is line 1 with the empty list, on a declared output place: core062_empty_declared. On an undeclared place the empty call is an error (line 2, AC3); the spec edit CORE-062-ac4 says so in the AC.
AC5 (producing to an undeclared output place results in an error) is line 2.

The test derivation is CORE_062_nonvacuous: an action that calls output(place, value) through the reference context builds the buffer [(2, 5)], and the reference action firing deposits the token in place 2; the bulk call with the three values 5, 6 and 7 appends three entries in that order, and on a transition whose only output branch names place 2 three times the reference firing deposits the three tokens in place 2 in that order; the bulk call on a foreign place reports an error, so nothing is appended.

requirements.title: Context Structure Enforcement
requirements.statement:
fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] _value C ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),
      ∀ p ∉ inPlaces t,
        δ.inputs p = [] →
          C.inputs t δ p = none ∧ C.input t δ p = none ∧ C.inputToken t δ p = none) ∧
    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (p : N),
        ¬ReadArc t p → δ.reads p = [] → C.read t δ p = none) ∧
      ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (e : List (N × V)) (p : N) (vs : List V),
        ¬OutputArc t p → C.output t e p vs = none
requirements.scope: the transition context of every implementation; the inputToken part of line 1 only where the context gives access to tokens: Java and TypeScript
reading: For every value projection value and every context C, every transition t, every delivery δ (the tokens the firing consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read), every output buffer e, every place p and every list of values vs:
if p is not an input place of t and δ delivered no token from p, inputs, input and inputToken on t, δ and p each report an error;
if p is not a read place of t and δ delivered no read token from p, read on t, δ and p reports an error;
if p is not an output place of t, the output call on t, e, p and vs reports an error (it returns no buffer).
quotes: *If* an action calls an input accessor (`inputs(place)`, `input(place)` or, where it exists, `inputToken(place)`) on a place that does not resolve to an input place of its transition ([MOD-031]), *then* the call *shall* report an error.

*If* an action calls `read(place)` on a place that does not resolve to a read place of its transition ([MOD-031]), *then* the call *shall* report an error, also when the place is an input place of the transition.

*If* an action calls `output(place, ...)`, in its single or its bulk form, on a place that does not resolve to an output place of its transition ([MOD-031]), *then* the call *shall* report an error and declare no token, also when it passes no values.
Every executor hands an action consumed tokens only from the input places of its transition ([EXEC-010]) and read tokens only from its read places ([EXEC-012]).

The plural accessors some languages add, such as `reads(place)` and Java's `inputTokens(place)`, are not named by these rules; each implementation guards them with the check of the singular accessor of the same kind.
These rules govern the calls an action makes through its transition context; a token that reaches the executor without passing through the context is the subject of [CORE-072] AC3.
assumes: The model is the pair (value, C), the model of CORE-060 to CORE-062. C is a transition context (Ctx, Spec/GlossaryContext.lean): inputs, input, inputToken and read take the transition, the delivery and a place and return none when the call reports an error; output takes the transition, the buffer written so far, a place and the values of one call and returns none when the call reports an error, some of the new buffer otherwise. The value projection value : T → V is not used by the three lines; it keeps the block on the same model as CORE-060. The witness is the reference context refCtx.

'Declared in the transition's structure' is read per accessor: an input accessor needs an input arc (inPlaces), read needs a read arc (ReadArc), an output call needs a place the output specification names (OutputArc, glossary: Output arc; CORE-035, IO-017). It is not 'some arc of the transition names the place': a context that guards every accessor by that union answers inputs on an output place with the empty list and violates line 1 (CORE_063_mutant_anyArc_killed), and one that accepts an output on any arc place of the transition (a net-membership check) violates line 3 (CORE_063_forbids_anyArcOutput). Each conjunct of line 1 is load-bearing on its own: a context that keeps the consumed and the read tokens in one store (TypeScript's rawInput, Java's precompiled executor) and drops only the guard of input, or only that of inputToken, answers the read token of a read place and violates line 1 (CORE_063_forbids_unguardedInput, CORE_063_forbids_unguardedToken).

Lines 1 and 2 range over the deliveries a firing makes at the place: line 1 takes a place from which the delivery holds no consumed token, line 2 a place from which it holds no read token. Every reference firing meets both premises (qDelivered_inputs_off, qDelivered_reads_off), and every runtime builds its delivery that way, as the fourth quoted sentence records: EXEC-010's line 3 and EXEC-012's line 7 require it of every executor, which CORE-061 records as core061_ByArcs (core061_byArcs_of). core063_on_firing gives the three lines on the delivery of any reference firing with no premise left, which is the reading of the three EARS sentences. On a delivery that breaks the premises, which no runtime makes, the block makes no claim. The premises accept the Rust and Python check, which is key presence in the maps of delivered tokens: Rust's input accessors answer from self.inputs.get(place_name) and read from self.reads.get(place_name) (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:278-375), the backends insert a key only when they push a token (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/bitmap_backend.rs:785-830), and Python copies those keys (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs:207-245). That context, core063_keyedCtx, satisfies CORE-063 (CORE_063_allows_keyed). Line 3 has no delivery premise: every runtime checks the output call against the output places of the transition (Rust require_output over allowed_outputs, context.rs:462-473; Java requireOutput over transition.outputPlaces(), TransitionContext.java:438-445; TypeScript requireOutput, typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:227-233; Python require_output, rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs:307).

Line 1 is CORE-060 line 4, word for word in Lean (core063_line1_of_core060), and the inputToken part of it is scoped as CORE-060's is: Java and TypeScript have inputToken, the Rust and Python contexts expose values only. Line 2 is CORE-061 line 2 (core063_line2_iff_core061) and line 3 is CORE-062 line 2 (core063_line3_iff_core062), both by Iff.rfl, so a change to one formula breaks the build here; CORE_063_of_lines records that the block is the conjunction of the three error lines, and CORE_063_of_060_061_062 that a context that meets CORE-060, CORE-061 and CORE-062 meets CORE-063, which is the Depends on line. The EARS sentences of lines 2 and 3 restate CORE-061's and CORE-062's error sentences in other words on purpose: CORE-063 is the requirement that collects the three error rules, and the Iff.rfl theorems keep the restatement from drifting in Lean.

The fifth quoted sentence leaves the plural accessors out: Ctx has no field for them, as in CORE-061. Every implementation guards each with the check of the singular accessor of the same kind: Java reads and inputTokens call requireRead and requireInput (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:203-206, :248-251), TypeScript reads calls requireRead (typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:163-166), Rust reads, read_tokens_raw and input_tokens_raw look the place up in the same map as read and inputs (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:319-375), and Python reads uses the lookup of read (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs:239-243). That second half of the sentence is a description of the code, not a line of the block.

Line 2 says 'also on an input place': no place is both an input and a read place of one transition (ruling D15, NoInputRead), so an input place is a place that is not a read place. A context that keeps the consumed and the read tokens in one store and guards read by 'an input or a read place' meets the reading 'read reports an error on a place that is neither an input nor a read place' and violates line 2 (CORE_063_mutant_sharedSet_killed). TypeScript's context keeps one such store (read answers from rawInput.value, typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:156-160), so read depends on its own guard requireRead: without it, read answers the consumed token of an input place (CORE_063_forbids_unguardedRead).

'Results in an error' is read as 'the call reports an error' (none): Rust returns an Err, Java throws IllegalArgumentException, TypeScript throws, Python raises. Whether the firing then fails is not CORE-063's: it fails only if the action lets the error out (EXEC-030), and a produce action passes it on (CORE-054 lines 3 and 4). An output call that silently drops the values meets the reading 'producing to an undeclared output declares no token' and violates line 3 (CORE_063_mutant_silentDrop_killed). Line 3 holds for every list of values, the empty one included, as the third quoted sentence says ('also when it passes no values'): every runtime checks the place before it iterates (CORE-062 AC3), so an empty bulk call on an undeclared place is an error too, and the call leaves no partial output.

Ruling D63 (a): the block is a rule on the calls an action makes through its context, and the last quoted sentence says so. Java and TypeScript expose the context's raw output collector (rawOutput(), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:561, typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:340), documented internal and used by the executors; a token written there bypasses the check, and CORE-072 AC3 retains it as a token on an unknown place. That seam is not witnessed by any model of the joint consistency theorem, because CORE-035 line 1 and CONC-026 line 2 say that no firing deposits outside its output places. The firing-level statement is derived: core063_deposits_outputs shows that an action that writes through a context that satisfies CORE-063, whose successful output calls append only entries at the named place (core063_AppendsAt, CORE-062 line 1 gives it), deposits in a reference action firing only in output places of its transition.

The error sentences name the place the call resolves to (MOD-031), and the block reads every place that way: after instancing or port binding, Java and TypeScript map a declared place the action names to the composed place first, and Python falls back through its local name map (MOD-031, W8). A type mismatch between the place and the value is API shape and not modelled: V is one type of values. Calls made after a timeout severed the firing's output (IO-013) are out of scope, as for CORE-062.
AC1 (accessing an undeclared input gives an error) is line 1.
AC2 (accessing an undeclared read gives an error) is line 2.
AC3 (producing to an undeclared output gives an error) is line 3.

The test derivation (create a context with restricted place sets, attempt out-of-bounds access, verify errors) is CORE_063_nonvacuous: on the reference firing of a transition with input place 0, read place 1 and output place 2, the reference context answers each accessor on its own place and reports an error for inputs, input and inputToken on the read and the output place, for read on the input and the output place, and for output on the input place and, with no values, on the read place.

requirements.title: Marking State
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} Ops ↦
  (∀ (P : List N),
      ∃ s, (∀ p ∈ P, Ops.ok s p) ∧ ∀ (q : N), Ops.view s q = [] ∧ Ops.count s q = 0) ∧
    (∀ (p : N), Ops.view Ops.empty p = [] ∧ Ops.count Ops.empty p = 0) ∧
      (∀ (s : Ops.σ) (p : N) (x : T),
          Ops.ok s p →
            Ops.view (Ops.add s p x) p = Ops.view s p ++ [x] ∧
              Ops.count (Ops.add s p x) p = Ops.count s p + 1 ∧
                ∀ (q : N),
                  Ops.ok s q →
                    Ops.ok (Ops.add s p x) q ∧
                      (q ≠ p →
                        Ops.view (Ops.add s p x) q = Ops.view s q ∧
                          Ops.count (Ops.add s p x) q = Ops.count s q)) ∧
        (∀ (s : Ops.σ) (p : N),
            Ops.ok s p →
              Marked (Ops.count s) p →
                (Ops.removeFirst s p).1 = (Ops.view s p).head? ∧
                  Ops.view (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 p = (Ops.view s p).tail ∧
                    Ops.count (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 p = Ops.count s p - 1 ∧
                      ∀ (q : N),
                        Ops.ok s q →
                          Ops.ok (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q ∧
                            (q ≠ p →
                              Ops.view (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q = Ops.view s q ∧
                                Ops.count (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q = Ops.count s q)) ∧
          (∀ (s : Ops.σ) (p : N),
              Ops.ok s p →
                ¬Marked (Ops.count s) p →
                  (Ops.removeFirst s p).1 = none ∧
                    ∀ (q : N),
                      Ops.ok s q →
                        Ops.ok (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q ∧
                          Ops.view (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q = Ops.view s q ∧
                            Ops.count (Ops.removeFirst s p).2 q = Ops.count s q) ∧
            ∀ (s : Ops.σ) (p : N), Ops.ok s p → Ops.count s p = (Ops.view s p).length
reading: Let Ops be a store of markings: view s p is the queue place p holds in state s, oldest token first; ok s p says that s holds a queue for p; empty, add, removeFirst and count are the operations.
For every list of places P there is a state that holds every place of P, and in which every place holds the empty queue and has token count 0.
In the designated empty marking every place holds the empty queue and has token count 0.

For every state s holding p: add s p x holds at p the queue of s followed by x, and its count at p is one more; every place q that s holds is still held, and if q is not p it keeps its queue and its count.

For every state s holding p, with p marked: removeFirst s p returns the head of p's queue, leaves p holding the rest of its queue in order, and its count at p is one less; every place q that s holds is still held, and if q is not p it keeps its queue and its count.
For every state s holding p, with p not marked: removeFirst s p returns no token, and every place q that s holds is still held and keeps its queue and its count.
For every state s holding p, the token count of p is the length of p's queue.
quotes: A marking represents the current distribution of tokens across all places.
Internally, each place maps to a FIFO queue of tokens.
A marking *shall* hold a queue of tokens for each place of its net, oldest token first, and the token count of a place *shall* be the length of its queue.
