(1) no park step starts in a state whose event queue is not empty;
(2) no step of any label goes from a state that is not parked to a parked one when the event queue of its start state is not empty;
(3) for every place p and token x, a request step for (p, x) answered accepted ends in a state that is not parked;
(4) no step that ends the external-events step (endEvents) starts in a state whose event queue is not empty;
(5) no step goes from a state outside the enablement update phase into it when the event queue of its start state is not empty.
quotes: Injecting a token wakes the orchestrator from idle immediately.
The orchestrator does not need to wait for a timer or poll.

An injection is queued from the moment inject() accepts it ([ENV-003]) until it leaves the queue: the executor puts its token into the marking, or, once the executor is closed or stopped or the run has ended, discards it ([ENV-013], [ENV-015], [EXEC-042]).
An injection that inject() accepts after the external-events step of a cycle has last read the queue counts as accepted after that step ends, and is left to the next cycle.

*While* an accepted injection is queued, the executor *shall not* block in its wait ([EXEC-001] step 6, [CONC-010]), neither at the end of a cycle nor again after it has answered something during the wait, such as a marking snapshot.
*When* inject() accepts a token, the executor *shall* end any block of its wait at once, without waiting for a timer.

*While* an accepted injection is queued and the executor is in its wait with no terminal place marked, the executor *shall* be able to leave the wait at once, by waking up or by taking a queued injection from the queue, without waiting for a timer.
*While* an accepted injection is queued, the executor *shall not* end the external-events step of a cycle and *shall not* start the enablement update of a cycle ([EXEC-001] steps 2 and 3).

Read with the definition of queued above, this means that a token accepted while the executor waits has left the queue before the enablement update of the cycle the wake-up starts, and is in the marking by then unless the run has closed, stopped or ended first; the earlier sentences mean that no timer or polling is needed to find it.

The requirement on the external-events step covers every injection queued during that step, not only those queued when it begins ([EXEC-001] step 2), so the step has no limit on how many injections it takes.
The words immediately, promptly and at once mean that nothing in the executor waits between the acceptance and the injection; the latency itself is tested, not proven.

Under a host clock an implementation may leave the wait to the host ([TIME-015]); the wait these sentences speak of is then the host's, and [TIME-015] requires its readiness predicate to observe the queued injection.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The outside step request p x r is a call of inject(); r = accepted is the call accepting the token, which queues it with a ticket in XSt.eq (ENV-003). Step 2 of a cycle takes queued injections into the marking one at a time (inject k, at the tail of the place, FIFO by ticket) or, once closed or stopped, discards them (discard k, ENV-013), and ends with endEvents, after which the enablement update (phase update) runs. The wait is the loop phase await; park is the loop blocking in it and XSt.parked marks the block; wake is its end (a timer, a spurious wake-up or an arrival), after which the loop runs step 1 again; an injection may also be taken straight from the wait (inject k or discard k from phase await). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), checked rule by rule against the Rust executor.

Definition of queued: an injection is queued while its ticket is in XSt.eq. The reference takes a ticket out by inject k (into the marking), by discard k (closed or stopped, ENV-013), by terminateNow (ENV-015, the queue dropped at once) and by a finish step (the end of the run: quiescent, closed, or a marked terminal place, EXEC-042). The linearization sentence is how a run places a request: the request is an atomic outside step whose place in a run is the moment the runtime's step 2 can see the event. Java polls its external queue until it is empty and Rust drains its channel with try_recv until it is empty, so an event sent after the last read is a request after endEvents; TypeScript walks the prefix queued when step 2 begins, and an inject() made inside that step (from an event store append) is likewise a request after endEvents. Such an event goes to the next cycle, which lines 1 and 2 and the coverage clause Env005Covers make the loop reach without blocking.

AC1 (the orchestrator is idle, no ready transitions) is the precondition of the lines, not a criterion of its own, and the lines drop it: they bind every accepted injection, idle or not. The idle orchestrator is the loop in its wait, blocked (parked) or about to block. Its blocking is constrained by lines 1 and 2: it may block only with nothing queued, and the rest of the park guard (nothing Ready or Expired at the cycle reading, the timer bound) is CONC-010's.

Its offers are in ExecCoversW5.Env005Covers (ConsistencyExec.lean; the convention of GlossaryExec.lean: offers are coverage clauses, never block lines). The third EARS sentence (the executor shall be able to leave the wait at once) demands an answer and is quoted whole; it has no safety half among the lines, and its existence half is that clause. AC2 and the first description sentence's 'wakes the orchestrator' are line 3 and Env005Covers. Line 3 is the observable block marker: an accepted request clears it (ENV_005_forbids_deafRequest: an executor whose request leaves the marker set breaks it). Env005Covers is the behaviour: a live wait with an injection queued can always be left by the executor's own step, a wake or the injection or discard of a queued ticket, so leaving it never needs a timer; the reference meets it (env005_ref_covers). An inject() that queues the token but never signals the wait, so that only a completion, a drain, a close or a timer could end it, meets every line and fails that clause (env005_covers_unsignalled). Lines 1 and 2 keep the loop from blocking again while the token is queued (ENV_005_forbids_parkWithQueued: a polling executor that blocks with the token queued; ENV_005_forbids_reblock: a wait that answers a snapshot and blocks again). Together they are the second description sentence: no timer and no poll is needed to find the token. Line 3 holds for every accepted request, whether or not the loop was blocked; a request answered refused or error queues nothing and is ENV-006's and ENV-002's.

AC3 is lines 4 and 5 for 'within one cycle': step 2 does not end, and the enablement update does not start, while an injection is queued, so a token accepted while the loop waits has left the queue before the enablement update of the cycle the wake-up starts, and while the executor is open it is in the marking then and the transitions it enables are judged in that cycle (ENV_005_nonvacuous part 4). An executor that ends step 2 with an injection still queued, for instance one event per cycle, breaks line 4 (ENV_005_forbids_leavesQueued); one that skips step 2 and takes injections only from the wait reaches the update with the token queued and breaks line 5 (ENV_005_forbids_skipsEvents). EXEC-001 line 5 states the phase-entry form (the tickets queued when step 2 begins leave the queue before the next update); lines 4 and 5 read it on every queued ticket, as the markdown says, so no cap on the events per cycle is allowed. The consequence sentence ('Read with the definition of queued above') is lines 4 and 5 with the definition of queued; it is a reading, not a separate line.

Kind Q, outside the lines: 'immediately' and 'promptly' in AC2 and AC3, 'at once' in the EARS sentences, and 'within milliseconds' in the test derivation, are latencies; the model gives steps no duration, so they are tested, not proven, as the markdown says. The lines say that nothing in the executor waits between the acceptance and the injection: no block, no missing way out of the wait, no deferral to a later cycle.

Closed, stopped and ended runs: all five lines hold in every mode. Once the executor is closed or stopped a queued injection is discarded instead of put into the marking (ENV-013), an immediate termination drops the queue at once (ENV-015), and a finish clears it (EXEC-042 for a marked terminal place); these are the exits of the definition of queued and the 'unless' clause of the consequence sentence. Env005Covers asks nothing once a terminal place is marked: the loop then finishes (finish terminal). A request after a drain or a close is refused (ENV-006) and queues nothing. Java and TypeScript keep a pre-close event in their queue, unanswered, until the loop ends, and may block in the wait for the action in flight meanwhile; the sentence 'Once the executor is closed, an event that Java or TypeScript still holds in its queue counts as discarded from the first external-events step or wait after the close, though its inject() is answered only when the loop ends ([ENV-013], [ENV-004]).' is the reading: a Java or TypeScript run is the model run whose discard steps for those events come in the first step 2 or wait after the close, so the queue the lines read is empty before the wait blocks. The late answer is ENV-004's.

Host clock (TIME-015, clash env-a#9): under an injected host clock an implementation may stop raising its own wake-up (Java returns before releasing its wake-up semaphore when a host clock is installed) and leave the wait to the host, whose wait returns when the readiness predicate holds; Java's predicate reads the external queue. The model has one wait for both cases: under a host clock, the wait and its block marker stand for the host's wait, and line 3 and Env005Covers are met when the predicate reports the queued injection, which TIME-015's visibility duty requires. The host's own wait and the predicate are TIME-015's and outside the model; the markdown sentence is informative and puts the duty on TIME-015.

Depends on: CONC-010 (lines 1 and 3 are its park guard and arrival line restricted to the event queue), ENV-003 (acceptance and the queue), EXEC-001 (steps 2, 3 and 6), and, for the definition of queued and the consequence sentence, ENV-013, ENV-015 and EXEC-042; TIME-015 for the host-clock sentence. The test derivation (start an executor with an environment place, wait for quiescence, inject a token, check that it is processed) is ENV_005_nonvacuous: the loop blocks with nothing queued, a request is accepted and clears the block, a wake-up is offered, step 2 of the next cycle injects the token, and the transition it enables starts in that cycle.

requirements.title: inject() Rejection on Closed or Draining Executor
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    (while fun s ↦ Env006.Refusing s, never fun s s' ↦
        ∃ p x, R C s (XLbl.request p x Reply.accepted) s') ∧
      (on fun s s' ↦ Env006.Refusing s ∧ ∃ p x r, R C s (XLbl.request p x r) s', shall
          fun s s' ↦ s' = s) ∧
        (∀ (s0 : XSt N T) (k : ℕ) (tr : List (XStep N T)),
            XRun R C s0 tr → (at-most-once acceptsTicket k) tr) ∧
          ∀ (s0 : XSt N T) (k : ℕ),
            on-ideal-runs IdealRun R C s0, shall fun tr ↦
              (when acceptsTicket k, shall Env006.answersTicket k) tr
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C:
while the executor is draining, closed or stopped, or its run has finished, it accepts no injection request;
an injection request made in such a state leaves the executor state unchanged, whatever it answers;
on every run of R, at most one injection request is accepted with a given ticket k (the next identity of the state it is made in);

on every run of R under C that reaches its finish, every injection request accepted with ticket k is followed by a step that answers k: the injection of k, or a step that takes the event with ticket k out of the event queue (a discard on a close, an immediate termination, or a finish).
quotes: If the executor has been closed, is draining, or execution has completed, inject() returns an error or false rather than silently dropping the token.
*If* `inject()` is called while the executor is draining, closed or stopped ([ENV-011], [ENV-013], [ENV-015]), or after the run has finished, *then* it *shall* return an error or `false`.

*If* `inject()` is called while the executor is draining, closed or stopped, or after the run has finished, *then* the executor *shall* change nothing: the token *shall not* reach the marking, and no event *shall* be queued for injection.
Each accepted injection *shall* stay an event of its own until it is injected, discarded or dropped: the executor *shall not* merge two accepted injections into one.

*Where* `inject()` returns an admission signal ([ENV-004]), *when* a run that accepted an injection finishes, the executor *shall* have completed the signal of that injection, with the value [ENV-004] gives: by injecting the token, by discarding the event on a close ([ENV-013]), by dropping it on an immediate termination ([ENV-015]), or by dropping it at the finish of the run while it is still queued.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A call of inject() is the outside step request p x r: the caller asks to inject token x into place p and the executor answers r, which is accepted, refused (false) or error. An accepted request queues the event in the event queue (XSt.eq) with a ticket, the executor's next identity (XSt.nextId, the one supply of firing identities and event tickets), and the orchestrator later injects it (inject k), discards it once closed (discard k), or drops it with the whole queue on an immediate termination (terminateNow) or a finish (finish c). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), checked rule by rule against the Rust executor: ExecutorHandle::inject (executor_handle.rs 67-74) refuses once the handle drained or closed, and the Event arm of handle_signal injects.

'Draining, closed or stopped, or finished' is the glossary-free predicate Refusing of this block: the mode is not open (draining, closed, or stopped by the immediate termination of ENV-015), or the loop phase is done. The body's 'execution has completed' is the finished run (phase done, after any finish step). The markdown's scope note on a terminal place (EXEC-042) says the same: a run whose terminal place is marked but whose finish step has not yet been taken is still running, a request there is accepted, and the finish terminal step that follows drops the event, which answers it false (line 4). TypeScript refuses at the call already once a terminal place is marked; that answer is false as well, so the two shapes agree on what the caller learns.

Ruling D44 (a), one injector per executor: lines 1 and 2 read the lifecycle as shared by every injector, as in Java, TypeScript and Python (one handle per executor). In Rust the drained flag belongs to the ExecutorHandle: a second sender on the same channel is answered true after another handle drained or closed, and the executor drops that event on receipt (executor_core/executor.rs 1394-1396), unreported. The markdown's scope note says so; the model has one injector, an assumption of kind A for Rust, under which a handle's own drain or close is the executor's. The token still never reaches the marking in Rust, which is the part of line 2 every sender keeps.

Line 1 is the first shall sentence: no request is answered accepted in a refusing state, so the answer is error (a place that is not an environment place, ENV-002's subject) or refused (false). AC1 (after a close, inject() returns error or false) and AC2 (after drain(), inject() returns error or false) are line 1 at a closed and at a draining state; ENV_006_nonvacuous exercises both, and a finished run as well. An executor that answers accepted while draining and drops the token, the silent drop the body sentence forbids, breaks line 1 (ENV_006_forbids_silentDrop); one that treats draining as open and queues the event breaks lines 1 and 2 (ENV_006_forbids_acceptWhileDraining).

Line 2 is the second shall sentence, read as 'changes nothing': the state after the request is the state before it, so the token reaches neither the marking nor the event queue, nor any other queue a later step would deposit from. An executor that answers refused and queues the event all the same, so that the orchestrator injects it while draining, breaks line 2 alone (ENV_006_forbids_refusedButQueued). Java refuses after the run ended by queueing the event and discarding it at once; at the grain of the model that is one refused request that changes nothing.

Its offers are in ExecCoversW5.Env006Covers (ConsistencyExec.lean; the convention of GlossaryExec.lean: offers are coverage clauses, never block lines). The body sentence and the first EARS sentence demand an answer and are quoted whole; their safety half is line 1, and their existence half is that clause. The 'shall return' of the first shall sentence is Env006Covers: from every refusing state a request into any place with any token has a step, so inject() returns an answer rather than blocking (ENV-015 AC3 says the same after an immediate termination). With line 1 that answer is error or refused, with line 2 it changes nothing. Env006Covers reads every refusing state, reachable or not; the reference's request rule answers in every state (env006_ref_covers). An executor whose inject() blocks once the executor drains, closes or finishes has no request step there, so it meets every line (lines 1 and 2 with no refusing request at all) and fails that clause (env006_covers_hang).

Line 3 is the third shall sentence: an accepted injection is told apart by its ticket, so 'an event of its own' reads as at most one acceptance per ticket on every run. Without it line 4 could not tell two acceptances under one ticket apart, and one answer would pay for both. The reference draws tickets from a supply that no step lowers and an accepted request raises (env006_nextId_le). An executor that does not raise the supply on an accepted request, and so accepts a second injection under the ticket of a queued one and forgets it, meets line 4 (the injection of that ticket answers both acceptances) and breaks line 3 (ENV_006_forbids_sharedTicket): the second token never reaches the marking.

Line 4 is the fourth shall sentence and AC3, which ruling D44 (a) rewords to 'where an admission signal exists, every accepted injection completes it'. A step answers ticket k when it injects k (the signal completes with true) or takes the event with ticket k out of the queue without injecting it (false): the discard of k on a close, an immediate termination, or a finish, each of which empties the queue in the reference. That is ENV-004's reading of an answer (env004_answers); the values of the signal, and which steps may drop an event, are ENV-004's lines, as the sentence says ('with the value ENV-004 gives'), and this line says that every accepted injection reaches one of those steps. It reads only runs that reach their finish (IdealRun, an assumption of kind A: every action returns and the executor is drained, closed or quiescent); a net that never finishes has no ideal run, so ENV_006_nonvacuous decides four ideal runs, one per kind of answer. An executor that answers accepted while open and never queues the event (accept and forget) meets lines 1 to 3 and breaks line 4 on a run that drains and finishes (ENV_006_forbids_forget). So does an executor whose finish leaves the queued events queued, the slip of dropping the end-of-run completion of what is still queued (Java's drainPendingExternalEvents() in the executeLoop finally block, TypeScript's after the loop of run): the future or promise of such an event stays pending forever (ENV_006_forbids_finishKeepsQueue).

Scope of line 4: Java and TypeScript return an admission signal. Rust and Python report acceptance only (ENV-004, ruling D44 (a)), so an accepted event that a stop on a terminal place drops is not reported to their caller; the model still requires the executor to inject, discard or drop every accepted event by the finish, which is the step a signal would complete at, and the markdown's scope note says so for Rust and Python. The result-less forms (TypeScript's injectNoAwait, Java's injectAsync) report nothing and are outside this requirement, as the scope note says; on a draining, closed or finished executor they drop the token without an answer, which at the grain of the model is lines 1 and 2 and Env006Covers with an answer nobody reads.
The test derivation (run to completion, inject, error; drain, inject, error) is ENV_006_nonvacuous's refused requests after a finish and after a drain.

requirements.title: Implicit Long-Running Behavior
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    C.envs ≠ [] →
      (while fun s ↦ Live C s ∧ s.mode = Mode.open, never fun s s' ↦
          R C s (XLbl.finish Cause.quiescent) s') ∧
        ∀ (p : N) (x : T) (r : Reply),
          on fun s s' ↦
            R C s (XLbl.request p x r) s' ∧
              p ∈ C.envs ∧ Live C s ∧ s.mode = Mode.open ∧ isExecPhase s.phase = true,
            shall fun x x_1 ↦ r = Reply.accepted
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C that registers at least one environment place:
(1) while no terminal place is marked and the executor's mode is open (not draining, closed or stopped), R takes no finish quiescent step;
(2) on every request step of R that asks to inject into a registered environment place while no terminal place is marked, the mode is open and the run has not finished, the reply is accepted.
quotes: When environment places are registered with the executor, the executor does NOT terminate at quiescence (no transition armed, no firing in flight, and no completion, publication or external event queued, as in [EXEC-040]) while it has not been drained ([ENV-011]), closed ([ENV-013]) or stopped by an immediate termination ([ENV-015]) and no terminal place is marked ([EXEC-042]).
Instead, it waits for external events that may enable new transitions.
This behavior is derived from the presence of environment places: no explicit flag is needed.

*While* environment places are registered, the executor is open (it has not been drained, closed or stopped by an immediate termination) and no terminal place is marked ([EXEC-042]), the executor *shall not* terminate as quiescent ([EXEC-041]).

*While* environment places are registered, the executor is open and running and no terminal place is marked, *when* a caller asks to inject a token into a registered environment place, the executor *shall* answer the request and *shall* accept the injection.

*While* environment places are registered, the executor is open and no terminal place is marked, *when* the loop reaches its termination test ([EXEC-040]), the executor *shall* go on to its firing pass ([EXEC-001]).

*While* environment places are registered, the executor is open and no terminal place is marked, *when* an accepted injection is queued, the executor *shall* leave its wait ([ENV-005]) and *shall* inject the oldest queued injection in its event step ([ENV-003]).
The executor *shall not* need a long-running flag or any setting other than the registered environment places to wait at quiescence.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The registered environment places are C.envs (glossary: Environment place, ENV-001); 'environment places are registered' is C.envs ≠ []. The run has not finished ('running') while its phase is not done (isExecPhase), and a run ends with a step finish c, where c is the termination cause of EXEC-041; 'terminate as quiescent' is finish quiescent. A request step request p x r is a caller asking to inject x into p and getting the reply r (accepted, refused or error). The mode is open until a drain (draining, ENV-011), a close (closed, ENV-013) or an immediate termination (stopped, ENV-015): 'open (it has not been drained, closed or stopped by an immediate termination)' is mode = open. 'No terminal place is marked' is the glossary term Live. 'The termination test' is the phase test, 'its firing pass' is the phase pass that the step begin enters, 'its wait' is the phase await (step 6), 'its event step' is the phase events (step 2), and the queued injections are the event queue eq, oldest first. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), checked rule by rule against the Rust executor: the termination checks of executor_core/executor.rs (1084-1095), the exit test of the wait (1137-1143) and ExecutorHandle::inject (executor_handle.rs 67-74); and against Java and TypeScript, whose shouldTerminate (BitmapNetExecutor.java 1264-1276, bitmap-net-executor.ts 697-711) ends an executor with environment places only when draining or closed.

Guard (ruling D73 (a)). Line 1 forbids only the quiescent finish, which is what the requirement is about. The other causes are tied to their own conditions by EXEC-041 (finish closed only once closed or stopped, finish stopped only once stopped, finish terminal only with a terminal place marked, and no step but a finish ends the run), so an executor that meets EXEC-041 and line 1 does not end at all under the guard. The reference offers no finish of any cause there. The guard is the open mode and not the registered places alone: a drained executor with environment places ends at quiescence (ENV-011), which line 1 allows (ENV_010_allows_drainedQuiescence). A marked terminal place ends the run whatever is registered (EXEC-042), which is why both lines and the coverage clause carry Live. Runtime exits that sit outside the guard: in Rust an executor whose signal channel has closed, every sender dropped, accepts no injection and ends at quiescence as a drained one does (dropping an ExecutorHandle sends a drain first), which is a drain in the model; Rust's run_sync has no signal channel and accepts no injection, so it is not an executor this requirement binds; a Java interrupt taken while the loop waits ends the run as interrupted, a cause EXEC-041 keeps out of the model (N), as are faults of the host runtime.

Quiescence (rulings D5, D13 (a) and D20, ENVB-R7 item 1) is EXEC-040's rest: no transition armed, no firing in flight, no completion, publication or external event queued (Rest of GlossaryExec). A reaped transition that is still enabled does not count. Line 1 does not need the term: it forbids the quiescent finish in every state under the guard, at rest or not, and EXEC-040 and EXEC-041 already allow that finish only at rest.

The first shall sentence and the first quoted body sentence are line 1, and so is AC3 (an executor with environment places does not terminate at quiescence). ENV_010_forbids_quiesceAnyway is an executor that ends at quiescence whatever is registered: started with an environment place and nothing to do, it ends at its first termination test.

The second shall sentence is line 2 and the first part of Env010Covers: the request is answered (the clause, a step that is offered in every state under the guard) and the answer is an acceptance (line 2). Line 2 alone does not make the executor answer, since it speaks only of the request steps R takes; the clause does. ENV_010_forbids_deafWait answers an injection refused while its wait is parked, as if it had ended (it breaks line 2). env010_covers_muteWait does not answer at all while parked, so the caller can not inject (it meets both lines and fails the first part of the clause). Line 2 and the clause carry Live: once a terminal place is marked the run is about to end with finish terminal (EXEC-042), and what a request there gets is ENV-006's, where the reference accepts it and the finish answers it false, and TypeScript refuses it at the call (bitmap-net-executor.ts 611 and 652, the terminalReached test). The caller learns false either way, and ENV_010_allows_terminalRefusal shows that ENV-010 allows the TypeScript shape.

AC1 and the sentence 'Instead, it waits for external events that may enable new transitions.' are line 1 together with the first two parts of Env010Covers: at quiescence the executor does not end (line 1), goes on from its termination test to its firing pass (the second part), whose end leads to the wait (EXEC-001, CONC-010), and accepts a caller's injection there (the first part). The third shall sentence is the second part. env010_covers_hold is an executor that holds at its termination test once its only work is queued injections: it accepts every request and never goes on to inject them (it meets both lines and fails the second part). That the end of the pass leads to the park (endPass, park) is EXEC-001's and CONC-010's.

AC5 (injecting a token resumes execution from quiescence) and the fourth shall sentence are the first, third and fourth parts of Env010Covers: the injection is accepted while the executor idles (the first part), the wait does not stay idle with an injection queued, it wakes or injects (the fourth part), and step 2 injects the oldest queued injection (the third part). env010_covers_stuckWait is a wait that an arrival does not end, and env010_covers_noInject a step 2 that never injects; each meets both lines and fails its part of the clause. What the inject step does to the queue and the marking is ENV-003's, that an accepted request clears the park is ENV-005's (CONC-010), and that the injected token arms the transition it enables is the injected-token clause of TIME-010 and TIME-013 (the inject step writes its place, ruling D6). ENV_010_nonvacuous decides the test derivation on the reference: an executor with one environment place reaches a test at rest and does not end, parks, accepts an injection while parked, injects it, fires the transition it enables, reaches a test at rest again and does not end, is drained, and then ends quiescent with the token moved.

AC2, the fifth shall sentence and the body sentence on the flag: the only premise on the configuration, of the statement and of Env010Covers, is C.envs ≠ [], and the configuration has no long-running field, so the waiting is derived from the registered places alone. An executor that waits only when a separate long-running flag is set (env010_flagStep) is the reference when the flag is set (env010_flagStep_true) and the quiesceAnyway executor when it is not, so with the flag at its unset default it is forbidden (ENV_010_forbids_quiesceAnyway). An executor with such a flag set by default meets the statement; that no such flag exists on the executor API is API shape (kind Q), with no Lean witness beyond the unset flag: Rust derives the waiting from the registered set (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/executor.rs 142), Java and TypeScript from the environment places given to the builder (BitmapNetExecutor.java 351, bitmap-net-executor.ts 345).

AC4 and the sentence 'When no environment places are registered, the executor terminates at quiescence per [EXEC-040].' belong to EXEC-040, whose block is premised on C.envs = [], the complement of this block's premise. env010_finish_iff_noEnvs is the bridge on the reference: at a termination test at rest, with no terminal place marked and the mode open, a finish quiescent step is offered exactly when no environment place is registered. ENV_010_allows_noEnvQuiescence shows the same net without environment places ending at its first test.

Its offers are in ExecCoversW5.Env010Covers (ConsistencyExec.lean; the convention of GlossaryExec.lean: offers are coverage clauses, never block lines), as ENV-002's are in Env002Covers. The second, third and fourth EARS sentences demand an answer and are quoted whole; the safety half of the second is line 2, and their existence halves are that clause: in every state where environment places are registered, no terminal place is marked and the mode is open, R offers the accepted request, the begin step at the test, the inject step in step 2 and the way out of the wait. The clause reads every such state, reachable or not, and the reference meets it (env010_ref_covers). Requests into a place that is not an environment place are ENV-002's (Java and TypeScript answer error, Rust and Python deposit, ruling D89 (a)); line 2 and the first part of Env010Covers speak only of registered environment places, where all four runtimes accept. Requests while draining, closed, stopped or after the finish are refused (ENV-006, ENV-011, ENV-013). Injections before the run starts are outside the model, whose runs start at xinit in mode open.

requirements.title: Graceful Drain
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    (on fun s s' ↦ R C s XLbl.drain s', shall fun s s' ↦
        s.mode = Mode.open ∧ s' = Env011.drained s ∨ s.mode ≠ Mode.open ∧ s' = s) ∧
      (∀ (p : N) (x : T) (r : Reply),
          on fun s s' ↦ s.mode = Mode.draining ∧ R C s (XLbl.request p x r) s', shall
            fun s s' ↦ r ≠ Reply.accepted ∧ s' = s) ∧
        (∀ (k : ℕ),
            while fun s ↦ s.mode = Mode.draining, never fun s s' ↦
              R C s (XLbl.discard k) s') ∧
          (∀ (s : XSt N T) (l : XLbl N T) (s' : XSt N T),
              s.mode = Mode.draining →
                Env011.sameAsOpen C s l = true →
                  (R C s l s' ↔
                    ∃ s'',
                      R C (Env011.withMode Mode.open s) l s'' ∧
                        s' = Env011.withMode Mode.draining s'')) ∧
            (on fun s s' ↦
                (s.mode = Mode.draining ∧ Live C s) ∧ ∃ c, R C s (XLbl.finish c) s', shall
                fun s x ↦ s.phase = Phase.test ∧ Rest C s) ∧
              (while fun s ↦
                  s.mode = Mode.draining ∧ Live C s ∧ s.phase = Phase.test ∧ Rest C s,
                  never fun s s' ↦
                  ∃ l,
                    R C s l s' ∧
                      l.outside = false ∧
                        (∀ (a : Option Bool), l = XLbl.snapshot a → s' ≠ s) ∧
                          ∀ (c : Cause), l ≠ XLbl.finish c) ∧
                ∀ (l : XLbl N T),
                  on fun s s' ↦
                    (s.mode = Mode.draining ∧ Rest C s) ∧
                      (Env011.waitEffect s l).isSome = true ∧ R C s l s',
                    shall fun s s' ↦ Env011.waitEffect s l = some s'
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C:
a drain step from an open state enters mode draining, wakes the wait and changes nothing else; a drain step from any other mode (draining, closed or stopped) changes nothing;
a request step from a draining state is answered with something other than accepted and changes nothing;
no discard step starts in a draining state;

from a draining state s, every step whose label is not a request, a snapshot, a lifecycle call (drain, close, terminateNow), or, at rest with environment places, a begin, finish, park or wake step, leads to s' exactly when the same label leads from s in mode open to some s'' and s' is s'' in mode draining;

a finish step from a draining state with no terminal place marked starts at the termination test and at rest: no transition armed, no firing in flight, and the completion, publication and event queues empty;

in a draining state with no terminal place marked, at the termination test and at rest, every executor step is a finish step (outside steps such as the clock advancing are still possible, and an answer to a snapshot request that leaves the state as it is is not a step of the loop and is allowed);
a park or wake step from a draining state at rest has the effect of the wait and nothing else: a park sets the parked flag, a wake clears it and returns to step 1 of the cycle.
quotes: The executor provides a `drain()` method that signals graceful shutdown.
After `drain()` is called:
New `inject()` calls are rejected (return error/false).
Already-queued external events are processed normally.
In-flight actions are allowed to complete.
The executor terminates when quiescent (no armed transitions, no in-flight, no pending events).

Items 2 to 4 hold while no terminal place is marked: a marked terminal place stops the executor at once, abandoning the actions in flight and ending the run with the queued external events unapplied ([EXEC-042]).
For executors without environment places, a drain does not change when the executor terminates, since the executor already terminates at quiescence.

*When* an open executor is drained, it *shall* enter the draining mode and *shall* leave the rest of its state as it was, apart from waking its wait ([CONC-010]): its marking, its queued external events and its firings in flight stay as they were.
*If* an executor that is not open (draining, closed or stopped) is drained, *then* the drain *shall* change nothing.
*While* the executor is draining, *when* an injection is requested, the executor *shall* reject it (error or false) and *shall* change nothing.
*While* the executor is draining, it *shall not* discard a queued external event.

*While* the executor is draining, it *shall* take every step of its cycle as it takes it while open, with the same effect: it *shall* inject the queued external events, let the actions in flight complete, settle their outcomes and start ready transitions as an open executor does; only the answers to requests and snapshot requests ([ENV-014]), and the wait and the termination test of an executor with environment places at quiescence, differ.
A close or an immediate termination of a draining executor is governed by [ENV-013] and [ENV-015].

*While* the executor is draining and no terminal place is marked, it *shall not* terminate except at the termination test of a cycle ([EXEC-001]) that finds it quiescent: no transition armed, no firing in flight, and no completion, publication or external event queued.
*While* the executor is draining and no terminal place is marked, *when* the termination test of a cycle finds it quiescent, the executor *shall* terminate.
*While* the executor is draining and quiescent, *when* it enters or ends its wait, it *shall* change nothing but the wait, and ending the wait *shall* take it to the first step of the next cycle.
*While* the executor is draining and quiescent and no terminal place is marked, it *shall* end its wait at once, without waiting for an arrival or a timer ([CONC-010]).
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The executor state carries a lifecycle mode (open, draining, closed, stopped); drain is the outside step of a caller calling drain(), request p x r a caller's inject() of x into p answered r (accepted, refused or error), discard k the executor dropping queued event k unapplied, park and wake the start and the end of the wait of step 6, and finish c a termination with cause c (EXEC-041). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), checked rule by rule against the Rust executor: ExecutorHandle::drain and inject (executor_handle.rs 67-113), the Drain arm of handle_signal, the draining termination check and the draining exit before the wait (executor_core/executor.rs 1087-1089, 1138-1143, 1424-1426); Java BitmapNetExecutor.drain, shouldTerminate and awaitWork, TypeScript drain, its termination check and its latched wake run the same rules.

Scope (ruling D20, clash env-b#4, ENVB-R7 item 7): items 2 to 4 hold while no terminal place is marked; a marked terminal place stops the executor at once and abandons the actions in flight, and the run ends with the queued events unapplied (EXEC-042), in every runtime whatever the mode. That end is the finish terminal, not a discard step, so it does not touch line 3. Lines 5 and 6 carry the premise (Live). Lines 1 to 4 and 7 need none: the reference's rules are mode-blind there too, and EXEC-042's own lines govern the terminal stop.

'After drain() is called' is the mode draining: the drain step sets it, and only a close (ENV-013) or an immediate termination (ENV-015) leaves it, both lifecycle steps with their own requirements; the quoted sentence on a close or an immediate termination of a draining executor says so, and line 4 leaves the lifecycle calls out of its comparison for that reason. A drained executor that later closes is governed by ENV-013 from that step on. After the run ends the mode stays draining, so line 2 also answers a request to a drained executor that has finished; ENV-006 states the replies in every mode.

The first and second shall sentences are line 1. A drain wakes the wait (CONC-010, ruling D13 (a): a drain is a wake reason), which is the parked flag of the state; nothing else changes. An executor whose drain also drops the queued events breaks line 1 (ENV_011_forbids_drainDrops), and so does one whose drain leaves a parked wait asleep (ENV_011_forbids_drainKeepsParked). A drain of an executor that is not open, whether draining, closed or stopped (ENV-015), changes nothing: Rust's drain() returns false and sends no signal once the handle is drained, Java and TypeScript set a flag that is already set (a closed executor stays closed, closed is tested first, and a stopped one stays stopped). The reference has no drain step there, which line 1's second half allows; an executor whose drain reopens a closed executor into draining breaks it (ENV_011_forbids_reopenClosed).

The third shall sentence and item 1 (AC2) are line 2: while draining, an inject() is not accepted (it is refused, or error for a place that is not an environment place) and changes nothing. An executor that accepts it breaks the first half (ENV_011_forbids_acceptWhileDraining), one that answers refused and queues the event anyway breaks the second (ENV_011_forbids_queueRefused). In Rust the draining flag is a field of the handle (executor_handle.rs 44, 68), and an event sent through a second sender after the Drain signal is answered true and discarded (executor_core/executor.rs, the Event arm with draining set); the model has one injector per executor, an assumption for Rust and Python (ruling D44 (a), ENVB-R3). Events accepted before the drain were queued before the Drain signal in the one channel, so they are 'already queued'.

The fourth shall sentence and item 2 (AC3) are lines 3, 4 and 5. Line 3: a draining executor never discards a queued event (ENV_011_forbids_discardWhileDraining). Line 4 for the inject label: a queued event is injected while draining exactly as while open (ENV_011_forbids_stallEvents, an executor that stops injecting once drained). Line 5: a draining executor terminates only with the event queue empty, so no queued event is lost to the finish. 'Processed before termination' as liveness is an ideal run (IdealRun, kind A: every action returns) together with coverage; ENV_011_nonvacuous decides one.

The fifth shall sentence is line 4, and with it item 3 (AC4) and the no-op sentence. Line 4 compares a draining state with the same state in mode open, label by label: the steps an action takes (write, flush, return, expiry of its budget), the settle steps (commit, fail, tdeposit), the publication steps, injection, the update, the deadline step, the firing pass and, away from rest, the wait. 'Allowed to complete' is that the actions' own steps and the settle steps are those of an open executor; line 5 adds that a draining executor does not terminate before they are settled. The answers that do differ are named in the sentence: a request is refused (line 2), a snapshot request is rejected (ENV-014 AC4, which every runtime applies after a drain, with or without environment places), and at rest an executor with environment places ends its wait and terminates where an open one waits for an arrival (ENV-010, lines 5 to 7).

Line 4 restates an open-mode requirement where the two modes agree: without environment places begin, finish, park and wake are compared at rest too, so with line 6 an open executor without environment places takes no executor step at a termination test at rest but a finish. That is EXEC-040's own line, which the no-op sentence presupposes.

The no-op sentence (ruling D20, clash env-b#6, ENVB-R7 item 2) is line 4 without environment places: then begin, finish, park and wake are compared at rest too, so a drained executor without environment places terminates exactly where it would have terminated had it not been drained. The literal reading 'drain() is a no-op', a drain step that changes nothing, is the mutant ENV_011_mutant_noop: it is told apart from the requirement by an executor that ignores the drain of an executor without environment places, which meets the literal reading and breaks line 1. The rewording is what every runtime does: after a drain, snapshot() is rejected whatever the net (ENV-014 AC4), so the state does change.

The sixth shall sentence is line 5 and item 4 read with 'armed' for 'enabled' (ruling D5, ENVB-R7 item 1): quiescent is the glossary term Rest of GlossaryExec (restB), nothing armed, nothing in flight, nothing queued (ruling D13 (a)), and the finish is taken at the termination test of a cycle (EXEC-001), not elsewhere in the cycle. A firing counts as in flight until it is settled and its publications are deposited (EXEC-040). An executor that terminates while an action is in flight breaks line 5 (ENV_011_forbids_finishInFlight), and so does one that terminates from its wait (ENV_011_forbids_finishInWait). Rust leaves its loop from step 6 when it is draining and quiescent (executor_core/executor.rs 1138-1143); the model reads that exit as the wake and the next cycle's termination test, which change nothing at rest. The cause of a draining finish is not fixed here: ENV-011 alone admits a draining executor that finishes with cause closed at quiescence, and EXEC-041 excludes it (a finish closed needs a closing mode, a finish stopped a stopped one, a finish terminal a marked terminal place), leaving quiescent.

The seventh shall sentence and AC5 are line 6: at a termination test with no terminal place marked and at rest, a draining executor takes no executor step but a finish (in particular no firing pass, begin). An executor that treats a draining executor with environment places as an open one there, beginning a pass where it should terminate, breaks it (ENV_011_forbids_neverEnds). Java's draining termination check reads no external event queue: it is empty there because step 2 of the same cycle emptied it and a draining executor accepts no new event.

The eighth shall sentence is line 7: a draining executor at rest that enters its wait changes only the parked flag, and one that ends it changes only that flag and the phase, which returns to step 1 of the cycle; an executor whose drained wait at rest skips to the termination test, past the enablement update, breaks it (ENV_011_forbids_wakeSkipsCycle). The reference may park a draining executor at rest (parkStep does not read the mode), where no runtime waits: Rust leaves the loop before its wait, Java's awaitWork does not wait when draining (BitmapNetExecutor.java 2012, hasEnvironmentPlaces && !draining), TypeScript returns on the latched wake. That is harmless because the reference's wake is offered in every live wait, so line 7 constrains the effect of such a park and does not forbid it.

Existence is coverage, not a line, and belongs to the consistency theorem: Env011Covers below is the conjunct ENV-011 asks of it, a clause of ExecCoversW5 (ConsistencyExec.lean), with three clauses. AC1 (drain() is available): a drain step is offered from every open state. The seventh shall sentence and AC5 ('shall terminate'): finish quiescent is offered at every termination test of a draining executor with no terminal place marked and at rest. The ninth shall sentence (the wait ends at once): a wake is offered in every wait of a draining executor with no terminal place marked and at rest. The reference meets all three (env011_ref_covers, from env011_drain_offered, env011_finish_offered and env011_wake_offered). AC1, AC5's 'shall terminate' and the ninth shall sentence are therefore enforced by the consistency theorem and not by this block's lines: an executor with an edge-triggered wait, whose parked loop wakes only after an arrival cleared its flag or on a timer (the hazard TypeScript's latched wake guards against, bitmap-net-executor.ts 225-242), meets every line (env011_lostWake_meets) while a drain raised before it parks leaves it asleep for good; it fails Env011Covers (env011_lostWake_not_covered, on the run: the open executor with an environment place reaches its wait at rest, is drained, then parks).
The test derivation (inject, drain, the queued event processed, a new inject rejected, termination at quiescence) is ENV_011_nonvacuous's run.
The model reads one executor per configuration with its own queue; Rust's run_sync and the exits of a dropped handle (the handle's Drop sends a Drain) are ENV-010's notes (ruling D73 (a)).

requirements.title: Immediate Close
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    (on fun s s' ↦ R C s XLbl.close s', shall fun s s' ↦
        s' =
          { M := s.M, now := s.now, cyc := s.cyc, st := s.st, fl := s.fl,
            nextId := s.nextId, cq := s.cq, pq := s.pq, eq := s.eq, mode := Mode.closed,
            phase := s.phase, order := s.order, delta := s.delta, started := s.started,
            parked := s'.parked }) ∧
      (∀ (p : N) (x : T) (r : Reply),
          on fun s s' ↦ s.mode = Mode.closed ∧ R C s (XLbl.request p x r) s', shall
            fun s s' ↦ r ≠ Reply.accepted ∧ s' = s) ∧
        (∀ (l : XLbl N T),
            on fun s s' ↦ s.mode ≠ Mode.closed ∧ s'.mode = Mode.closed ∧ R C s l s', shall
              fun x x_1 ↦ l = XLbl.close) ∧
          (∀ (l : XLbl N T),
              on fun s s' ↦ s.mode = Mode.closed ∧ s'.mode ≠ Mode.closed ∧ R C s l s',
                shall fun x x_1 ↦ l = XLbl.terminateNow) ∧
            (while fun s ↦ s.mode = Mode.closed, never fun s s' ↦
                ∃ k, R C s (XLbl.inject k) s') ∧
              (∀ (c : Cause),
                  on fun s s' ↦ s.mode = Mode.closed ∧ R C s (XLbl.finish c) s', shall
                    fun x s' ↦ s'.eq = []) ∧
                (∀ (c : Cause),
                    on fun s s' ↦
                      Live C s ∧ s.mode = Mode.closed ∧ R C s (XLbl.finish c) s', shall
                      fun s x ↦ s.fl = []) ∧
                  (while fun s ↦
                      s.mode = Mode.closed ∧ Live C s ∧ s.phase = Phase.test ∧ s.fl = [],
                      never fun s s' ↦
                      ∃ l,
                        R C s l s' ∧
                          l.outside = false ∧
                            (∀ (a : Option Bool), l = XLbl.snapshot a → s' ≠ s) ∧
                              ∀ (c : Cause), l ≠ XLbl.finish c) ∧
                    (∀ (i : ℕ) (l : XLbl N T),
                        on fun s s' ↦
                          s.mode = Mode.closed ∧
                            i ∈ List.map (fun x ↦ x.id) s.fl ∧
                              i ∉ List.map (fun x ↦ x.id) s'.fl ∧ R C s l s',
                          shall fun x x_1 ↦
                          l = XLbl.commit i ∨ l = XLbl.fail i ∨ l = XLbl.tdeposit i) ∧
                      on fun s s' ↦ s.mode = Mode.closed ∧ R C s XLbl.endPublications s',
                        shall fun s x ↦ s.pq = []
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C:

a close step sets the mode to closed and changes no field of the state but the mode and the parked flag: the marking, the clock readings now and cyc, the clock statuses, the firings in flight, the completion, publication and event queues, the identity supply, the loop phase and the pass's remaining order, hidden tail and started flag stay as they are;
a request step from a closed state is not accepted and leaves the state as it is;
a step that turns a mode other than closed into closed is a close step;
a step that turns the closed mode into another mode is an immediate termination step;
while the mode is closed, no inject step happens;
a finish step from a closed state, whatever its cause, leaves the event queue empty;
a finish step from a closed state with no terminal place marked happens only when no firing is in flight;

while the mode is closed, no terminal place is marked, the phase is the termination test and no firing is in flight, no step happens that is neither an outside step nor a finish (an answer to a snapshot request that leaves the state as it is is not a step of the loop and is allowed);
a step from a closed state after which a firing identity in flight before it is no longer in flight is a commit, fail or tdeposit step of that firing;
an endPublications step (the end of step 1b) from a closed state happens only when the publication queue is empty.
quotes: The executor provides a `close()` method for immediate shutdown.
Calling `close()` after `drain()` escalates from graceful to immediate shutdown.
A close does not stop the firing pass.

While an action is in flight, a closed executor keeps running its cycles and may start ready transitions, whose actions are then in flight too; it terminates at the first termination test ([EXEC-040]) that finds no action in flight.
A close alone therefore does not bound a run whose firings overlap; an immediate termination ([ENV-015]) does.
A run budget ([ENV-016]) bounds only the caller's wait.

*When* the executor takes a close, it *shall* enter the closed mode and *shall* leave every part of its state other than its mode and whether its loop waits ([CONC-010]) as it was: the marking, the clock of every transition, the clock reading of the cycle, the actions in flight, the queued outcomes, publications and external events, the supply of identities, the phase of its loop and the rest of a firing pass.
*While* the executor is closed, it *shall* reject every `inject()` call, and a rejected call *shall* change nothing.
The executor *shall* enter the closed mode only when it takes a close, and *shall* leave it only for an immediate termination ([ENV-015]).
*While* the executor is closed, it *shall not* inject a queued external event.
*When* a closed executor ends its run, it *shall* leave no external event queued.
*While* the executor is closed and no terminal place is marked, it *shall* end its run only when no action is in flight, or on a cancellation it observes in its wait ([EXEC-041]).
*While* the executor is closed, no terminal place is marked and no action is in flight, it *shall* take no step at a termination test ([EXEC-040]) other than ending its run.
*While* the executor is closed, it *shall* remove an action from the actions in flight only by settling its outcome.
*While* the executor is closed, it *shall* end step 1b of a cycle ([EXEC-001]) only when no publication is queued.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The close is the outside step close; the closed mode is Mode.closed. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), whose close rule (closeStep) takes a close from the open or the draining mode.

Naming: the markdown's 'the executor takes a close' is the close step. In Java and TypeScript that is the call of close(), which sets the closed flag the loop and inject() read. In Rust it is the executor reading the Close signal in Phase 2 (executor_core/executor.rs handle_signal, Close arm); the handle refuses injections from the call of close() (executor_handle.rs close sets drained), and every event sent before the call travels the channel ahead of the Close. A Rust run is therefore the model run in which the injections of those events come before the close step and the requests refused by the handle come after it: a refused request changes nothing (line 2), so placing it after the close step changes no state. One injector per run is assumed (Rust's events from a second sender, sent after the Close, are answered true and dropped by the Close arm), as in the reference's own notes on D44 (a).

Item 1 and AC4 ('inject() returns error/false after close') are line 2: a request to a closed executor is refused (an environment place) or an error (not one, Java and TypeScript), never accepted, and queues nothing (ENV_013_forbids_closedAccepts). Which of refused and error, and the false or error value inject() hands the caller, are ENV-002's and ENV-006's subject.

Item 2, AC2 and ruling D44 (a): line 5 is the common line, 'a closed executor injects no queued event' (ENV_013_forbids_closedInjects), and line 6 says no event is left queued when a closed run ends (ENV_013_forbids_finishKeepsQueue). An event still queued after the close leaves the queue by a discard step or by the finish. Java completes it with false at loop exit (drainPendingExternalEvents); the reference also offers the discard in step 2 and in the wait, so the markdown's informative sentence on when Java and TypeScript answer such an inject() names no instant and is not a line. That the answer is false exactly at the discard or the finish is ENV-004's line. Which accepted events are still queued at the close is implementation shape, kind N: Java and TypeScript discard every event still queued when the flag is set; Rust and Python inject every event sent before the close (the run of the naming assumption) and answer inject() at enqueue time.

Item 3, AC3 and the shutdown being a close, not a stop: line 1 keeps the firings in flight, their queued outcomes and their queued publications at the close (ENV_013_forbids_closeAbandons), line 9 says a firing leaves the firings in flight while closed only by being settled (ENV_013_forbids_closedDropsInFlight: a closed executor that abandons its firings at step 1 and then finishes closed with nothing in flight), line 10 says a closed executor ends step 1b only with no publication queued, so a batch an action flushed is still published after the close, as ruling D17 has it for every published token (ENV_013_forbids_closedSkipsPublications: a closed executor that stops publishing and finishes with the batch lost), and line 7 says the run ends, with no terminal place marked, only when none is in flight (ENV_013_forbids_finishInFlight). Together they are 'in-flight actions complete before termination'. Line 9 does not say where a settle happens (step 1, the wait or the pass); that is EXEC-001's. That the actions do return, and that a returned outcome is settled, is coverage, not a line here: ExecCovers (every firing in flight can return) and ValidatedBy (every completion the loop may settle is settled) in the consistency theorem (ConsistencyExec.lean), neither of which depends on the mode; settlement in the closed mode is the reference's commit, as spec/04-execution-model.md says of a close (it waits for the actions in flight and takes their completions up in step 1), exercised by ENV_013_nonvacuous. An executor that takes no step at all after the close passes every line here; it fails that coverage. The seventh shall sentence's 'or on a cancellation it observes in its wait ([EXEC-041])' is out of the model, which has no interrupt (EXEC-041's assumes): line 7 states the sentence without it, and Java's interrupt path (awaitCompletionPolling ending the loop interrupted while closed with actions in flight, BitmapNetExecutor.java 2062-2070) is that cancellation, allowed by EXEC-041 and not a run of the model.

Item 4 and ruling D85 (a): line 7 is 'terminates after in-flight actions complete'; line 8 is 'it terminates at the first termination test that finds no action in flight': at such a test, with no terminal place marked, a closed executor takes no executor step but a finish (EXEC-040's line 3 read with nothing in flight in place of Rest), in particular it begins no firing pass (ENV_013_forbids_closeWaitsForQuiescence: a close that behaves as a drain, starting a ready transition with nothing in flight). That a finish is in fact offered at such a test is coverage: Env013Covers, a clause of the consistency theorem's ExecCoversW5 (ConsistencyExec.lean), asks for finish closed at every such test, and the reference offers it (env013_finish_offered). Line 8 alone is safety: an executor that offers no step at such a test (one whose finish closed also waits for the event queue to empty, which no closed step ever empties) passes this block and fails Env013Covers. Line 8 bans loop steps only: answering a snapshot request, which is not a step of the loop (EXEC-041, EXEC-042), is allowed at the test provided it changes nothing (the exemption EXEC-042's line 1 makes). The permission 'may start ready transitions' while an action is in flight is the reference starting a firing after the close (ENV_013_nonvacuous); a close therefore does not bound the run (the quoted 'A close alone therefore does not bound ...' sentence), and the bound is ENV-015's immediate termination; a run budget (ENV-016) bounds only the caller's wait, since its expiry ends the wait and not the loop (EXEC-041; under the close policy it is a close, ENV-016's line 2).

'A close does not stop the firing pass.' is line 1 at the close step: the phase, the pass's remaining order, its hidden tail and its started flag stay (ENV_013_forbids_closeStopsPass: a close taken mid-pass that empties the order, so the ready transitions left in it never start). The steps after the close are EXEC-003's: its endPass line, which reads no mode, ends a pass only with the order exhausted, so an executor that ends a closed pass early breaks EXEC-003, not this block. Line 1 also keeps the clock readings now and cyc, at which steps 4 and 5 judge readiness, and the identity supply.

Scope (ENVB-R7 item 7, D20): the markdown's 'unless a terminal place is marked ([EXEC-042])' is the premise Live C s of lines 7 and 8. A terminal stop ends the run whatever is in flight, the firings abandoned (EXEC-042's finish terminal, which keeps them in the state); lines 6 and 9 hold across it (the finish clears the event queue, and an abandoned firing is not removed). The cause the finish reports is EXEC-041's: at a rest reached after a close the reference offers both quiescent and closed (ruling D53 (c), ENV_013_nonvacuous).

The mode lines 3 and 4 pin what EXEC-041's lines 6 and 7 read as 'a close was requested': the mode becomes closed only by a close (ENV_013_forbids_drainCloses) and stays closed until the run ends unless an immediate termination ([ENV-015], Java, Mode.stopped) replaces it (ENV_013_forbids_drainReopens). The escalation sentence 'Calling `close()` after `drain()` escalates from graceful to immediate shutdown.' is the reference's close from the draining mode (ENV_013_nonvacuous), after which every closed line applies. That the close is offered at all, from the open mode ('provides a `close()` method') and from the draining mode (the escalation), is coverage, not a line: inside the consistency theorem ENV-016's coverage clause Env016Covers and its line 2 carry it (an expiry under the close policy is offered in every executing phase and is a close step from the open and the draining mode), and the reference offers the close from both modes in every phase (env013_close_offered). A second close of a closed executor is no step of the reference (Rust and Java return without effect); line 1 does not need it.

AC1 ('close() signals immediate shutdown') is line 1: the close step enters the closed mode, which every other line reads. Waking the wait on a close is CONC-010's (the reference's close clears parked), which is why line 1 leaves the parked flag free.

The test derivation (an executor with an action in flight is closed; the action completes; queued events are discarded; the executor terminates) is ENV_013_nonvacuous's run: an event queued before the close is discarded, a request after it is refused, the firing in flight is committed after the close, and the run finishes closed with nothing in flight. A second run of ENV_013_nonvacuous publishes, after the close, a batch the action flushed before it.

requirements.title: Mid-Execution Marking Snapshot
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    (∀ (a : Option Bool),
        on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.snapshot a) s', shall fun s s' ↦ s' = s) ∧
      (∀ (a : Option Bool),
          on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.snapshot a) s', shall fun s x ↦
            s.mode ≠ Mode.open → a = none) ∧
        (∀ (a : Option Bool),
            on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.snapshot a) s', shall fun s x ↦
              s.mode = Mode.open → isExecPhase s.phase = true → a ≠ none) ∧
          (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.snapshot (some false)) s', shall fun s x ↦
              s.fl = []) ∧
            (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.snapshot (some false)) s', shall fun s x ↦
                s.eq = []) ∧
              ∀ (s0 : XSt N T) (tr : List (XStep N T)),
                s0.fl = [] →
                  s0.pq = [] →
                    XRun R C s0 tr →
                      ∀ x ∈ tr, x.2.1 = XLbl.snapshot (some false) → x.1.pq = []
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C:
for every answer a, a snapshot step answered a ends in the state it starts from;
for every answer a, a snapshot step answered a from a state whose mode is not open (draining, closed or stopped) answers none;
for every answer a, a snapshot step answered a from a state whose mode is open and whose loop is running (an executing phase) does not answer none;
a snapshot step answered some false starts in a state with no firing in flight;
a snapshot step answered some false starts in a state whose event queue is empty;
on every run of R that starts in a state with no firing in flight and no published batch queued, a snapshot step answered some false starts in a state whose publication queue is empty.
quotes: The executor exposes a `snapshot()` operation that returns a point-in-time copy of the current marking **without affecting lifecycle** — unlike `drain()` ([ENV-011]) and `close()` ([ENV-013]), it neither stops nor pauses execution.
**Work in flight** means either of two things: an **action** that has started and not completed, or an **external event the executor has accepted but not yet injected** ([ENV-003], [ENV-004]).
Consequently a snapshot offered as a restore point for [CORE-073] MUST be taken at a moment when no work is in flight — no action, and no accepted external event still awaiting injection.

A firing therefore counts as in flight **from the moment its inputs are consumed** — not from the moment its action first suspends — so the window covers the action's synchronous prefix and any event-store callback the firing triggers, and the indication MUST report work in flight throughout it.
**The answer and its two readings.** An answer to `snapshot()` is either a rejection or a marking, and a marking either reports a restore point (no work in flight) or reports work in flight.
A refusal of a restore-point snapshot while work is in flight reports work in flight; the rejection is reserved, while the run lasts, for an executor that has been drained, closed or terminated.
An answer that reports a restore point describes the instant at which the executor captured it.

An answer to a request the orchestrator could not serve reports work in flight and may describe an earlier instant of the same run, while a parked executor still answers with the current marking (AC9).

*When* the executor answers a `snapshot()` request, it *shall* leave its whole state as it was, among it the marking, the lifecycle, the firings in flight, the queued completions, publications and external events, the clocks of the transitions, and the orchestrator's place in its cycle, a wait it is parked in included ([CORE-071]).
*If* the executor has been drained or closed ([ENV-011], [ENV-013]), or terminated immediately ([ENV-015]), *then* it *shall* reject a `snapshot()` request.
*While* the executor is running and has been neither drained, closed nor terminated, it *shall not* reject a `snapshot()` request.

*If* a firing is in flight at the instant the executor captures the marking for a `snapshot()` answer, counted from the moment its inputs are consumed until the executor has processed its completion and deposited every token its action published ([IO-015]), *then* the executor *shall not* report that answer as a restore point.

*If* an external event that the executor accepted before a `snapshot()` request is still queued for injection at the instant the executor captures the marking for that request's answer, *then* the executor *shall not* report that answer as a restore point.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A snapshot request and its answer are one step labelled snapshot a, taken at the instant the executor captures the marking. The answer a is none for a rejection, some true for a marking that reports work in flight, some false for a marking that reports a restore point. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean): it answers snapAnswer s (some of whether a firing is in flight or an event is queued while the mode is open, none otherwise), in step 2 after the injections, at entry to the enablement update and in the wait, which is Rust's handle_signal Snapshot arm (executor_core/executor.rs 1433-1446) and Java's serviceMarkingRequest after the external-events phase.

Which marking an answer returns is a modelling assumption (kind A), not a line. The label carries no marking: the model reads the marking of an answer as the marking s.M of the state the step starts from, which line 1 makes the marking of the state it ends in too, and an executor that answers with any other marking cannot be written in the model, so no mutant can break what follows. Four quoted duties rest on that reading alone: 'An answer that reports a restore point describes the instant at which the executor captured it'; the second half of 'An answer to a request the orchestrator could not serve ...', a parked executor answers with the current marking, which is AC9's 'MUST return the current marking, not an earlier published one'; the first half of that sentence, that an answer describing an earlier instant (Java's unserved request, ruling D43 (a)) reports work in flight; and the marking side of the body's 'MUST be decided at the same instant the marking is captured'. The lines pin the flag side of that last duty: the flag is read off the state of the step, so an indication computed at another instant shows as an answer some false from a state with work in flight, which lines 4 to 6 forbid. The first two duties become lines of their own once the label carries the marking (an answer some (m, b) with m = s.M when b is false, and when the loop is parked); the glossary has no such label yet.

The three conforming shapes of the body (refuse, indicate, defer) are one abstraction. An indication is the flag of the answer. A refusal of a restore-point snapshot while work is in flight is an answer some true: the caller can tell it from a restore point, and the rejection none is reserved for a drained, closed or stopped executor (the quoted paragraph 'The answer and its two readings'). A deferral is an answer step taken later, at a state with nothing in flight. An executor that never answers some false meets the block: it never offers a restore point. The reference answers some false exactly when nothing is in flight and nothing is queued, and ENV_014_nonvacuous decides such an answer.

Work in flight (the quoted definition) is read off the state. A firing is in flight while it is in XSt.fl, from the start step that consumes its inputs to the settle step that commits or fails its completion (EXEC-001, EXEC-031), so a firing whose action returned but whose completion is not yet processed still counts (Rust decrements in_flight_count only when it processes the completion, executor_core/executor.rs 1046 and 1169). Tokens its action published mid-action (IO-015) wait in XSt.pq as flushed batches until step 1b deposits them, which can come after the settle step (EXEC-001 step 1b, executor_core/executor.rs 1043-1058). An accepted external event is queued while it is in XSt.eq, from the request step answered accepted (ENV-003) to its inject or discard step (ENV-004). The fourth quoted shall sentence keeps a firing in flight until its completion is processed and every token its action published is deposited: line 4 is the part up to the settle step, line 6 the part after it.

Line 1 is the first quoted shall sentence and the first quoted body sentence ('without affecting lifecycle', 'neither stops nor pauses execution'): the answer changes no field of the state, which is the sentence's 'its whole state': the marking, the clock reading of the host and of the cycle, the clocks of the transitions, the mode, the firings in flight, the completion, publication and event queues, the identity supply, the phase, the pass order and its same-pass counts, and the parked flag. It owns CORE-071's 'MUST NOT mutate the live marking' for a snapshot (plan section 7). An executor whose answer drains it, as a snapshot taken through drain() would, breaks it (ENV_014_forbids_drainingSnapshot), and so does one that serves a request in the wait by waking the orchestrator (ENV_014_forbids_wakingSnapshot, AC9).

Line 2 is the second quoted shall sentence and AC4: once the mode is draining (ENV-011), closed (ENV-013) or stopped (ENV-015, the immediate termination; Java's terminateNow sets closed, so snapshot() throws), the answer is none. ENV_014_nonvacuous parts 5 to 7 decide a rejection after a drain, after a close (the test derivation's 'call after close() and verify rejection') and after an immediate termination. An executor that answers a drained request with a marking breaks it (ENV_014_forbids_answersAfterDrain); Rust's executor arm has no draining test (executor_core/executor.rs 1433-1446), and Rust meets the line at its handle, which refuses once drained (executor_handle.rs 200-203): with one sender per run, a request sent before the drain is a snapshot step before the drain step, in channel order (map note, with ENV-011).

Line 3 is the third quoted shall sentence and AC1 (reworded under ruling D20, ENVB-R7 item 3, to 'while the executor is running and has been neither drained, closed nor terminated'): a running open executor answers with a marking, whatever is in flight. An executor that rejects while work is in flight, a refusal the caller cannot tell from a closed executor, breaks it (ENV_014_forbids_rejectsWhileBusy). Line 3 binds only a running loop, and so does the quoted 'reserved, while the run lasts': after a run ended on its own the runtimes differ (Java and TypeScript still answer, BitmapNetExecutor.java 2380-2381, bitmap-net-executor.ts 1599-1608; the Rust handle answers Err once the channel is gone, executor_handle.rs 204-207), and the block leaves that open.

That a snapshot step is offered at all is coverage, and no line says it. An executor with no snapshot step meets every line: line 2's 'shall reject' and line 3's 'shall not reject' are both met by never answering, and so are AC2's 'serviced within one orchestrator cycle' and AC8's 'does not park the orchestrator against itself', which rest on the same coverage. The consistency theorem excludes it: its coverage conjunct ExecCoversW5 (ConsistencyExec.lean) has the clause Env014Covers, that a live state in step 2, at entry to the update or in the wait has a snapshot step; env014_snapshot_offered proves it of the reference.

Line 4 is the fourth quoted shall sentence up to the settle step, the action half of 'Consequently a snapshot offered as a restore point ... MUST be taken at a moment when no work is in flight', AC5 and AC6. The start step that consumes a firing's inputs is the step that puts it in flight, synchronous or not, so 'from the moment its inputs are consumed' (the quoted sentence and the first half of AC8) needs no line of its own: an executor that counts a firing as in flight only once its action suspends answers some false from inside a synchronous action and breaks line 4 (ENV_014_forbids_suspendOnlyInFlight; Java's inline capture on the orchestrator thread answers true, BitmapNetExecutor.java 2427-2431). So does an executor that always reports a restore point (ENV_014_forbids_alwaysRestorePoint). AC6 is ENV_014_nonvacuous part 1: the net's only marked place feeds a transition whose action is in flight, the consumed token is in no place of the marking, and the answer is some true.

Line 5 is the fifth quoted shall sentence, the event half, the paragraph 'Two conforming shapes for the pending-event half' and AC7: an answer some false comes from a state whose event queue is empty. An executor whose indication reads the actions alone breaks it (ENV_014_forbids_actionsOnlyFlag): an event accepted while the loop waits is in neither the marking nor the flag. TypeScript and Java read the marking outside the event queue and OR the pending queue into the flag (the reference's reading). Rust and Python serve the request on the same FIFO channel as injections (executor_core/executor.rs 1433-1446): every event accepted before the request is injected before the answer, so the event queue holds no such event when the marking is captured; an event accepted after the request was sent is a request step after the snapshot step, in channel order, which is what the quoted sentence's 'accepted before a snapshot() request' allows. ENV_014_nonvacuous part 4 is AC7's test derivation: an event accepted while the loop is parked, the snapshot flagged.

Line 6 is the fourth quoted shall sentence after the settle step, with reason (1) ('those tokens are simply absent'), AC8's 'outputs deposited, no token missing' and the pending-event paragraph's 'a token the executor has accepted is never absent from a snapshot that reports itself a restore point': an answer some false comes from a state with no flushed batch waiting for step 1b. An executor that serves the request before step 1b (Rust's loop with Phase 2 moved before Phase 1b, its flag still in_flight_count or a queued event) answers some false after the settle and before the deposit, with the published token in no place, and breaks line 6 alone (ENV_014_forbids_answerBeforeDeposit). Line 6 reads runs that start with no firing in flight and no batch queued: the initial state xinit, or a restored marking. From an arbitrary state the reference itself answers some false with a batch queued (env014_needs_runStart), because its flag reads the firings and the events only; on its own runs a batch is queued only while its firing is in flight or in steps 1 and 1b, where it does not answer (env014_pubInv_step). ENV_014_nonvacuous part 8 decides a reference run whose action flushes a batch in the wait, answers some true with the batch queued and some false only once step 1b has deposited it.

AC8: a snapshot requested by a running action is a snapshot with that firing in flight (line 4), from its synchronous prefix on.
