                (∀ (p : N), s'.M p = qConsume (vis s) t p ++ hid s p) ∧
                  s'.delta = s.delta ∧
                    ∀ f ∈ s'.fl, f ∉ s.fl → f.deliv = qDelivered (vis s) t) ∧
        (∀ (n : String),
            on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.lose n) s', shall fun s s' ↦
              ∃ t rest,
                s.order = t :: rest ∧
                  t.core.name = n ∧
                    ¬((stampOf (s.st n)).isSome = true ∧
                          Novel.Seam.enabledNA (qCount (vis s)) t.core = true) ∧
                      s'.order = rest) ∧
          (∀ (n : String),
              on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.lose n) s', shall fun s s' ↦
                s'.st n = Status.off ∧ s'.M = s.M) ∧
            (on fun s s' ↦
                s.phase = Phase.pass ∧
                  ∃ l, R C s l s' ∧ ∀ (n : String) (sy : Bool), l ≠ XLbl.start n sy,
                shall fun s s' ↦ vis s' = vis s ∧ ∀ (p : N), hid s p <+: hid s' p) ∧
              (on fun s s' ↦
                  s.phase = Phase.pass ∧
                    ∃ l,
                      R C s l s' ∧
                        (∀ (n : String) (sy : Bool), l ≠ XLbl.start n sy) ∧
                          ∀ (n : String), l ≠ XLbl.lose n,
                  shall fun s s' ↦ s'.order = s.order) ∧
                (on fun s s' ↦ R C s XLbl.endPass s', shall fun s x ↦ s.order = []) ∧
                  on fun s s' ↦ R C s XLbl.begin s', shall fun s s' ↦
                    s'.M = s.M ∧ vis s' = s'.M
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C:

a start step of the name n starts the head t of the pass's order, named n, holding a clock and enabled on the pass-visible marking (input counts, read arcs and inhibitor arcs), and removes it from the order;

a start step of t leaves in every place p the pass-visible queue of p with t's consumption and drains applied, followed by the tail of p deposited inside the pass, keeps that tail hidden, and every firing it adds is handed what t takes from the pass-visible marking;
a lose step of the name n drops the head t of the pass's order, named n, only when t holds no clock or is not enabled on the pass-visible marking, and removes it from the order;
a lose step of the name n leaves n without a clock and the marking unchanged;
every step from inside a firing pass other than a start leaves the pass-visible marking unchanged and only extends the hidden tail of every place;
every step from inside a firing pass other than a start or a lose leaves the pass's order unchanged;
an end of pass step happens only when the pass's order is empty;
a begin step leaves the marking unchanged and makes all of it pass-visible.
quotes: When multiple transitions compete for the same input tokens, the highest-priority ready transition fires first and consumes the tokens.
Lower-priority transitions become disabled if their inputs are no longer satisfied.
A firing pass takes the transitions of its ready order ([EXEC-002]) one at a time from the front: it starts the next transition, or it drops it and goes on with the rest.

The pass-visible marking is the marking a firing pass began with, minus the tokens earlier firings of the same pass consumed or drained; tokens a synchronous action deposited during the pass are not part of it.
*When* a firing pass starts or drops a transition, the transition *shall* be the next one of the pass's ready order, and it *shall* leave that order.
*When* a firing pass starts a transition, the transition *shall* hold a clock and be enabled on the pass-visible marking, with input counts, read arcs and inhibitor arcs all judged on that marking.
*If* the next transition of a firing pass's ready order holds a clock and is enabled on the pass-visible marking, *then* the executor *shall not* drop it.
*When* a firing pass drops a transition, the transition *shall* lose its clock ([TIME-012]), and the marking *shall* stay unchanged.
*While* a firing pass is under way, its ready order *shall* change only when the pass starts or drops a transition.

*When* a firing pass ends, its ready order *shall* be empty, so a transition of the order that does not hold a clock or is not enabled on the pass-visible marking when it is next is dropped, loses its clock and does not start in that pass.

*When* a transition starts in a firing pass, it *shall* consume, drain and hand its action only tokens of the pass-visible marking, so a token a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same pass survives its `all()`, `atLeast(n)` and reset arcs and does not reach its action.

*While* a firing pass is under way, the executor *shall* change the pass-visible marking only by starting a transition, and *shall* keep every token deposited earlier in the pass, so a token a synchronous action deposits in the pass does not become part of the pass-visible marking.
*When* a firing pass begins, the executor *shall* keep the marking, and every token of the marking *shall* be part of the pass-visible marking of the new pass.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean). The pass-visible marking is the derived term vis s: each queue of s.M without its last s.delta p tokens, the tokens deposited inside the current pass (hid s). It is the model's form of the definition sentence, read inductively: lines 2 and 5 say how vis changes inside a pass, and line 8 where it starts. The sentence before it ('takes the transitions of its ready order one at a time from the front') is lines 1, 3, 6 and 7 together. 'Drops' is the lose step, 'the next one of the ready order' the head of s.order, and 'holds a clock' is stampOf (s.st n) being some stamp, whatever the restart flag (the glossary's 'armed' adds 'enabled', which the sentences state separately, on the pass-visible marking).

The headline sentence ('the highest-priority ready transition fires first and consumes the tokens') is lines 1, 3, 6 and 7 together with the order the pass begins with: the pass takes its transitions head first, each start or lose takes the head and removes it, nothing else changes the order, and the pass does not end before the order is empty, so the first transition of the order that is still enabled on the pass-visible marking consumes the tokens. Which order the begin step sets (the ready order of EXEC-002 at the cycle reading) is TIME-014's first line and EXEC-002's companion line, not restated here, so this block takes no side in ruling D14 (the all-immediate fast path). The second quoted sentence ('become disabled') is lines 3 and 4: the loser leaves the order and its clock is gone (ruled: it loses its clock, TIME-012's sentence on the recheck); a later enablement update arms it again if it is enabled (TIME-010, CONC-005 companion).

EARS mapping. 'Starts or drops ... the next one ... leave that order' is lines 1 and 3 (head, name, removal). 'Hold a clock and be enabled on the pass-visible marking' is line 1. 'Shall not drop it' is line 3. 'Lose its clock ... marking stay unchanged' is line 4. 'Its ready order shall change only when the pass starts or drops' is line 6. 'When a firing pass ends, its ready order shall be empty' is line 7; its 'so' clause follows from lines 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7: every entry leaves the order by a start or a lose before the pass ends, line 1 forbids starting one without a clock or not enabled on the pass-visible marking, so it leaves by a lose and line 4 takes its clock, and line 6 keeps it from coming back into the order of that pass (names are pairwise distinct, ruling D10). 'Consume, drain and hand its action only tokens of the pass-visible marking' is line 2. 'Change the pass-visible marking only by starting a transition, and keep every token deposited earlier in the pass' is line 5 for every step but a start, and line 2's last two conjuncts (the tail follows the consumed queue, delta unchanged) for a start. 'When a firing pass begins ... keep the marking ... part of the pass-visible marking' is line 8.

Line 2 fixes the exact marking after a start: the FIFO prefix of every input queue is consumed ([EXEC-010]), reset places and all() or atLeast(n) inputs are drained to the end of the pass-visible queue ([EXEC-013], [IO-003], [IO-004]), read arcs peek at the pass-visible queue ([EXEC-012]), and a start deposits nothing ([CONC-002]). Those are the cited requirements' rules applied to the pass-visible queue (qConsume and qDelivered of Reference/Queue.lean); what this block adds is the queue they apply to, as AC5 says. That a start adds exactly one firing is EXEC-001's and CONC-002's; line 2 only says what any firing it adds is handed.

Line 1 kills an executor that re-checks on the live marking (EXEC_003_mutant_liveRecheck_killed, the XPol field recheckOn) and one that starts any ready transition of the order rather than its head (EXEC_003_forbids_anyOrder). Line 2 kills an executor that consumes and drains the live marking (EXEC_003_forbids_drainSwallows) and one that removes the right tokens but hands the action the live queue, deposit included (EXEC_003_forbids_liveDeliver). Line 3 kills an executor that tests inhibitor arcs on the live marking (EXEC_003_forbids_liveInhibitor, ruling D75 (b)); the inhibitor test is part of the enablement test lines 1 and 3 share, and this mutant breaks it by a wrongful lose. Line 4 kills an executor whose loser keeps its clock (EXEC_003_forbids_loserKeepsClock). Line 5 kills an executor whose in-pass deposit is visible to the rest of the pass (EXEC_003_forbids_visibleDeposit) and one whose end of pass cuts every queue back to its pass-visible prefix, losing the same-pass deposits (EXEC_003_forbids_tailCut). Line 6 kills an executor whose in-pass settle prunes from the order the entries no longer enabled, so they never lose their clock (EXEC_003_forbids_pruneOrder). Line 7 kills an executor that ends the pass with entries still in the order (EXEC_003_forbids_earlyEnd). Line 8 kills an executor whose begin cuts the marking to the pass-visible one of the previous pass (EXEC_003_forbids_beginCut) and one that keeps the hidden tail into the next pass (EXEC_003_forbids_staleDelta).

The lines are safety lines over the steps an executor takes: none obliges a step to happen. That the loop reaches the pass and that a pass under way takes its next step is EXEC-001's; TIME-014 states the same progress over a whole pass (the starts and loses of a pass name its ready order, all of it once the pass ends), of which lines 6 and 7 are the step form. A pass that a terminal place stops (EXEC-042) has no end of pass step, and line 7 says nothing of it. Steps outside a pass (step 1 settles, injections, publications) do not drop tokens by EXEC-001's frame, not this block's, so the tail line 5 keeps to the end of the pass and line 8 makes visible is the same tail when no outside step intervenes, as in every example here.

Ruling D75 (a): inside a firing pass an inhibitor arc reads the pass-visible marking, as the input counts and the drains do (Rust recheck_can_fire on the pass snapshot, bitmap_backend.rs 708-713, inhibitors tested on that snapshot, compiled_net.rs 355-361; Java canEnable(tid, fireScanBitmap, true)). CORE-022 and CORE-031 say that a transition shall not fire while an inhibitor place is marked; their blocks are stated over the one-step firing of a marking, and AC4's added sentence says that inside a firing pass the marking a transition fires from in that sense is the pass-visible marking. The assumes line in CORE-022 and CORE-031 that says so, and the bridge from a reference start to those blocks, belong to the integrator; EXEC_003_start_inhibitors states the start half here.

AC1 (T1 priority 10, T2 priority 5, one token, T1 fires, T2 disabled) and the test derivation are EXEC_003_nonvacuous's first part: T1 heads the order and starts, T2 loses and has no clock. The decided runs take the all-immediate single-priority path, where the order is the declaration order, because the kernel does not evaluate the general path's merge sort on two or more ready transitions; with priorities 10 and 5 EXEC-002 forces the same order, and the block reads only the head. The priority half of AC1 is therefore EXEC-002's and TIME-014's, not exercised here.

AC2 (T1 not ready, T2 may fire) is EXEC_003_allows_notReady: with T1 Delayed(10) and armed but below its earliest bound, the order of the pass holds T2 only, and T2 starts and takes the token T1 is waiting for. That a transition that is not ready is not in the order is TIME-014's first line.

AC3 is lines 1, 3 and 5: T1 consumes P's token, its synchronous action refills P inside the pass (the in-pass commit step of EXEC-021), the refill stays outside the pass-visible marking (line 5, third part), and T2, judged on it, loses (EXEC_003_nonvacuous, second part). 'May fire no earlier than the next cycle' is line 3's removal from the order with line 6 (it does not come back in that pass), line 5 (the refill stays in the marking to the end of the pass, seventh part) and line 8 (the next pass begins with the refill pass-visible, sixth part, where T2 is in the order again). The wording fix of ruling D20 (the reason is the recheck, not 'outputs deposit in step 1') is in the markdown.

AC4 is line 1 for counts: enablement on the pass-visible marking compares every input arc's required count, exactly(n) and atLeast(n) included, with the pass-visible count. 'Visible at the next cycle' is line 8. The inhibitor sentence added under D75 (a) is line 1 for inhibitor arcs (EXEC_003_nonvacuous, fifth part: T4 starts while its inhibitor place holds a same-pass deposit). Its ν part (a correlated join whose correlated input place received a same-pass deposit fires no earlier than the next cycle) is not stated here: the start of RefExec takes no match specification. It is a follow-up line of this block, to be added when RefExec's start takes the ν firing of RefNu (W9, NU-020's correlated take), recorded with the integrator.

AC5 is line 2: a reset arc (and an all() or atLeast(n) input) applied to the pass-visible queue takes its prefix, and the same-pass tail follows it unchanged (EXEC_003_nonvacuous, fourth part: the reset of T3 takes the old token 3 and leaves the deposited 8); what reaches the action is taken from the pass-visible queue too (EXEC_003_forbids_liveDeliver). Rust drainable (precompiled_backend.rs 690-695), Java drainable() (PrecompiledNetExecutor.java 791).

The closing paragraph ('as if every firing in it started before any of them deposited') is the observational form of lines 2 and 5: moving each in-pass settle behind the last start of its pass keeps every start's pass-visible marking equal to the live marking of the moved run. It is link L5 of Reference/ExecLink.lean (ExecLink.hoist_vis), proved there, and it is not a line here. Its second sentence (verification reads such a firing as two steps) is VER-004's.

TypeScript settles every firing in step 1 (bitmap-net-executor.ts processCompletedTransitions), so no deposit happens inside its passes: its runs are runs of RefExec without an in-pass commit step, and the lines hold of them with an empty hidden tail.

Which transitions keep their clocks across a start (the restart flag on the live intermediate marking, ruling D7) is TIME-012's companion line, and re-entrancy (ruling D8 (b)) is CONC-002's; neither is stated here. Transition names are pairwise distinct (ruling D10, Cfg.WF), so the name a start or lose step carries names one transition and leaves the order with it.

requirements.title: FIFO Token Consumption
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] Q ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
      ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,
        ¬ResetArc t p →
          on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦
            List.drop (Consumes t (Counts M) p) (M p) <+: M' p ∧
              (M' p).Perm (List.drop (Consumes t (Counts M) p) (M p) ++ EmittedTo e p)) ∧
    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
        ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,
          on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M x ↦
            δ.inputs p = OldestFirst M p (Consumes t (Counts M) p)) ∧
      ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
        ∀ p ∉ inPlaces t, on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun x x_1 ↦ δ.inputs p = []
reading: For every queue firing relation Q:

for every firing of a transition t and every input place p of t that is not a reset place of t: the queue p holds after the firing begins with the tokens of p's queue before the firing after its oldest Consumes tokens, in their queue order, and it holds exactly those tokens and the tokens the action emits to p, in some order;
for every firing of a transition t and every input place p of t: the tokens delivered to the action from p are the oldest Consumes tokens of p's queue before the firing, in queue order;
for every firing of a transition t and every place p that is not an input place of t: no consumed token is delivered to the action from p.
quotes: When a transition fires, it consumes tokens from the oldest-first (FIFO) end of each input place's queue.
The number of tokens consumed is determined by the input cardinality's `consumptionCount(available)`.

*When* a transition fires, it *shall* consume from each of its input places that is not a correlated input of its match specification ([NU-020]) the oldest tokens the place holds, as many as the consumption count of the input arc.
*When* a transition fires, its action *shall* receive the tokens consumed from each input place that is not a correlated input of its match specification in queue order, the oldest first.
*When* a transition fires, its action *shall* receive consumed tokens only from the input places of the transition.

A correlated input of a ν-net match specification is the one exception to oldest-first consumption: it takes the matched tokens of the chosen name, oldest first among the tokens of that name, so it can pass over an older token of another name ([NU-020]).
Its non-correlated inputs consume as above.
assumes: A firing relates a queue marking before it to the queue marking after it, with what it delivered to the action and the emissions of the action (glossary: Queue order, QueueMarking, Delivered, QFireRel). Consumes t (Counts M) p is the consumption count of t's input arc on p at the token counts of M (glossary: Consumption count, Consume), so 'as many as the consumption count of the input arc' is the length of the prefix both lines name, and the paragraph 'The number of tokens consumed is determined by the input cardinality's consumptionCount(available)' is the same count.

Correlated inputs (ruling D16): the transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no ν-net match specification, so every input place is an input that is not a correlated input of a match specification, and the lines quantify over every input place. The exception paragraph is therefore not a line of the formula: how a correlated input consumes (the matched tokens of the chosen name, oldest first among them) is NU-020's, not encoded here; this block makes no claim about a correlated input, and a mutant that consumed a correlated input oldest first would not be killed by it.

Line 1 is the first 'shall' sentence. It is stated at every input place that is not a reset place, including a place the action also emits to (a self-loop): the place keeps its tokens after the oldest Consumes ones, in queue order and ahead of every token emitted to it, and gains exactly the tokens emitted to it, so the tokens that left it are the oldest. Keeping the kept tokens ahead (a prefix, not only a subsequence) is what makes the consumed tokens the oldest when token values repeat: a place holding 10, 11, 10 whose action emits 10 back would otherwise pass with 10, 11, 10, the newest 10 consumed, which no count or value check can tell from the oldest 10 consumed and the emission put at the head (killed by EXEC_010_mutant_sublist_killed). That the emitted tokens follow the kept ones agrees with EXEC-020's tail append; the order among the emitted tokens is EXEC-020's, so line 1 fixes them only up to order. A reset place is left to line 2: it ends the firing holding exactly what was deposited there (CORE-034). With nothing emitted to the place, line 1 says the queue before the firing is its oldest Consumes tokens followed by the queue after it (exec010_line1_noEmission). The line is exercised by EXEC_010_nonvacuous; a relation that removes the newest tokens from a self-loop place is killed by EXEC_010_forbids_selfLoopNewest.

Line 2 is the second 'shall' sentence: the action receives, from each input place, the consumed tokens in queue order, the oldest first (OldestFirst, the FIFO prefix). On an input place that is also a reset place line 2 is the only line: the consumed prefix is still the oldest, the rest is drained. Line 3 is the third shall sentence, the counterpart of line 2 at every other place: the action receives no consumed token from a place that is not an input place, a read, reset, inhibitor or output place included. CORE-063 cites it for its sentence that an executor hands an action consumed tokens only from the input places of its transition, and CORE-061's delivery by arcs follows from it with EXEC-012's line 7 (core061_byArcs_of). All runtimes meet it: Rust's consume_for_firing walks the transition's input specs only and keys the consumed tokens by input place (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/bitmap_backend.rs and precompiled_backend.rs), Java and TypeScript fill the consumed tokens from inputSpecs only in fireTransition (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java, typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts, and the precompiled executors' input opcodes), and drained reset tokens never reach the action. Java and TypeScript keep the consumed and the read tokens in one store (rawInput) and separate them by the context's input gate (CORE-060); an executor that hands the read tokens over as consumed ones too breaks line 3 (EXEC_010_forbids_mergedInputs).

The firing is the atomic firing of the reference: the counts the consumption count reads are the counts at the start of the firing. Same-pass deposits (EXEC-003 AC5: a draining arc ships the pass-start count, not the live one) need the cycle relation of Phase 2 (RefExec) and are deferred to it; consume_faithful (Conservation.lean) states the same FIFO prefix for one firing on the compiled consume program, under the module's assumption that no same-pass deposit is outstanding.
A transition with two input arcs on one place is rejected when it is built (CORE-030); the model reads the first arc (nspecAt), as Consumes does.

AC1 (tokens A, B, C added in that order; One consumes A), AC2 (Exactly(2) consumes A, B) and AC3 (All consumes A, B, C) are EXEC_010_nonvacuous, with tokens 10, 11, 12 for A, B, C: the reference delivers [10], [10, 11] and [10, 11, 12] and leaves [11, 12], [12] and [].
The test derivation (identifiable token values, fire, check the consumed tokens are in FIFO order) is the same check as AC1 to AC3.

requirements.title: FIFO Token Consumption (executor companion)
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T) (n : String) (sy : Bool),
    (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.start n sy) s', shall fun s s' ↦
        ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (rest : List (Reference.Trans N)),
          s.order = t :: rest →
            t.core.name = n →
              ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,
                ¬ResetArc t p →
                  s'.M p = List.drop (Consumes t (Counts (vis s)) p) (s.M p)) ∧
      on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.start n sy) s', shall fun s s' ↦
        ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (rest : List (Reference.Trans N)),
          s.order = t :: rest →
            t.core.name = n →
              ∀ f ∈ s'.fl,
                f ∉ s.fl →
                  ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,
                    f.deliv.inputs p = OldestFirst s.M p (Consumes t (Counts (vis s)) p)
reading: For every executor R, every configuration C and every start step of a name n in R, from state s to state s', if the head of the pass's order in s is a transition t named n (the transition the step starts), then:

every input place p of t that is not a reset place of t holds in s' the queue it held in s without its oldest k tokens, where k is the consumption count of t's input arc on p at the pass-visible counts of s (Consumes t (Counts (vis s)) p);
every firing in flight in s' that was not in flight in s is handed, from every input place p of t, the oldest k tokens of p's queue in s, in queue order, for the same k.
quotes: When a transition fires, it consumes tokens from the oldest-first (FIFO) end of each input place's queue.

*When* a transition starts in a firing pass, it *shall* remove from each of its input places that is neither a reset place nor a correlated input of its match specification the oldest tokens the place holds, as many as the consumption count of the input arc counted on the pass-visible marking ([EXEC-003]).

*When* a transition starts in a firing pass, its action *shall* receive from each of its input places that is not a correlated input of its match specification the oldest tokens the place holds, as many as that consumption count, in queue order.
assumes: This is the second block of EXEC-010 (ruling D33 (a), design NR-1). The first block, EXEC_010 (EXEC_010.lean), states FIFO consumption over the atomic queue firing and is unchanged; it deferred same-pass deposits to the executor model: 'Same-pass deposits (EXEC-003 AC5: a draining arc ships the pass-start count, not the live one) need the cycle relation of Phase 2 (RefExec) and are deferred to it'. This block is that executor line.

The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean). 'Fires' is read as 'starts in a firing pass': the start step consumes and hands the action its tokens, and the action runs after it. The started transition is named, not constrained: both lines read 'if the head of the pass's order is t and t is named n', so a start of a transition other than the head is left to EXEC-003's first line (a start takes the head of the order, named n) and TIME-014, which forbid it. Both lines read every start step, while the sentences speak of a start in a firing pass; that a start happens only in a pass is EXEC-001's (step 5 is the firing pass) and EXEC-003's (a start takes the head of the pass's order), so the two readings agree on the runs those blocks allow, and the lines are stronger elsewhere. The pass-visible marking is the derived term vis s (EXEC-003): each queue without the tokens deposited inside the current pass, which sit at its tail (EXEC-020). vis and hid are read off the executor's own record of the same-pass deposits; that the record holds exactly the tokens deposited earlier in the pass is EXEC-003's lines 2, 5 and 8, so the lines mean 'the tokens a synchronous action deposited earlier in the pass' only jointly with EXEC-003.

Both lines are consequences of EXEC-003's first two lines, restated per place under ruling D33 (a): EXEC-003's second line fixes the marking after a start to the pass-visible marking with t's consumption applied, followed by the same-pass tail, and the delivery to the pass-visible prefix, and its first line makes t enabled on the pass-visible marking, so the consumption count is at most the pass-visible length. The reference proof (EXEC_010_cycle_reference, exec010c_drop_take and exec010c_take_take) is that derivation. The new sentences repeat EXEC-003's 'consume, drain and hand its action only tokens of the pass-visible marking' at the grain of EXEC-010's oldest-first rule and add no constraint beyond it.

Line 1 is the first new shall sentence, and the first quoted sentence at the grain of a pass: the start removes the oldest tokens of the whole queue, so a token deposited earlier in the same pass, which sits at the tail, is not consumed. The count is taken on the pass-visible marking (EXEC-003 AC4 and AC5), so an all() or atLeast(n) input takes the pass-visible tokens only: a start that counts the live marking swallows the deposit (EXEC_010_cycle_forbids_drainSwallows), and one that takes the newest pass-visible tokens breaks the oldest-first rule (EXEC_010_cycle_forbids_newest). A reset place is left to EXEC-013's companion: an input place that is also a reset place keeps only its same-pass tail.

Line 2 is the second new shall sentence: what the action receives from each input place is that oldest prefix, in queue order. An executor that removes the right tokens and hands them to the action newest first breaks it (EXEC_010_cycle_forbids_reversedDelivery). Read arcs are EXEC-012's and EXEC-003's line 2 (the delivery is taken on the pass-visible marking). Line 2 holds of a start that puts no new firing in flight, which hands nothing; that a start puts exactly one new firing in flight is CONC-002's second line (the firings in flight after a start are a permutation of the new firing and those before it), not restated.

Correlated inputs (ruling D16): the reference start takes no ν-net match specification (Trans has no match-specification field), so every input place is an input that is not a correlated input, as in the first block, and both lines read every input place. The sentences' exemption 'that is not a correlated input of its match specification' therefore has no counterpart here: on the nets this model holds the lines say what the sentences say, and the exemption itself, with the correlated take, is NU-020's (W9), not encoded.

AC1 to AC3 (One, Exactly(2) and All on tokens A, B, C) are the first block's examples. At the grain of a pass EXEC_010_cycle_nonvacuous shows an all() input that takes the pass-visible token 3 and leaves the same-pass deposit 8, and an exactly(2) input that takes 10 and 11 of 10, 11, 12, hands the action 10 then 11 and leaves 12. The test derivation is the first block's.

requirements.title: Read Arc Peek
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] Build Q ↦
  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
      NoInputRead t →
        ReadArc t p →
          on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M x ↦
            (δ.reads p).head? = Head M p ∧
              (∀ y ∈ δ.reads p, Head M p = some y) ∧
                (List.count p t.core.reads = 1 → (δ.reads p).length ≤ 1)) ∧
    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
        NoInputRead t →
          ReadArc t p →
            ¬ResetArc t p →
              on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦ AppendedAtTail M M' e p) ∧
      ((∀ (t : Reference.Trans N), ¬NoInputRead t → Build t ≠ none) ∧
          (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
              InputsDistinct t →
                InputCountsPositive t →
                  firstInputRead t = some p → Build t = some (msgInputRead t p)) ∧
            (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
                ¬InputsDistinct t ∨ ¬InputCountsPositive t →
                  Build t ≠ some (msgInputRead t p)) ∧
              ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
                NoInputRead t → Build t ≠ some (msgInputRead t p)) ∧
        ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
          ¬ReadArc t p → on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun x x_1 ↦ δ.reads p = []
reading: Let Build be the builder (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg) and Q the queue firings.

For every transition t with no input arc and read arc on one place, every read place p of t, every delivery δ and every emission e, every firing of t from the queue marking M that delivers δ and emits e delivers at p the head of p's queue in M: the first token delivered at p is the head of M at p, every token delivered at p is that head, and when t has one read arc on p at most one token is delivered there;

for every such t, every read place p of t that is not a reset place of t, every δ and every e, every firing of t from M to M' that delivers δ and emits e leaves at p the queue M held at p, identity and order, followed by the tokens e emits to p in emission order (AppendedAtTail);
every transition with an input arc and a read arc on one place fails to build;

every transition whose input places are distinct and whose input arcs each require at least one token, and whose first read arc on an input place, in declaration order, is on p, fails to build with the message msgInputRead t p;
no transition whose input places are not distinct, or one of whose input arcs requires fewer than one token, fails to build with this message, for any place;
no transition with no input arc and read arc on one place fails to build with this message, for any place;
for every transition t, every place p that is not a read place of t, every δ and every e, no firing of t that delivers δ and emits e delivers a read token at p.
quotes: When a transition fires, read arc values are provided to the action without consuming the tokens.
The oldest token in the read place is peeked.
*When* a transition fires, its action *shall* receive, for each of its read places, the oldest token the place holds.
*When* a transition fires, its action *shall* receive read tokens only from the read places of the transition.

*When* a transition fires, each of its read places that is not one of its reset places *shall* end the firing holding the tokens it held before the firing, in the same queue order, followed by the tokens the firing deposits there.
*If* a transition declares an input arc and a read arc on the same place, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with
The message is the same, byte for byte, in every implementation.
"The same place" is the implementation's own `Place` equality, as for [CORE-030] ([CORE-002]; name-and-type in Java, name-only in TypeScript and Rust).
It runs after every input-arc check ([CORE-030], [IO-002], [IO-004]) and before the timing check ([TIME-001]) and the output-spec checks ([IO-011]–[IO-014]).
It walks the read arcs in declaration order and names the place of the first read arc whose place is an input place of the transition.
assumes: The model is the pair (Build, Q). Build is the transition builder, read as the message building a transition fails with, none when it builds; the witness is the reference builder refBuild (glossary: Build-time checks), which runs the [IO-002]/[IO-004] count checks (stand-in message msgCount) and the D15 check after its CORE-030 check and before its output-spec checks; it is the builder of the CORE and IO blocks too. Q is a queue firing relation (glossary: Queue order; QFireRel in GlossaryQueue.lean): a firing of t from the queue marking M, the head of each queue the oldest token, that delivers δ (the consumed input tokens and the read tokens, per place) to the action, whose action emits e (places and tokens, in emission order), and that leaves M'. The witness is the reference queue firing RefQFire. Timing and priority play no part.

Ruling D17: a Q step is a firing whose completion the executor admits and whose produced tokens pass output validation ([EXEC-020], [EXEC-021]), so e is what the firing deposits. A firing whose completion is not admitted (its timeout outcome [EXEC-022], a stop on a terminal place [EXEC-042], an immediate termination [ENV-015]) or whose output validation fails ([EXEC-021], TransitionFailed) is not a Q step, and line 2 says nothing about it; what such a firing leaves in its read places (the queue, plus the tokens [IO-015] already published) is [EXEC-020]'s and [EXEC-021]'s. The witness RefQFire has only admitted, validated firings (deposit ... = some (e.map fst)).

Firings are atomic: line 2 is the firing's own effect on p, with no other firing consuming from p or depositing to p between the firing's start and its completion. In the runtimes an action can be in flight while other firings consume from a shared read place or deposit to it first ([EXEC-003]; ruling D7, live intermediate marking), so the second shall sentence read of the whole interval does not hold of them; which of the two the sentence means is not ruled and is not encoded.

Ruling D15: the third shall sentence is lines 3 to 6. The firing lines (1 and 2) speak only of transitions with no input arc and read arc on one place (NoInputRead), because line 3 rejects every other transition when it is built, so no executor holds one. On those transitions the queue of a read place after input consumption is its queue before the firing (exec012_head_postInput), so the read sees the head 'after input consumption' ([EXEC-013] AC4) and 'the oldest token the place holds' at once; and draining a reset place comes after the peek, so a read and a reset on one place deliver the pre-drain head (line 1 reads M, before the drain; [EXEC-013]).

Line 1 reads 'receive, for each of its read places, the oldest token the place holds' as: every token the firing delivers at the read place is the head of its queue, the first is the head, and a single read arc on p delivers at most one token there, so a marked p with one read arc delivers exactly its head (a firing that hands the head over twice is killed as EXEC_012_mutant_noCount). How many copies a transition that declares two read arcs on one place gets is not fixed by the sentence, so for it the line constrains only which token they are. That a firing needs its read places marked is [CORE-032]'s and [CORE-022]'s; on an unmarked read place line 1 forbids a delivered token (its head is none).

Line 2 is the second shall sentence and 'without consuming the tokens': the read place keeps its queue, identity and order, and the firing's deposits there follow at the tail ([EXEC-020]). A read place that is also a reset place is drained ([EXEC-013], [CORE-034]) and is excluded, as the sentence says. Keeping only the count (a firing that reorders the read place) is killed as EXEC_012_mutant_countOnly, and a read that consumes the head as EXEC_012_mutant_readConsumes.

Line 7 is the third shall sentence, the counterpart of line 1 at every other place: the action receives no read token from a place that is not a read place of the transition, an input, reset, inhibitor or output place included. CORE-063 cites it for its sentence that an executor hands an action read tokens only from the read places of its transition, and with EXEC-010's line 3 it gives CORE-061's delivery by arcs (core061_byArcs_of). All runtimes meet it: Rust collects the read tokens from the transition's read arcs only, into a map of its own (consume_for_firing, rust/libpetri-runtime/src/bitmap_backend.rs, and peek_reads over the read opcodes in precompiled_backend.rs); Java and TypeScript peek the head of each read arc's place in fireTransition (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java, typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts, and the read opcodes of the precompiled executors); the Python binding copies only the read places Rust delivered (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs). An executor that hands the consumed tokens over as read tokens too breaks line 7 (EXEC_012_forbids_mergedReads).

Lines 4 to 6 are the check order and the named place. The message is msgInputRead, the fenced message with the transition's name and

the place; exec012_msg pins the template byte for byte, and how an implementation renders and

follows its sibling build messages (ruling D15: Java may differ only there). Line 4 names the first read arc, in declaration order, whose place is an input place (firstInputRead), when the input-arc checks that run before it pass: distinct input places ([CORE-030], InputsDistinct) and input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002] AC1, [IO-004] AC1; InputCountsPositive). Line 5 is 'after every input-arc check': a transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, not this one (two input arcs on one place: the [CORE-030] stand-in, EXEC_012_forbids_early; an exactly(0) input arc: the count stand-in, EXEC_012_forbids_beforeCounts). Line 6 says the message names only an input-and-read pair: a builder that also rejects a read and a reset on one place with it is forbidden as EXEC_012_forbids_readReset.

'Before the output-spec checks' is encoded by line 4, which asks for this message whatever the output spec, so a transition that also breaks an output-spec check fails with this message (EXEC_012_before_output). 'Before the timing check ([TIME-001])' is quoted but not encoded: the transition of this model carries no timing (timing is TimedNet's, and TIME-001's builder is a separate contract over timings), so this builder never runs that check, and nothing here tells the order against it apart.

'The same place' is equality on N, read as the implementation's own Place identity ([CORE-002]): N is abstract with decidable equality (the place name in TypeScript and Rust, name and type in Java), and ToString N renders the place's name in the message. 'On every construction path' (channel merge [MOD-021], instantiation [MOD-020], fusion [MOD-061]) is not encoded: Build reads one transition definition, and the construction paths that reach it are the composition model's.

AC1 (read place has tokens A, B; the action receives A; both A and B remain after firing) is EXEC_012_nonvacuous: a reference firing with one input arc on place 0 and one read arc on place 1, which holds 20 then 21, delivers 20 at 1 and leaves 20, 21 there, followed by the token 30 the action emits to 1.
AC2 (a one() input arc and a read arc on one place is rejected with the message, and so are all(), exactly(2) and atLeast(1)) is EXEC_012_ac2, under the reference builder.

AC3 (inputs on a and b with reads declared b then a names b; two input arcs on p and a read on p give the CORE-030 message) is EXEC_012_ac3; the CORE-030 message is the reference builder's stand-in, which line 5 keeps apart from this message.

AC4 (an input on a and a read on b builds; a read and a reset on one place builds) is EXEC_012_ac4 for the witness. The statement asks of AC4's transitions only that they do not fail with this message (line 6); that they build at all is the build-time checks' (glossary: Builds), not this requirement's.

Without ruling D15 a read on an input place could be read as a peek before consumption. That reading (a builder with no D15 check and a firing that reads the pre-firing head on every transition) is EXEC_012_mutant_preFixReads. It is killed by the build line alone: on transitions with no input arc and read arc on one place its pre-consumption peek and RefQFire agree, as D15 intends. The reference builder without the check (exec012_buildNoCheck, refBuild as it was before ruling D15) is forbidden as EXEC_012_forbids_noCheck.

requirements.title: Reset Arc Execution
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] Q ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
    NoInputRead t →
      (∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
          on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun x M' ↦
            ∀ (p : N), ResetArc t p → M' p = EmittedTo e p) ∧
        (∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
            on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M x ↦
              ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,
                ResetArc t p →
                  (δ.inputs p).length = Consumes t (Counts M) p ∧
                    (δ.inputs p).Sublist (M p)) ∧
          (∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),
              on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M x ↦
                ∀ (p : N),
                  ReadArc t p →
                    ResetArc t p →
                      δ.reads p ≠ [] ∧ ∀ tok ∈ δ.reads p, Head M p = some tok) ∧
            ∀ (M : QueueMarking N T) (e : List (N × T)),
              (∃ p, ResetArc t p ∧ M p = []) →
                Enabled t (Counts M) →
                  (∃ ch,
                      deposit (Consumes t (Counts M)) (OutputSpec t) ch =
                        some (List.map Prod.fst e)) →
                    ∃ δ M', Q t M δ e M'
reading: For every transition t with no input arc and read arc on one place (ruling D15):
every firing of t that emits e leaves each reset place of t holding exactly the tokens e sends there, in emission order;

every firing of t from M that delivers δ hands the action, from each input place of t that is also a reset place, as many tokens as the input arc consumes, taken from the place's queue in M and kept in queue order;

every firing of t from M that delivers δ hands the action, for each place that is both a read place and a reset place of t, a nonempty read bag whose every token is the head of the place's queue in M;
from every queue marking M at which t is enabled and one of its reset places is unmarked, every emission e whose places are a deposit t offers is the emission of some firing of t from M.
quotes: When a transition fires, all tokens are removed from each reset place.
This happens during the firing step, before the action executes.
*When* a transition fires, it *shall* drain each of its reset places ([CORE-034]) before its action starts.
*When* a transition fires, it *shall* consume from its input places first, then peek its read places, then drain its reset places.
*When* a transition with a read arc and a reset arc on the same place fires, its action *shall* receive as the read token the oldest token the place held before the drain.
*If* a reset place of a firing transition is unmarked, *then* the drain *shall* remove nothing and the firing *shall* proceed.
assumes: A firing is one step Q t M δ e M' (glossary: QFireRel): t fires from the queue marking M, delivers δ to its action (the consumed tokens per input place and the read tokens per read place), the action emits e (places and tokens, in emission order) and the firing leaves M'. Queue order, Head, Emitted to and Appended at the tail are the glossary terms of GlossaryQueue.lean. Timing, priority and events play no part. Correlated ν inputs are not modelled (NU-020); ruling D16 excludes them from EXEC-010's oldest-first consumption, and line 2 does not say which tokens an input consumes, only that they are taken from the queue before the drain, so it makes no claim that D16 would contradict.

e is the emission of a completion the executor admitted and output validation accepted ([EXEC-020], [EXEC-021], ruling D17); a discarded, timed-out, stopped or failed completion is not a step of Q. Tokens an action published before it completed ([IO-015]) are not modelled: they land after the drain and survive it, also when the completion then fails validation (ruling D17). Both are Phase 2 (RefExec).

Every line is stated for transitions satisfying NoInputRead (ruling D15): a transition with an input arc and a read arc on one place is rejected when it is built (EXEC-012) and never fires. Under D15 no place is both an input place and a read place, so the 'input consumption, then read peeks' half of the fourth quoted sentence is not observable in a single firing: a read place is untouched by input consumption, and the read sees its pre-firing head whichever comes first. That half is therefore not a line; the halves 'input consumption, then reset draining' and 'read peeks, then reset draining' are lines 2 and 3.

Line 1 is the first quoted sentence and the single-firing consequence of the second and third: the drain comes before the action's outputs land, so every token the action emits to a reset place survives it, and the place ends with exactly those tokens, in emission order. A drain after the action's outputs would leave the place empty (exec013_outputsFirst violates it). The other half of 'before its action starts', that the drained marking is the intermediate marking other transitions see while the action runs (the unquoted body sentence 'Like input consumption, the drain lands in the intermediate marking, so it restarts the clocks of transitions it disables there'), is TIME-012's and the Phase 2 executor model's (RefExec), not a line here. On token counts line 1 is CORE-034's first line.

Line 2 is the fourth quoted sentence's 'input consumption, then reset draining': an input place that is also a reset place hands the action as many tokens as the input arc's consumption count (IO-007) on the pre-firing counts, taken from its pre-firing queue in queue order; a drain first would hand it nothing (exec013_drainFirst violates it). Which tokens they are (the oldest, except for a correlated ν input) is EXEC-010's subject; the queue an input place that is not a reset place keeps, and the tail append of the emitted tokens, are EXEC-010's and EXEC-020's. What is delivered from a place that is not an input place (for instance the drained tokens of a reset place that is not an input place) is not constrained by this block, nor by any other requirement block: the spec has no shall sentence on it, so that the action receives nothing from such a place is not encoded.

Line 3 is the fifth quoted sentence, which is the 'read peeks, then reset draining' half of the fourth: the read token of a place that is both a read place and a reset place is the head of its queue before the drain. The read bag is nonempty and every token in it is that head; how many copies a transition with several read arcs on one place receives is CORE-032's and EXEC-012's subject and is not fixed here.

Line 4 is the sixth quoted sentence's 'the firing shall proceed': an unmarked reset place blocks no firing, so every firing the counts allow (enabled, an offered deposit, glossary Enabled, Consumes and OutputSpec) is a firing of Q. Its 'the drain shall remove nothing' is line 1 at an unmarked reset place: the place ends with exactly the emitted tokens, which is the empty queue followed by them (EXEC_013_unmarked_removes_nothing).

The body sentence 'A token a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same firing pass survives the drain ([EXEC-003] AC5).' is about a firing pass of several firings; a single queue firing has no earlier firing, so it is EXEC-003's subject and the Phase 2 cycle relation's, not encoded.

AC1 (reset place with 5 tokens, all removed) is line 1 at a reset place that is not an output place: it ends empty (EXEC_013_nonvacuous, the five-token place 3). On token counts it is CORE-034's first line (cited on CORE_034_reference).

AC2 (reset place empty, no error) is line 4 and line 1 at an unmarked reset place (EXEC_013_nonvacuous). On token counts it is CORE-034's second line: a reset arc does not affect whether its transition can fire (cited on CORE_034_reference).

AC3 (the reset place is also an input or read place of another enabled transition, whose clock restarts) is read in TIME-012's form and is not encoded here: the queue firing has no clocks. TIME-012 says the other transition loses its clock in the intermediate marking and is newly armed with a fresh clock when it is enabled again; AC3's bare 'restarts' is read as that, not as a restart of a transition that the drain leaves disabled. The evidence is TIME-012's AC3 example TIME_012_ac3 (cited there).

AC4 (reset draining after read peeking; a read arc and a reset arc on one place observe the pre-reset front token; the overall order is input consumption, read peeks, reset draining) is lines 2 and 3; the mutants exec013_resetFirst (draining before the peek) and exec013_drainFirst (draining before input consumption) are killed by lines 3 and 2.
The test derivation's clock-restart check is AC3's and is TIME-012's subject.

requirements.title: Reset Arc Execution (executor companion)
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T) (n : String) (sy : Bool),
    on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.start n sy) s', shall fun s s' ↦
      ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (rest : List (Reference.Trans N)),
        s.order = t :: rest → t.core.name = n → ∀ (p : N), ResetArc t p → s'.M p = hid s p
reading: For every executor R, every configuration C and every start step of a name n in R, from state s to state s': if the head of the pass's order in s is a transition t named n (the transition the step starts), then every reset place p of t holds in s' exactly the tokens deposited inside the current pass (the hidden tail hid s p of the pass-visible marking).
quotes: This happens during the firing step, before the action executes.
*When* a transition fires, it *shall* drain each of its reset places ([CORE-034]) before its action starts.
A token a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same firing pass survives the drain ([EXEC-003] AC5).

*When* a transition starts in a firing pass, it *shall* drain each of its reset places in that same step, so the place keeps exactly the tokens a synchronous action deposited there earlier in the pass.
assumes: This is the second block of EXEC-013 (ruling D33 (a), design NR-1). The first block, EXEC_013 (EXEC_013.lean), states the order of the parts of one atomic queue firing and is unchanged; it deferred 'The body sentence: A token a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same firing pass survives the drain ([EXEC-003] AC5)' and the deposits of an action's publications to the executor model. This block is that executor line.

The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean); the witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean). 'Fires' is read as 'starts in a firing pass'. The firing step of the first quoted sentence is the start step: the drain happens in it, and the action's steps (write, flush, ret) can only follow it, because the firing is in flight only from its start. So the drain is 'before its action starts' (the first shall sentence) and the action's output, deposited later at the tails (EXEC-020, EXEC-021, CONC-003), is never drained by its own firing. A start that leaves the reset places as they are, deferring the drain past the action's start, breaks the line (EXEC_013_cycle_forbids_drainLate).

The line is the new shall sentence and the third quoted sentence: the drain takes the pass-visible tokens only (EXEC-003 AC5), so the place keeps exactly its same-pass tail; an input place that is also a reset place keeps it too. A start that drains the live marking swallows the deposit (EXEC_013_cycle_forbids_drainSwallows). The tail is the derived term hid s (EXEC-003); outside a firing pass it is empty, and the line says the place ends the start empty.

The started transition is named, not constrained, as in EXEC-010's companion: the line reads 'if the head of the pass's order is t and t is named n', and that a start takes the head is EXEC-003's first line. The line reads every start step, while the sentence speaks of a start in a firing pass; a start happens only in a pass by EXEC-001 and EXEC-003. hid is read off the executor's own record of the same-pass deposits, so 'the tokens a synchronous action deposited there earlier in the pass' is the line's meaning only jointly with EXEC-003's lines 2, 5 and 8, which fix how that record evolves. The line is a consequence of EXEC-003's second line (a reset place, which qConsume empties, keeps its same-pass tail), restated for EXEC-013 under ruling D33 (a); it adds no constraint beyond it.

The other quoted sentences of the first block (consumption, then read peeks, then draining; the read token of a read and reset place; an unmarked reset place blocks nothing) are its subject, applied by EXEC-003's line 2 to the pass-visible marking; they are not restated. Tokens an action published before it completed land at the tails by a publish step, after the start that drained, and stay whatever happens to the completion (ruling D17): that is CONC-003's second line and EXEC-021's second line, with this line placing the drain before them. The clock restart of AC3 is TIME-012's companion (the restart flag set at the start from the live intermediate marking, ruling D7).

AC1 (five tokens, all removed), AC2 (empty reset place, no error) and AC4 (draining after read peeking) are the first block's. AC3 is TIME-012's. At the grain of a pass EXEC_013_cycle_nonvacuous shows a reset place holding the old token 5 and the same-pass deposit 6: the start drains 5 and keeps 6. The test derivation is the first block's.

requirements.title: Output Token Deposition
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] Q ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (M : QueueMarking N T) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T))
    (M' : QueueMarking N T),
    Q t M δ e M' →
      ∃ base,
        (∀ (p : N), AppendedAtTail base M' e p) ∧
          (∀ p ∉ inPlaces t, ¬ResetArc t p → base p = M p) ∧
            ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t, ¬ResetArc t p → (base p).Sublist (M p)
reading: For every queue firing of Q, of a transition t from the queue marking M, delivering δ, emitting e and leaving M', there is a queue marking base (the queues the firing leaves before its deposit) such that:
every place p holds after the firing the queue base holds at p, followed by the tokens e emits to p, in emission order (AppendedAtTail base M' e p);
on every place p that is neither an input place nor a reset place of t, base holds the queue M held at p;
on every input place p of t that is not a reset place, base holds at p tokens M held at p, in the order M held them (a sublist of M's queue at p).
quotes: Each token is added to the end of the target place's FIFO queue, in the order the action produced it.

*When* the executor admits the completion of an action and output validation does not reject the produced tokens ([EXEC-021], [CONC-026]), the executor *shall* add each produced token at the tail of its place's queue, in the order the action produced the tokens.
assumes: A queue firing relates a transition, the queue marking it fires from, what it delivers to its action, the tokens the action emits (places and tokens, in the order the action produced them) and the queue marking it leaves (glossary: QFireRel, Queue order). The firing is atomic: the step that starts it deposits its emission.

Phase 1 has no completion and no admission. Every firing of the reference queue relation (RefQFire) deposits an emission whose places are an offered deposit of the output spec, so it stands for an admitted completion whose produced tokens pass output validation, which is the trigger of the quoted 'shall' sentence. Which completions the executor admits (not one whose firing ended with its timeout outcome, [EXEC-022] and [IO-013]; not one a stop on a terminal place abandoned, [EXEC-042]; not one an immediate termination abandoned, [ENV-015]; every in-flight one a close waits for, [ENV-013]) is the executor model of Phase 2 (RefExec) and is deferred to it, as is the moment of admission ([EXEC-001] step 1, or the firing pass for a synchronous action).

The sentence 'If the completion of an action is not admitted, or output validation rejects the produced tokens, then the executor shall not deposit any token the action produced at completion.' is deferred to Phase 2: it speaks of completions that are not admitted and of a validation that fails, neither of which is a firing of the atomic Phase 1 relation. The joint model's QProjectsTo Q RefFire excludes every step whose emitted places are not an offered deposit, so at Phase 1 grain no step deposits an emission validation would reject; it is not a line of this block. It does not model the rejected completion itself: a firing that consumes, fails validation and deposits nothing (TransitionFailed, [EXEC-021], [EVT-008]) is not a step of the atomic relation, and neither is a firing of an executor with the validation skip of [CONC-026], which deposits a write that is not an offered deposit. Both are Phase 2 (RefExec).

Tokens an action published before it completed ([IO-015]) are not modelled: the Phase 1 action emits only at the end of the firing. That they are not deposited again and survive a failed or abandoned completion is deferred to Phase 2.

Line 1 is the quoted sentences: the emitted tokens are the tail of each queue, in emission order. Lines 2 and 3 say what 'its place's queue' is, the queue the deposit goes after: on a place the firing does not consume from or reset, the tokens already there (line 2); on an input place that is not reset, tokens the place held, kept in queue order (line 3, glossary Queue order: 'The tokens of a place are kept in the order they were added'). Line 3 does not say which tokens the firing consumes: oldest first is [EXEC-010], and a correlated input of a ν-net match ([NU-020], ruling D16) may take other tokens, which also leaves a sublist; the exact queue left is [EXEC-010] and [EXEC-013]. On a reset place base is unconstrained here; [EXEC-013], [CORE-034] and the count guard QProjectsTo Q RefFire make it empty. Without line 3 an executor that reorders the tokens left on an input place it also deposits to would satisfy the block (EXEC_020_mutant_restOrder_killed).
AC1 (an action produces V to P; V appears at the end of P's queue) is line 1 with line 2: the nonvacuous example EXEC_020_nonvacuous deposits 30 to a place already holding 40 and leaves 40 then 30.

AC2 (multiple tokens to the same place are added in order) is line 1 for an emission with several tokens to one place. The reference queue firing deposits one token per claimed place on an action outcome (Reference.deposit, as every branch-enumerating analysis, [IO-016]), and the count guard QProjectsTo Q RefFire imposes the same on every Q, so the joint model has no step with two tokens to one place until the projection compares places as a set, as [IO-015] does. AC2 is therefore witnessed outside the joint model, by executors that accept several tokens into one claimed place under that set comparison: the in-order one satisfies EXEC-020 and leaves 40, 30, 31 when 30 then 31 go to a place holding 40 (EXEC_020_allows_several), and the reverse-order one violates it (EXEC_020_forbids_reversed).

AC3 (a completion that is not admitted deposits none of the action's tokens) and AC4 (a completion whose produced tokens fail validation deposits none of them) are the deferred sentence above, Phase 2.

requirements.title: Output Token Deposition (executor companion)
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    (∀ (i : ℕ),
        on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.commit i) s', shall fun s s' ↦
          ∃ f e,
            AdmittedCompletion C s i f e ∧
              C.validate f.t (validIn f e) = true ∧ s'.M = qAppend s.M e) ∧
      (∀ (l : XLbl N T),
          exec020c_deposits l = false →
            on fun s s' ↦ R C s l s', shall fun s s' ↦ s'.M = s.M) ∧
        (on fun s s' ↦ isExecPhase s.phase = false ∧ ∃ l, R C s l s', shall fun s s' ↦
            s'.M = s.M) ∧
          (∀ (i : ℕ),
              on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.tdeposit i) s', shall fun s s' ↦
                ∃ f e,
                  List.find? (fun x ↦ x.id == i) s.fl = some f ∧
                    f.out = some (Outcome.timedOut e) ∧
                      canSettle C s i f = true ∧ s'.M = qAppend s.M e) ∧
            ∀ (i : ℕ) (s : XSt N T) (f : Firing N T) (e : List (N × T)),
              s.phase = Phase.completions →
                AdmittedCompletion C s i f e →
                  C.validate f.t (validIn f e) = true →
                    C.relay f.t f.deliv e = true → ∃ s', R C s (XLbl.commit i) s'
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C:

a commit step of a firing identity i, from state s to state s', settles an admitted completion of i (glossary: Admitted completion: the run is under way, no terminal place is marked, the outcome of i is queued, it returned normally with emission e, and the phase allows it) whose emission output validation accepts, and leaves in s' the marking of s with e appended at the tails, in emission order;
a step whose label is not a start, a commit, a tdeposit, a publish or an inject leaves the marking unchanged;
a step from a state whose run has finished leaves the marking unchanged;

a tdeposit step of i, from s to s', settles a firing of i whose outcome is a timeout outcome e, under the guard every settle shares (canSettle: the run is under way, no terminal place is marked, the outcome of i is queued, and the phase allows settling it), and leaves in s' the marking of s with e appended at the tails, in the order of e;
in step 1 (phase completions), every admitted completion of i with emission e that output validation and the relay check accept can be deposited: R offers a commit step of i.
quotes: It never admits the completion of a firing that ended with its timeout outcome ([EXEC-022], [IO-013]), that a stop on a terminal place abandoned ([EXEC-042]) or that an immediate termination abandoned ([ENV-015]).
*If* the completion of an action is not admitted, or output validation rejects the produced tokens, *then* the executor *shall not* deposit any token the action produced at completion.
A publication still queued when a terminal place stops the run ([EXEC-042]) is discarded.

*When* the executor deposits the tokens an action produced at completion, it *shall* do so only in the step that admits that completion, while the run is under way and no terminal place is marked, and *shall* add them at the tails of their places' queues in the order the action produced them.

The executor *shall* change the marking only when it starts a transition, deposits the tokens of an admitted completion, deposits a timeout outcome ([EXEC-022]), deposits a mid-action publication ([IO-015]) or injects an external event ([ENV-003]).
*When* a run has finished ([EXEC-041]), the executor *shall not* change the marking, so a completion, a timeout outcome or a publication that is still in flight or queued deposits nothing.

*When* the executor deposits the timeout outcome of a firing ([EXEC-022], [IO-013]), it *shall* do so only in a step in which a completion of that firing would be admitted, while the run is under way and no terminal place is marked, and *shall* add exactly the tokens of that outcome at the tails of their places' queues, in the order of the outcome.

*When* the executor admits the completion of an action and output validation does not reject the produced tokens ([EXEC-021], [CONC-026]), the executor *shall* add each produced token at the tail of its place's queue, in the order the action produced the tokens.
assumes: This is the second block of EXEC-020 (ruling D33 (a), design NR-1). The first block, EXEC_020 (EXEC_020.lean), states the tail deposit of the atomic queue firing and is unchanged; it deferred to the executor model the sentence 'If the completion of an action is not admitted, or output validation rejects the produced tokens, then the executor shall not deposit any token the action produced at completion.', AC3 and AC4, and the paragraph on mid-action publications. This block is those executor lines.

The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean); the witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean). Naming: 'admits the completion' is the glossary term Admitted completion (AdmittedCompletion C s i f e): the executor takes the completion up in step 1, on the wake of the wait (ruling D70 (a)) or, for a synchronous action, inside its firing pass, while the run is under way and no terminal place is marked, and not in step 1 or the wait after an immediate termination (ENV-015). A completion it deposits is a commit step; one it rejects is a fail step (EXEC-021); 'the tokens an action produced at completion' is the emission e the action returned. The outside steps (the action writing, flushing, returning, its budget expiring, a caller's request) are CONC-001's.

Line 1 is the first new shall sentence: the deposit happens only in the step that admits the completion and appends the emission at the tails in emission order (the first block's line 1 at this grain). It covers the sentence 'It never admits ...' for the terminal stop and the immediate termination: an executor that deposits a completion while a terminal place is marked breaks it (EXEC_020_cycle_forbids_admitWhenTerminal), and so does one that deposits the emission in reverse order (EXEC_020_cycle_forbids_reversed). Line 1 also requires output validation to accept the emission (the places validation reads, validIn), so the validation half of the deferred shall-not sentence is this block's own: an executor whose commit step deposits an emission validation rejects breaks it (EXEC_020_cycle_forbids_commitUnvalidated). EXEC-021's first line states the same check from validation's side, with the relay check; which tokens the emission holds (those written after the last flush) is CONC-003's first line.

The 'only' of the first new shall sentence is lines 1 and 2 together with three blocks that fix what the other marking-changing steps deposit: a start removes and keeps tokens only as EXEC-003's second line says and adds none, a publish deposits exactly the oldest queued batch (CONC-003's first line), and an inject deposits exactly the injected token (ENV-003). Within this block alone an executor whose start, publish or inject step also appended a returned emission would pass lines 1 and 2; those blocks forbid it.

Line 2 is the second new shall sentence, the frame of every other step, outside steps included. With line 1 it is the deferred shall-not sentence: a completion that is not admitted or that validation rejects is settled by a fail step or not at all, and no step but a commit deposits its emission. An executor whose fail step deposits the rejected emission anyway breaks it (EXEC_020_cycle_forbids_failDeposits). The queue of publications on a fail step is EXEC-021's second line.

Line 3 is the third new shall sentence, and the quoted 'A publication still queued when a terminal place stops the run ([EXEC-042]) is discarded.' after the finish step: once the run has finished (the finish step of EXEC-041; a terminal stop, a quiescent or closed finish, an immediate termination), no step changes the marking, so an action still in flight that returns, a queued completion and a queued publication deposit nothing. An executor that keeps the publication queue across a terminal stop and deposits it afterwards breaks it (EXEC_020_cycle_forbids_publishAfterStop). Between the step that marks a terminal place and the finish step, line 2 still allows a publish step to change the marking; there the quoted sentence is EXEC-042's first line, which forbids every executor step but finish terminal while a terminal place is marked, and line 1 and line 4 keep commit and tdeposit out by their guard. That the finish step itself keeps the marking is EXEC-041's.

Line 4 is the fourth new shall sentence, the timeout half of 'It never admits ...': a timeout deposit settles the firing under the guard every settle step shares (canSettle, the guard of an admitted completion: the run is under way, no terminal place is marked, the outcome is queued, the phase allows settling it, and in step 1 or the wait no immediate termination was requested, ENV-015), and deposits exactly the outcome, in its order. An executor that deposits a timeout outcome while a terminal place is marked breaks it (EXEC_020_cycle_forbids_tdepositWhenTerminal); one that merges the action's unpublished writes into the outcome at the deposit breaks it (EXEC_020_cycle_forbids_mergeOnTimeout). The deposit is the outcome recorded on the firing (f.out); that the expiry step records a timeout outcome of the Timeout node and not the action's writes is EXEC-022's first line (exec022_QOutcome) with IO-013 and IO-014 (Cfg.timeoutOut), so 'not what the action wrote after its last publication' (AC3, the test derivation's timeout case) is line 4 together with EXEC-022's first line. The relay check on the outcome is EXEC-021's fifth line; that the expiry is offered only for an asynchronous firing with a Timeout node is EXEC-022's. Line 4 contains EXEC-022's deposit line (the same deposit, stated from the timeout's side) and adds the settle guard.

Line 5 is the shall sentence 'When the executor admits the completion of an action and output validation does not reject the produced tokens ..., the executor shall add each produced token ...' at the grain of the executor: lines 1 to 4 constrain the steps that occur, so without line 5 an executor that never deposits an accepted completion would satisfy them, and no line of EXEC-001 or EXEC-040 obliges a step to happen (EXEC-001's assumes: 'nothing here obliges a step to happen'). Line 5 says the commit is offered in step 1 for every admitted completion that validation and the relay check accept; EXEC-001's fourth line (no publication, injection or start before the queued outcome is settled) and EXEC-021's third line (a fail step only for an error, a rejected emission or a rejected relay) then leave the commit as the only way on. It is read in step 1 only: TypeScript settles every firing in step 1 and never inside the pass (EXEC-003), and Rust's settle in the wait goes on to step 1 (ruling D70 (a)), so an offer in the pass or the wait would hold of one runtime and not another. The relay check is NU-054's, carried by EXEC-021; with it accepted, the reference commit rule needs nothing else. An executor that never commits breaks line 5 (EXEC_020_cycle_forbids_neverCommits). That the loop goes on at all is CONC-010's and EXEC-040's.

The two sentences of the body before the shall sentences ('After an action completes and the executor admits the completion, ...' and 'Each token is added to the end of the target place's FIFO queue, in the order the action produced it.') and the paragraph defining a completion and admission are the first block's lines and this block's naming; 'A close ([ENV-013]) waits for in-flight actions and admits their completions.' is ENV-013's. The mid-action publication paragraph is CONC-003's (each batch deposited once, oldest first, at the tails, whatever happens to the completion, ruling D17) and line 3 with EXEC-042's first line (discarded at a terminal stop).

AC1 (V at the end of P's queue) and AC2 (several tokens to one place, in order) are lines 1 and 5: EXEC_020_cycle_nonvacuous deposits 30 then 31 into a place holding 40, which ends 40, 30, 31; unlike the first block, the executor model witnesses AC2 in the joint model, because validation reads sets of places (IO-015). AC3 (not admitted: the timeout outcome, or a terminal stop while the action was in flight) is line 4 with EXEC-022's first line and lines 1 and 3 with EXEC-042's first line: the example deposits the timeout outcome 5 and not the 50 the action wrote, and an abandoned firing returns after a terminal stop without a deposit. AC4 (validation fails, nothing deposited) is lines 1 and 2: the example fails a firing whose emission validation rejects and leaves its place empty. The test derivation (three tokens in order; a timeout budget outlived; a write outside the chosen branch) is these examples.

requirements.title: Output Spec Validation
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    C.SetValidated →
      ∀ (i : ℕ),
        (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.commit i) s', shall fun s s' ↦
            ∃ f ∈ s.fl,
              f.id = i ∧
                ∃ e,
                  f.out = some (Outcome.ok e) ∧
                    C.validate f.t (validIn f e) = true ∧
                      C.relay f.t f.deliv e = true ∧ s'.M = qAppend s.M e) ∧
          (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.fail i) s', shall fun s s' ↦
              s'.M = s.M ∧ s'.pq = s.pq) ∧
            (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.fail i) s', shall fun s x ↦
                ∃ f ∈ s.fl,
                  f.id = i ∧
                    (f.out = some Outcome.err ∨
                      (∃ e,
                          f.out = some (Outcome.ok e) ∧
                            (C.validate f.t (validIn f e) = false ∨
                              C.relay f.t f.deliv e = false)) ∨
                        ∃ e,
                          f.out = some (Outcome.timedOut e) ∧
                            C.relay f.t f.deliv e = false)) ∧
              (on fun s s' ↦
                  (∃ ok, R C s (XLbl.ret i ok) s') ∨ ∃ p x, R C s (XLbl.write i p x) s',
                  shall fun s s' ↦ s'.M = s.M) ∧
                on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.tdeposit i) s', shall fun s x ↦
                  ∃ f ∈ s.fl,
                    f.id = i ∧
                      ∃ e,
                        f.out = some (Outcome.timedOut e) ∧ C.relay f.t f.deliv e = true
reading: For every executor R, every configuration C whose output verdict reads a set of places, and every firing identity i:

a commit step of i deposits exactly the emission e the action of i returned, each token at the tail of its place in emission order, and only when output validation accepts the places of e followed by the places i has already published, and the join-relay check accepts e;
a fail step of i changes neither the marking nor the queue of publications not yet deposited;

a fail step of i happens only when the action of i failed, or it returned an emission e that output validation (over the same places as in the first line) or the join-relay check rejects, or i ended with a timeout outcome e that the join-relay check rejects;
a step in which the action of i writes a token or returns leaves the marking unchanged;
a step that deposits the timeout outcome e of i happens only when the join-relay check accepts e.
quotes: Before depositing tokens, the executor validates that the produced tokens satisfy the declared output specification (see [IO-015]).
An executor with the validation skip of [CONC-026] enabled does not validate.

*When* an executor with output validation enabled admits the completion of an action, it *shall* validate the produced tokens against the transition's output spec ([IO-015]) before it deposits any of them.
*If* the produced tokens of an admitted completion fail output validation, *then* the executor *shall* deposit none of them and *shall* emit a TransitionFailed event ([EVT-008]).

*If* the produced tokens of an admitted completion fail output validation, *then* the executor *shall not* restore the tokens the firing consumed and *shall not* remove the tokens the action published before it completed ([IO-015]).

*When* an executor with output validation enabled validates the produced tokens of an admitted completion, it *shall* count the places of every batch the action published before it completed ([IO-015]) as produced, together with the places of the produced tokens.
*If* the produced tokens of an admitted completion pass output validation, *then* the executor *shall not* fail the firing.
The timeout outcome is not a completion of the action: [EXEC-022] and [IO-013] govern its deposit.
*When* a firing ends with its timeout outcome, the executor *shall not* validate the timeout outcome against the transition's output spec; the join-relay check of [NU-054] still runs on it.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A firing starts in a firing pass and settles in a later step; the outside steps write, flush and ret are its action writing a token, publishing what it wrote, and returning normally (with what it wrote since the last flush as its emission) or with an error. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), the graph of a step function checked rule by rule against the Rust executor.

Naming: the markdown's 'admits the completion' is the executor taking the completion up in step 1 or inside the pass (glossary: Admitted completion). The model splits what follows into two labels: commit i, the admitted completion passes validation and is deposited, and fail i, it is rejected (or the action failed, [EXEC-030]).
