Snapshots: an answer to a snapshot request is exempt from line 1 only when it leaves the state as it is, so it cannot unmark the terminal place or settle anything; what it answers is ENV-014's. The reference answers none while a terminal place is marked (snapshotStep requires a live state); Java breaks its loop before serviceMarkingRequest; Rust answers a snapshot queued behind the stop after its loop, from the state finish terminal leaves. That state keeps the firings in flight (lines 5 and 6), so its answer reports the abandoned work as work in flight: EXEC_042_nonvacuous decides snapAnswer of the state AC2's run ends in to be some true, the quoted 'A snapshot taken afterwards ([ENV-014]) still reports abandoned work as work in flight.'

Line 2 is the second quoted shall sentence for a completion and 'the deposit that marks the terminal place completes atomically': the step that marks a terminal place deposits the firing's whole outcome, not the outputs up to the first token in a terminal place (EXEC_042_forbids_partialDeposit). That every commit and tdeposit deposits its whole outcome is EXEC-020's, EXEC-021's and EXEC-022's; this line states it for the step that ends the run. Which label deposits which outcome (a commit a returned emission, a tdeposit a timeout outcome) is not this line's: EXEC-021 line 1 ties a commit to a returned emission, and EXEC-022 ties a tdeposit to a timeout outcome. Outside the model: an event store throwing on TokenAdded while Java deposits a completion (processSyncOutput and processCompletedTransitions, BitmapNetExecutor.java:1788-1817 and 1897-1927), which Java reports as a failure of a partly deposited firing; if a token of the deposited prefix marked a terminal place, the stop is latched with a partial outcome. The model's deposit is atomic and has no host callback that can throw, so line 2 reads the model's deposits only (as EXEC-030's assumes do for its line 1).

Line 3 is the second quoted shall sentence for a published batch and the check point 'a mid-action publication ([IO-015])': a publish step that marks a terminal place deposits the whole batch at the head of the publication queue (EXEC_042_forbids_partialPublish). The publishing firing is still running when its batch marks the place; it is abandoned like any other action in flight (the quoted bullet), so its later writes and its returned emission are never deposited. EXEC_042_nonvacuous publishes a batch of a that marks 9 and 3, with a and b both still in flight, and finishes terminal. A batch still queued at the stop is discarded: the reference's finish terminal empties the publication queue (EXEC-020).

Line 4 is 'A terminal place MAY be an environment place: injecting into it ends the run.' and its shall sentence: an inject step of a queued event for a terminal place marks that place, so the state is not live and line 1 ends the run there (AC3). An executor that drops such an event instead of injecting it, so that a terminal environment place can never be marked from outside, violates it (EXEC_042_forbids_dropTerminalInject). That every inject step deposits its event's token at the tail of its place is ENV-003's; line 4 states only that the place is marked.

Line 5 is 'keep every firing still in flight as abandoned work in flight' from the deposit on: a step that marks a terminal place takes no firing out of flight except the one it settles (a commit, fail or tdeposit of that firing). An executor that cancels the firings in flight at the deposit that marks a terminal place (clearing its in-flight map at the latch) violates it (EXEC_042_forbids_cancelInFlight), although its finish terminal keeps the list it finds, which is then empty. Between that deposit and the finish, line 1 leaves only outside steps and unchanged snapshot answers; what outside steps (an action returning or timing out) do to the list of firings is not this block's.

Line 6 is the third, fifth and sixth quoted shall sentences: the finish terminal step happens only when a terminal place is marked (EXEC_042_forbids_terminalAtRest), keeps the marking, so the tokens the abandoned firings consumed stay consumed (EXEC_042_forbids_rollbackOnStop), keeps the firings in flight, which a snapshot taken afterwards reports as in flight (EXEC_042_forbids_dropInFlight), and empties the queue of external events, which refuses them (EXEC_042_forbids_keepQueued). Emptying the queue is how this level reads 'refuse': a refused event and a dropped one look the same here, and the completion signal of each event cleared by finish terminal is false (ENV-004, design R17), a line the ENV-004 block owes. The reference also empties the publication queue (EXEC-020: a queued publication is discarded).

The fourth quoted shall sentence ('without waiting for the actions still in flight') says that finish terminal is offered at once, firings in flight or not. That is coverage, which a safety line cannot state, so no line of this block encodes it; coverage belongs to the consistency theorem, whose coverage conjunct ExecCoversW5 (ConsistencyExec.lean) carries it. An executor that offers finish terminal only once every action in flight has returned (exec042_wait, a stop written in the shape of a close) satisfies this block (exec042_wait_meets) and the wave 0 ExecCovers, and fails that conjunct. The conjunct is Exec042Covers (finish terminal offered from every running state that is not live): the reference meets it (exec042_ref_covers, from exec042_finish_offered) and exec042_wait does not (exec042_wait_not_covered, on AC2's run with b's action not returned).

Late results: after the stop the run is over, so no step deposits anything (EXEC-041: no executor step after finish). Before the finish, line 1 forbids settling a completion, and an action's own steps (write, ret, expire) leave the marking unchanged (CONC-001). Together: once a terminal place is marked, every later step of a run is an outside step, an unchanged snapshot answer or finish terminal (exec042_stop_absorbs, under CONC-001's frame of outside steps; exec042_ref_stop_absorbs for the reference).

Requests: a request that arrives between the terminal deposit and the finish is accepted into the event queue and cleared by the finish (Rust: inject returns true once enqueued, the event is dropped with the receiver). Its answer is ENV-004's.

Events: 'No diagnostic event is emitted ([EVT-013] AC5): the stop was designed, not caller-requested.' is not encoded here; the executor relation carries no events, and EVT-013 (AC5) is the requirement that states it.

Scope: the configuration's terminal places are given; that they are the places the net declared, and that a declared terminal place is not consumed or read, is the build block EXEC_042_build. A terminal place that is an environment place ends the run when an injection marks it (line 4, AC3).

Implementation status: Java and Rust deposit a synchronous action's outputs inside the firing pass (a commit in phase pass) and break the pass there; TypeScript settles a synchronous firing in step 1, so a transition started earlier in the same pass is abandoned instead. Both are runs of RefExec (settleOk: a synchronous firing may settle in the pass or in step 1), and line 1 holds of both.

AC1 (initial marking marks a terminal place: fires nothing, ends terminal) is line 1 from the initial state (exec042_stop_absorbs); EXEC_042_nonvacuous finishes terminal from the initial state of such a net and shows that step 1 of the loop is not offered there.

AC2 (an asynchronous completion marks a terminal place; the run does not wait for another action in flight, whose result never appears) is lines 1, 5 and 6; EXEC_042_nonvacuous's AC2 run finishes terminal with the other firing still in flight and its output place empty, and no settle of it is offered. That the finish is offered with the action not returned is the coverage conjunct Exec042Covers.

AC3 (an injection marks a terminal environment place; an event queued behind it is refused) is lines 1, 4 and 6; EXEC_042_nonvacuous's AC3 run injects into the terminal environment place, which leaves a state that is not live, offers no second inject, and finishes with the second event cleared.

AC4 (no transition starts after the deposit that marks a terminal place, in both deposit locations) is line 1; EXEC_042_nonvacuous's AC4 run settles a synchronous firing inside the pass, offers no start of the next transition in the order, and finishes terminal.
AC5 (a transition that consumes or reads a terminal place is rejected when the net is built) is the build block EXEC_042_build.
AC6 (compose and instantiate reject a subnet body that declares a terminal place) is the composition model's (RefCompose, wave W8), not encoded here.

AC7, AC8 and AC9 (the verification paragraph: DeadlockFree with terminal places, byte-identical scripts without them, the QuiescentCount lower bound) are the verifier's; their evidence is the cites of Novel/InFlight.lean (split_covers_executor, split_stop_sound, quiescent_count_stop_sound, terminal_stop_witness) and the TerminalRewrite theorems, not encoded here. AC9's executor half (both executors end with a = ok = 0) is AC2's run up to renaming (s is place 0, a is place 1, ok is place 2, done is place 9, f is transition a with an extra output 3, t is transition b): EXEC_042_nonvacuous's AC2 run ends with places 1 and 2 empty.

requirements.title: Terminal Places
requirements.statement:
fun {N A} [DecidableEq N] B NB ↦
  ∀ (inp : NetIn B),
    (inp.TerminalClash → ∃ e, NB inp = Except.error e) ∧
      (¬inp.TerminalClash → ∃ b, NB inp = Except.ok b) ∧
        ∀ (b : BuiltNet N A),
          NB inp = Except.ok b → ∀ (p : N), p ∈ b.terminals ↔ p ∈ inp.terminals
requirements.scope: the net builder of every implementation, used without composition and without fusion sets
reading: For every transition builder B, every net builder NB over its instances, and every input inp (declared places, added transitions, declared terminal places):
if a declared terminal place of inp is an input place or a read place of one of its added transitions, NB rejects inp;
if none is, NB returns a net;
a net NB returns for inp has exactly the declared terminal places of inp as its terminal places.
quotes: A terminal place MUST NOT be an input or a read-arc place of any transition: such a transition could never fire, so the net is rejected when it is built.
*If* a declared terminal place is an input place or a read-arc place of a transition of the net, *then* building the net *shall* fail.

*When* a net is built without composition and without fusion sets and no declared terminal place is an input place or a read-arc place of one of its transitions, building it *shall* succeed, and the built net's terminal places *shall* be exactly the declared ones.
assumes: A net builder (NetBuilder B, Reference/Build.lean) is the build call of one implementation's net builder, read as a function from what the host added (NetIn B) to a built net (BuiltNet) or a rejection with a message (a panic or an exception). The added transitions are instances of the transition builder B (a net holds only builder outputs, the W2 tracer decision). The clash (NetIn.TerminalClash) is a declared terminal place that an added transition's definition names on an input arc or a read arc (TransDef.ConsumesOrReads). The witness is the reference net builder refNetBuild.

Line 1 is the first quoted sentence and the first shall sentence (Rust validate_terminals, Java checkTerminals, TypeScript requireWellFormedTerminals all reject both an input arc and a read arc). A builder without the check (EXEC_042_build_forbids_noCheck) or one that checks input arcs only (EXEC_042_build_forbids_inputsOnly) violates it. Only the rejection is stated, not its message: the messages differ between the runtimes and the spec fixes none.

Lines 2 and 3 are the second shall sentence and the body's 'A net MAY declare terminal places': a terminal place on an inhibitor arc, on a reset arc or on an output is allowed, so a builder that rejects every declared terminal place (EXEC_042_build_mutant_rejectAll_killed) violates line 2, and one that drops the declarations, so that the run has no terminal place, violates line 3 (EXEC_042_build_forbids_dropTerminals). Line 3 reads the terminal places as a set; the reference keeps them once each in declaration order (refNetBuild_terminals).

Scope: as for CORE-040, a builder used without composition (MOD-020, MOD-025) and without fusion sets (MOD-060, MOD-061), whose own rejections (fusion overlap, a reference to a bound port place) would make line 2 fail; the second shall sentence names that scope ('a net built without composition and without fusion sets'), so it is no stronger than line 2; what a composed net does with terminal places is the composition model's (W8), and AC6 (compose and instantiate reject a subnet body that declares a terminal place) is its line. With no terminal place declared, line 2 is CORE-040's line 4.

AC5 (a transition that consumes or reads a terminal place is rejected when the net is built) is line 1; EXEC_042_build_nonvacuous rejects a net whose transition reads the terminal place and builds one whose transition has it as inhibitor and output.

requirements.title: Graph Export Format
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),
    (∀ t ∈ X.trans,
        ∀ (p : String),
          p ∈ inPlaces t.toTrans ∨
              OutputArc t.toTrans p ∨
                InhibitorArc t.toTrans p ∨ ReadArc t.toTrans p ∨ ResetArc t.toTrans p →
            List.countP (fun n ↦ decide (n.ref = NodeRef.place p)) (E cfg X).nodes = 1) ∧
      ((List.map ExportTrans.name X.trans).Nodup →
          ∀ t ∈ X.trans,
            List.countP (fun n ↦ decide (n.ref = NodeRef.trans t.name)) (E cfg X).nodes =
              1) ∧
        (∀ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,
            (∀ (p : String),
                n.ref = NodeRef.place p →
                  p ∈ X.places ∨
                    ∃ t ∈ X.trans,
                      p ∈ inPlaces t.toTrans ∨
                        OutputArc t.toTrans p ∨
                          InhibitorArc t.toTrans p ∨
                            ReadArc t.toTrans p ∨ ResetArc t.toTrans p) ∧
              ∀ (u : String), n.ref = NodeRef.trans u → ∃ t ∈ X.trans, t.name = u) ∧
          (∀ t ∈ X.trans,
              ∀ (p : String),
                (p ∈ inPlaces t.toTrans →
                    ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                      e.arc = ArcType.input ∧
                        e.src = NodeRef.place p ∧ e.dst = NodeRef.trans t.name) ∧
                  (InhibitorArc t.toTrans p →
                      ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                        e.arc = ArcType.inhibitor ∧
                          e.src = NodeRef.place p ∧ e.dst = NodeRef.trans t.name) ∧
                    (ReadArc t.toTrans p →
                      ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                        e.arc = ArcType.read ∧
                          e.src = NodeRef.place p ∧ e.dst = NodeRef.trans t.name)) ∧
            ((List.map ExportTrans.name X.trans).Nodup →
                ∀ t ∈ X.trans,
                  ∀ (p : String),
                    exp001Drawn (E cfg X) ArcType.input p t.name =
                        List.count p (inPlaces t.toTrans) ∧
                      exp001Drawn (E cfg X) ArcType.inhibitor p t.name =
                          List.count p t.toTrans.core.inhibitors ∧
                        exp001Drawn (E cfg X) ArcType.read p t.name =
                          List.count p t.toTrans.core.reads) ∧
              (∀ t ∈ X.trans,
                  ∀ (p : String),
                    OutputArc t.toTrans p →
                      ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                        e.src.owner? = some t.name ∧
                          (e.arc = ArcType.output ∨
                              e.arc = ArcType.resetOutput ∧ ResetArc t.toTrans p) ∧
                            e.dst = NodeRef.place p) ∧
                ∀ t ∈ X.trans,
                  ∀ (p : String),
                    ResetArc t.toTrans p →
                      ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                        e.src.owner? = some t.name ∧
                          (e.arc = ArcType.reset ∨
                              e.arc = ArcType.resetOutput ∧ OutputArc t.toTrans p) ∧
                            e.dst = NodeRef.place p
requirements.scope: every exporter, the nodes and the arc edges of one exported net
reading: For the exporter E, every configuration cfg and every net X:

(1) every place p on which some transition t of X has an input arc, an output arc, an inhibitor arc, a read arc or a reset arc (the glossary predicates over the firing view t.toTrans) is the place of exactly one node of E cfg X;
(2) if the transitions of X have pairwise distinct names, every transition t of X is the transition of exactly one node of E cfg X (keyed by its name);

(3) every node of E cfg X that stands for a place p has p declared by X or has some transition of X with an input, output, inhibitor, read or reset arc on p, and every node that stands for a transition named u has a transition of X named u;

(4) for every transition t of X and place p: an input arc, an inhibitor arc or a read arc of t on p has an edge of E cfg X of arc type input, inhibitor or read respectively, from the node of p to the node of t;

(5) if the transitions of X have pairwise distinct names, then for every transition t of X and place p the number of edges of E cfg X of arc type input (inhibitor, read) from the node of p to the node of t is the number of times p occurs among the input places (inhibitor places, read places) of t;

(6) an output arc of t on p (p named by t's output spec) has an edge of E cfg X into the node of p whose source is the node of t or a junction of t (NodeRef.owner? is t's name), of arc type output, or of arc type resetOutput when t also has a reset arc on p;
(7) a reset arc of t on p has an edge of E cfg X into the node of p whose source is the node of t or a junction of t, of arc type reset, or of arc type resetOutput when t's output spec also names p.
quotes: The engine MUST support exporting the net structure to at least one standard graph format suitable for visualization.
The export *shall* draw exactly one node for each place on which some transition has an input, output, inhibitor, read or reset arc.
*Where* the transitions of a net have pairwise distinct names, the export *shall* draw exactly one node for each transition.
The export *shall* draw a place node only for a place that the net declares or on which some transition has an arc, and a transition node only for a transition of the net.
The export *shall* draw, for each input arc, inhibitor arc and read arc, an edge of the arc's type from the node of its place to the node of its transition.

*Where* the transitions of a net have pairwise distinct names, the export *shall* draw as many input, inhibitor and read edges from the node of a place to the node of a transition as the transition has arcs of that type on that place.

The export *shall* draw into each place that a transition's output spec names an edge from that transition or from one of its junctions, of type output or, where the transition also has a reset arc on that place, of the combined reset+output type of [EXP-013].

The export *shall* draw into each place on which a transition has a reset arc an edge from that transition or from one of its junctions, of type reset or, where the transition's output spec also names that place, of the combined reset+output type of [EXP-013].
assumes: The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): from a configuration and the export view of a net (glossary ExportNet: declared places, transitions with their input, inhibitor, read and reset arcs and their n-ary output tree, terminal places, membership), the typed graph (glossary XGraph: nodes with what they stand for, edges with their two ends and their arc type) the runtimes build before DOT text (the graph module of the Rust crate libpetri-export, graph.ts, the Java export/graph layer). The arcs are the glossary's arc predicates over the firing view ExportTrans.toTrans, which has the same arcs (ExportTrans.toTrans_core) and whose output arcs are the places the output tree's leaves name (ExportTrans.outputArc_iff), so the block speaks of the arcs the firing relations fire on.

AC1 (export produces valid, parseable output in the chosen format) is kind Q: the DOT text, its escaping and its grammar are not modelled, and the runtimes' renderer tests parse it. The canonical-format sentence of the body names DOT, which is what all three runtimes render the typed graph to; that the typed graph exists for every net is the block's model, a total function. The block's kind is F: its seven lines are the functional content of the requirement, and AC1 and the test derivation's parse check stay with the runtimes' tests.

AC2 (all places and transitions in the net are represented) is lines 1 to 3. A node is identified by what it stands for (glossary NodeRef: a place by its name, a transition by its name), not by its DOT ID; that two names map to two IDs is EXP-014's line under ruling D46, so a sanitising collision does not reach this block. Line 3 bounds the nodes from above: no node stands for a place that the net neither declares nor touches, or for a transition the net does not have (EXP_001_forbids_phantomPlace, EXP_001_forbids_phantomTrans). Junction nodes are not bounded here: which junctions an output tree has is EXP-012's, and that every junction an edge touches has a node is EXP-014's.

Ruling D60 (c): line 1 is the common form of the place set, and line 3 allows a node for every declared place. Rust draws a node for every place the net declares, Java and TypeScript only for the places some arc touches; a place that the net declares and that no arc touches may have a node or none (EXP_001_untouched_open), and both shapes satisfy the block (EXP_001_allows_arcDerived). The end state D60 (a), a node for every declared place, is the reference's answer; the line that asks for it waits for the Java and TypeScript mappers to change and is not encoded. The two readings are recorded in this file as candidate definitions, not requirement blocks (exp001DeclaredReading for D60 (a), exp001TouchedOnlyReading for D60 (b)), with EXP_001_placeSet: the reference meets the first and not the second, the Java and TypeScript shape the second and not the first. The markdown records the open case and the intended answer in a sentence without shall.

Lines 2 and 5 are stated for nets whose transitions have pairwise distinct names, as the timing requirements are (TIME-010): two transition instances that share a name are distinct under CORE-021, and all three mappers key a transition node by its name, so a net holding both draws one DOT ID for two transitions and the edges of both end at it. The exporter is not asked to draw anything particular for such a net beyond lines 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7.

AC3 (all arcs, input, output, inhibitor, read and reset, are represented) is lines 4 to 7. The direction of each edge is the runtimes' and EXP-004's (ruling D20): input, inhibitor and read edges run from the place to the transition (EXP_001_forbids_reversedInput), output and reset edges from the transition to the place. An output arc may be drawn from a junction of its transition (EXP-012); the edge's source is required to belong to the arc's own transition (NodeRef.owner?), so an exporter that draws the output of one transition from the node of another violates line 6 (EXP_001_forbids_foreignOutput). That a junction an edge leaves has a node is EXP-014's line, and that the junctions between the transition and the place form a path is EXP-012's and EXP-014's wiring line; neither is this block's.

An output arc and a reset arc of one transition on one place may be drawn as one combined reset+output edge (EXP-013). Lines 6 and 7 allow the combined arc type only where the transition has both arcs on the place, so an exporter that draws a plain output arc as a combined edge because another transition resets the place violates line 6 (EXP_001_forbids_globalResets), and one that draws a standalone reset arc as a combined edge violates line 7 (EXP_001_forbids_resetAsCombined). That the combined edge replaces the plain output edge and the standalone reset edge in exactly that case is EXP-013's line.

How many edges an arc gets: line 5 counts the input, inhibitor and read edges (one per arc, so an exporter that draws every such edge twice violates it, EXP_001_forbids_doubled); the output edges and the standalone reset edges of a transition into a place are counted by EXP-013 (one per leaf naming the place, one per reset arc on a place no leaf names), under the same distinct-names condition, and which output edges pass through which junctions is EXP-012's. Lines 4, 6 and 7 ask for at least one edge per arc. The labels (EXP-006, EXP-018), the style rows (EXP-004) and the categories of the nodes (EXP-002, EXP-003, EXP-008) are other blocks' lines. Ghost edges and clusters (EXP-016, EXP-017) add to the graph and are not read here; the block holds of the reference exporter with every cluster stage (EXP_001_any).

The implementation notes name the format each runtime renders (DOT in all three) and the test derivation (a net with all arc types, exported and checked) is EXP_001_nonvacuous on the reference exporter: the worked net of EXP-013, which has every arc kind.

requirements.title: Visual Semantics: Places
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),
    ∀ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,
      (n.cat ∈ NodeCat.placeRows ↔ ∃ p, n.ref = NodeRef.place p) ∧
        ∀ (p : String),
          n.ref = NodeRef.place p →
            (p ∈ X.places ∨ X.Touched p) ∧ n.xlabel = some p ∧ n.label = ""
requirements.scope: every exporter's mapper, on the nodes of the exported graph (before a documentation generator restyles interface ports)
reading: For the exporter E, every configuration cfg, every net X and every node n of the graph E draws for them:
n has a place category (one of NodeCat.placeRows) exactly when n stands for a place;
and when n stands for place p, p is a place of X (declared in X, or on an arc of a transition of X), the external label of n is p itself and its label is empty.
quotes: Places are rendered as distinct shapes from transitions:
Places: circles, ellipses, or stadium-shaped nodes (following Petri net convention)
Place names are displayed as labels

The mapper *shall* give every place node a place category, which is the place, start, end, environment or terminal row of the style table, and *shall* give no transition node and no junction node a place category (a transition node gets the transition category, see [EXP-003]).

The mapper *shall* draw every place node for a place of the net (one that the net declares or on which some transition has an arc), show the name of that place, as written and not sanitized, as the external label (`xlabel`) of the node, and give the node an empty label, so that nothing is drawn inside it.
assumes: The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): from an export configuration and a net, the typed graph the mapper builds before DOT text, whose nodes (glossary XNode) carry what they stand for (a place, a transition or a junction of a transition), a DOT ID, a node category (a row of the node table of spec/petri-net-styles.json, generated as Libpetri.Export.NodeCat), a label drawn inside the node and an optional external label (xlabel). The DOT text and the attribute syntax are not modelled (EXP-001 AC1, kind Q).

The body bullet on shapes is read on the style table, not on the graph: statement line 1 puts every place node in a place row and no other node in one, and EXP_002_place_rows (decided on the generated table) shows that every place row has shape circle or doublecircle, both circle forms the bullet allows, and that no place row shares its shape with the transition row or a junction row. That a transition node is drawn with the transition row itself is EXP-003's line (the first EARS sentence points to it); with it, line 1 and the table fact give the body's first sentence and AC1 (places are visually distinguishable from transitions). The typed graph has no shape field: a node is drawn with the shape of its category's row, and the runtimes' mappers set each node's shape from its row (Rust writes the transition shape as a literal box), so a mapper that overrides a place node's shape while keeping its category is caught by the runtimes' tests, not here. The colours and pen widths of the rows are the table's and are also checked by the runtimes' tests.

Which of the five place rows a place node gets (terminal, environment, start, end or the regular row) is EXP-008's subject, with the precedence of ruling D51. The exporter is tied to EXP-008's place classifier by the glossary agreement ExportAgrees (each place node has the category the classifier gives it), which the export consistency theorem carries; the reference draws each place node with the row of refPlaceCategory for every cluster stage (EXP_002_draws_EXP_008), so a mapper that draws an end place with the start row violates EXP-008 through that agreement, not this block.

The body bullet on names and AC2 (place names are readable) are read as statement line 2: the name is drawn beside the node as its external label, exactly as written (a place b1/x reads b1/x, not its sanitized DOT ID p_b1_x, EXP_002_forbids_sanitizedXlabel), and nothing is drawn inside the small fixed-size circle; all three mappers do this (an empty label and an xlabel attribute holding the name). An empty label is not the absence of a label: Graphviz draws a node's DOT ID inside it when the label attribute is missing, which statement line 2 rejects (EXP_002_forbids_idInside). Whether the drawn text is legible (font, size, overlap) is kind Q.

Which places get a node at all, and how many, is EXP-001's subject (ruling D60), and the DOT ID of a place node is EXP-014's (ruling D46); this block constrains only the nodes the exporter draws. It does ask, as its second shall sentence says, that the place a node stands for is a place of the net, in the common form of ruling D60 (declared, or on an arc), so that a mapper that records a place node as standing for its sanitized name b1_x and labels it so violates line 2 on its own (EXP_002_forbids_semanticSanitized), and not only through EXP-001's count of the nodes of b1/x. A junction node stands for a junction of a transition and gets a junction row (EXP-012); line 1 only excludes the place rows for it.

Out of scope: the documentation generators (EXP-011) rewrite the DOT of a subnet body after mapping and redraw its interface-port places with the interface-port row, which is not a place row here; that rewrite is a later step on the DOT text, as in EXP-008. Clustering (EXP-016, EXP-017) adds clusters and ghost edges and changes no node, so the block holds of the reference for every cluster stage.

The test derivation (export a net, check the place nodes' shape) is EXP_002_nonvacuous on the reference: a net whose place b1/x is consumed by transition t, which outputs to place done, draws b1/x as a start circle and done as an end double circle, both with an empty label and their names as external labels, and t as a box.

requirements.title: Visual Semantics: Transitions
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),
    (∀ t ∈ X.trans, ∃ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes, n.ref = NodeRef.trans t.name) ∧
      (∀ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,
          ∀ (tn : String), n.ref = NodeRef.trans tn → ∃ t ∈ X.trans, t.name = tn) ∧
        (∀ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,
            n.cat = Export.NodeCat.transition ↔ ∃ tn, n.ref = NodeRef.trans tn) ∧
          (∀ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,
              ∀ (tn : String), n.ref = NodeRef.trans tn → tn.toList <+: n.label.toList) ∧
            (cfg.showIntervals = false →
              cfg.showPriority = false →
                ∀ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,
                  ∀ (tn : String), n.ref = NodeRef.trans tn → n.label = tn)
requirements.scope: every exporter, on the nodes of the graph it draws for a configuration and a net
reading: For the exporter E, every configuration cfg and every net X:
every transition t of X has a node in the graph E cfg X that stands for t (its reference is the transition named t.name);
a node that stands for the transition named tn stands for a transition of X: some transition of X has the name tn;
a node of the graph has the transition category exactly when it stands for a transition;
the label of a node that stands for the transition named tn starts with tn (as character lists);
and when cfg hides both the timing interval and the priority, the label of a node that stands for the transition named tn is tn.
quotes: Transitions are rendered as rectangles or bars (following Petri net convention).
Transition names are displayed as labels.
The export *shall* draw a node for every transition of the net.
The export *shall* draw no node that stands for a transition the net does not have.
The export *shall* give a node the transition category exactly when the node stands for a transition.
The export *shall* label the node of a transition with a text that starts with the transition's name as written in the net.
*Where* the configuration hides the timing interval and the priority, the export *shall* label the node of a transition with the transition's name alone.
assumes: The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): from an export configuration (glossary ExportCfg: direction, the show flags, environment places, cluster source) and a net as the exporter reads it (glossary ExportNet), the typed graph the runtimes' mappers build before DOT text (glossary XGraph). A node (glossary XNode) carries what it stands for (ref), its DOT ID, its node category (a row of the node table, Libpetri.Export.NodeCat), its label and its external label. The DOT text, its attribute syntax and the fonts are not modelled.

Rectangles or bars: the transition category is the transition row of the node table, generated into Lean from spec/petri-net-styles.json (Libpetri.Export.Styles); its shape is box, a rectangle, so the export draws rectangles and does not use bars. No place row (the five rows place, start, end, environment and terminal of EXP-002), no junction row and not the interface-port row has that shape (EXP_003_nonvacuous, decided on the generated table). The third line is therefore the shape sentence: transitions are drawn box-shaped, and no place and no junction is drawn with the transition row. Which place row a place gets is EXP-008's and EXP-002's subject. The sync-channel row is also box-shaped (EXP_003_syncChannel_row); no mapper gives a node that row (only the documentation generators' rewrite of a subnet diagram would, EXP-011), line 3 forbids it for a transition node, and EXP-002's line 1 forbids it for a place node.

AC1 (transitions are visually distinguishable from places) is met jointly with EXP-002: line 3 gives a transition node the transition row and keeps every other node out of it, EXP-002's line 1 gives a place node a place row, and the transition row's shape differs from every place row's shape (the table fact above). This block alone does not keep a place node on a place row: an exporter that draws a place with the box-shaped sync-channel row meets EXP-003 and fails EXP-002's line 1, so the joint theorem rejects it (the row facts are EXP_003_syncChannel_row). The test derivation (verify transition nodes use correct shape syntax) is the table fact and line 3 on the reference; the DOT attribute syntax itself is kind Q.

AC2 (transition names are readable) is kind Q, a property of the rendered picture. What is checked is that the name is displayed: lines 4 and 5 put the transition's name, as written in the net and not its sanitised DOT ID (EXP-014), at the start of its label, so a mapper that labels a transition with its node ID violates the block (EXP_003_forbids_idLabel).

The label format is ruling D41 (a), pinned in EXP-007's label block: the name, then the timing interval when intervals are shown, then the priority when it is shown and is not 0. Lines 4 and 5 are the two consequences of that format this requirement states; the rest of the label is EXP-007's, and the agreement predicate ExportAgrees (glossary) ties the exporter's transition labels to EXP-007's labeller in the joint theorem.

Line 1 overlaps EXP-001's line on transition nodes, which also says that each transition has exactly one node and needs distinct transition names (glossary ExportNet.Distinct); this block states only that the node is drawn, so that an exporter that draws no transition node does not meet it vacuously (EXP_003_forbids_noTransNodes). Line 2 is the converse, which EXP-001 does not state (it counts only the nodes of the net's own transitions): a node whose reference names a transition names one the net has, whatever its row, so an edge pass that makes a node again from a sanitised endpoint ID (a_b from t_a_b) violates the block (EXP_003_forbids_ghostTrans). Lines 3 to 5 speak of every node that stands for a transition name, so two transitions of one name, which no net that builds has, change nothing here.
The external label of a transition node, its DOT ID (EXP-014), the cluster it is drawn in (EXP-016) and the order of the nodes are not stated here; node order is kind Q.

requirements.title: Arc Rendering
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),
    ((∀ t ∈ X.trans, ∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs, ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges, exp004InputEdge t s e) ∧
        ∀ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
          e.arc = ArcType.input →
            ∃ t ∈ X.trans, ∃ s ∈ t.core.inputs, exp004InputEdge t s e) ∧
      ((∀ t ∈ X.trans,
            ∀ p ∈ t.outLeaves,
              p ∉ t.core.resets →
                ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges, exp004OutputEdge t e ∧ e.dst = NodeRef.place p) ∧
          (∀ t ∈ X.trans,
              ∀ fw ∈ exp004TransForwards t,
                fw.2 ∉ t.core.resets → ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges, exp004ForwardEdge t fw e) ∧
            ∀ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
              e.arc = ArcType.output → ∃ t ∈ X.trans, exp004OutputEdge t e) ∧
        ((∀ t ∈ X.trans,
              ∀ p ∈ t.core.inhibitors, ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges, exp004InhibitorEdge t p e) ∧
            ∀ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
              e.arc = ArcType.inhibitor →
                ∃ t ∈ X.trans, ∃ p ∈ t.core.inhibitors, exp004InhibitorEdge t p e) ∧
          ((∀ t ∈ X.trans,
                ∀ p ∈ t.core.reads, ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges, exp004ReadEdge t p e) ∧
              ∀ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                e.arc = ArcType.read →
                  ∃ t ∈ X.trans, ∃ p ∈ t.core.reads, exp004ReadEdge t p e) ∧
            (∀ t ∈ X.trans,
                ∀ p ∈ t.core.resets,
                  p ∉ t.outLeaves → ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges, exp004ResetEdge t p e) ∧
              ∀ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                e.arc = ArcType.reset →
                  ∃ t ∈ X.trans,
                    ∃ p ∈ t.core.resets, p ∉ t.outLeaves ∧ exp004ResetEdge t p e
requirements.scope: every exporter, the input, output, inhibitor, read and reset edges
reading: For every configuration cfg and net X, in the drawn graph E cfg X:

(input) every input arc s of every transition t of X has an edge drawn for it (exp004InputEdge t s: arc type input, from the place of s to the node of t, solid, row match-input if t correlates the place, else row input), and every edge of arc type input is drawn so for some input arc of some transition of X;

(output) for every transition t of X and every leaf place p of its output spec that t does not reset, some edge into p is an output edge of t (exp004OutputEdge t: arc type output, row output, from the node of t or one of its junctions, into a place or a junction of t, and dashed only if it ends in the target P of a ForwardInput leaf from F of t, with P a place t does not reset, and is labelled forwardLabel l F for some l), for every ForwardInput leaf from F to P of t with P not reset by t, some output edge of t into P is dashed and labelled forwardLabel l F for some l (exp004ForwardEdge t), and every edge of arc type output is an output edge of some transition of X;

(inhibitor) every inhibitor arc of every transition has an edge drawn for it (exp004InhibitorEdge: arc type inhibitor, place to transition, row inhibitor, solid, no label), and every edge of arc type inhibitor is drawn so for some inhibitor arc;
(read) every read arc has an edge drawn for it (exp004ReadEdge: arc type read, place to transition, row read, label read), and every edge of arc type read is drawn so for some read arc;

(reset) every reset arc of t on a place that no leaf of t's output spec ends in has an edge drawn for it (exp004ResetEdge: arc type reset, from the node of t to the place, row reset, not dashed, label reset), and every edge of arc type reset is drawn so for some reset arc of some transition t on a place that no leaf of t's output spec ends in.
quotes: Each arc type has a visually distinct rendering.
Input arc: solid arrow from place to transition, row `input` (a correlated input of [EXP-018] takes row `match-input`)

Output arc: solid arrow from transition, or from one of its junction nodes ([EXP-012]), to place, row `output`; the edge of a `ForwardInput` leaf is dashed and labelled with its source place ([EXP-012])
Inhibitor arc: arrow with circle arrowhead (standard notation) from place to transition, without a label, row `inhibitor`
Read arc: dashed arrow from place to transition, labelled `read`, row `read`
Reset arc: bold arrow from transition to place, labelled `reset`, row `reset`; a reset arc into a place that a leaf of the output spec also ends in is drawn as the combined edge of [EXP-013]
The reset edge points from the transition to the place it empties. This is a drawing convention: the reset arc itself goes from the place to the transition ([CORE-034]).
Visually distinct means that any two edges of different types among these five differ in drawn direction, colour, line style or arrowhead.

The mapper *shall* draw each input arc as a solid edge of arc type `input` from its place to its transition, in the `match-input` row where [EXP-018] correlates its place and in the `input` row otherwise.

The mapper *shall* draw each output arc of a transition into a place that the transition does not reset as an edge of arc type `output` in the `output` row, from the transition or one of its junction nodes to the place.
Every edge of arc type `output` that the mapper draws *shall* run from a transition or one of its junction nodes to a place or to a junction node of that transition, in the `output` row.

An edge of arc type `output` *shall* be solid, except the edge of a `ForwardInput` leaf of its transition's output spec from place F to a place P that the transition does not reset, which is dashed, ends in P and is labelled `⟵F`, after another label and a space when it has one.
The mapper *shall* draw each inhibitor arc as a solid edge of arc type `inhibitor` from its place to its transition, in the `inhibitor` row and without a label.
The mapper *shall* draw each read arc as an edge of arc type `read` from its place to its transition, in the `read` row and labelled `read`.

*Where* no leaf of a transition's output spec ends in the place of one of its reset arcs, the mapper *shall* draw that reset arc as an undashed edge of arc type `reset` from the transition to the place, in the `reset` row and labelled `reset`.

Every edge of arc type `input`, `inhibitor`, `read` or `reset` that the mapper draws *shall* be the edge of one arc of that type, with the ends, row and line style the sentences above give it and the label they give it where they give one; an edge of arc type `reset` is the edge of a reset arc into a place that no leaf of its transition's output spec ends in.
assumes: The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): from a configuration and the export view of a net (ExportNet: declared places, transitions with their core arcs, n-ary output tree, timing, priority and correlated places), the drawn graph (XGraph). An edge (XEdge) has two ends (NodeRef: a transition, a junction of a transition, a place), an arc type, a style row of the edge table (Libpetri.Export.EdgeRow, generated from spec/petri-net-styles.json), a dashed flag that overrides the row's line style, a label and cluster clips. The statement names rows, never colours: the colour, line style, arrowhead and pen width of each row are the generated table (Libpetri.Export.edgeStyle), and the values the runtimes draw are checked against the same JSON by the generator and by tests (kind Q). This is how the second body sentence (each arc type is drawn with the row its bullet names) is read, and why the bullets' words solid, dashed, bold and circle arrowhead are stated as rows: the row input is solid with a normal arrowhead, read dashed, reset bold, inhibitor solid with an odot arrowhead.

The five bullets and the eight shall sentences say the same, line by line: the input bullet and the first shall sentence are line (input); the output bullet and the second to fourth are line (output), whose forward part (the edge of a ForwardInput leaf is dashed and labelled with its source place) is the bullet's last clause and the exception of the fourth; the inhibitor bullet and the fifth are line (inhibitor); the read bullet and the sixth are line (read); the reset bullet and the seventh are line (reset). The eighth shall sentence is the second half of lines (input), (inhibitor), (read) and (reset), and its clause on reset edges is the condition p not a leaf of t in the second half of line (reset); the second half of line (output) is the third shall sentence. The label the sentences give is none for an inhibitor edge, read for a read edge and reset for a reset edge; the input sentence gives none, so the label of an input edge is free here (EXP-006, EXP-018).

Drawn direction (AC2) is the ends of each edge: input, inhibitor and read edges start at a place node and end at the node of the arc's transition; output edges start at the transition's node or one of its junction nodes and end at a place or at one of its junction nodes; reset edges start at the transition's node and end at the place. The reset edge's direction is a drawing convention (the two reset sentences of the body): the glossary's reset arc goes from the place to the transition (ResetArc, CORE-034), and drawing it that way violates the block (EXP_004_forbids_resetReversed).

AC1 (each arc type is visually distinguishable) and the body sentence defining visually distinct are EXP_004_distinguishable, proved from the statement alone: for any exporter that meets EXP-004, two drawn edges whose arc types are two different ones of the five have different looks (exp004Look: whether the edge starts at a place, and the row's style with the line style dashed when the edge is drawn dashed), so they differ in drawn direction, colour, line style or arrowhead without reading a label. Input and output edges share the row style (colour, solid, normal arrowhead) and differ in drawn direction; a dashed output edge differs from a read edge in colour. The first body sentence is the same fact.

Out of scope here: the combined reset+output edge (arc type resetOutput) is EXP-013's subject, and so are its label reset+out and the leaf edge it replaces (which is why the output existence half and the forward part ask only for places the transition does not reset, and the reset existence half only for places no leaf ends in). The rows reset and reset-output have the same style, so the body sentence on the combined edge (it differs from the reset edge only in its label) is an exception to visually distinct that EXP-013 states; this block reads no label for AC1. That a reset arc into a place a leaf ends in gets no standalone reset edge is stated here as the second half of line (reset) and again by EXP-013. Ghost edges (arc type ghost) are EXP-017's. Which output edges are drawn, from which junction and with which label, is EXP-012's: line (output) fixes only arc type, row, drawn direction, that the edge of each ForwardInput leaf is dashed and labelled with its source place, and that no output edge is dashed unless it ends in the target P of a ForwardInput leaf from F of its transition, P a place the transition does not reset, and is labelled with F (so a dashed output edge into a reset place violates the block, EXP_004_forbids_fwdIntoReset). It does not tie that dash to the leaf's own edge (another output edge of the transition into P with the same label may be dashed too), nor require an output edge to end in a leaf place of its transition: the exact drawing, one edge per leaf from its junction, is EXP-012's, which ExportAgrees carries to the exporter. The labels of input edges (cardinality, EXP-006; the correlation prefix, EXP-018) and EXP-018's choice of correlated places are other blocks'; this block fixes the row of a correlated input edge as the bullet says. That every place and transition has a node is EXP-001's; how many edges an arc gets is EXP-001's line 5 for input, inhibitor and read arcs and EXP-013's for output and reset arcs (this block asks for at least one edge per arc and reads no count).

The test derivation (all five arc types, each with a distinct rendering) is EXP_004_nonvacuous on the reference: a transition with two input arcs (one correlated), an Xor output with a Place leaf and a ForwardInput leaf below a Timeout, an inhibitor, a read and a reset arc, whose drawn edges are listed with their ends, arc types, rows, dash and labels. Line and arrowhead values, pen widths and the DOT text are kind Q.

requirements.title: XOR Branch Labels
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (t : String) (R : List String) (o : OutTree),
    o.toOut.isSome = true →
      ∀ cs ∈ exp005XorGroups o,
        ∃ j ∈ (E t R o).junctions,
          j.1 = JKind.xor ∧
            (exp005OutOf (E t R o).edges (NodeRef.junction t JKind.xor j.2)).length =
                cs.length ∧
              ∀
                ec ∈
                  (exp005OutOf (E t R o).edges (NodeRef.junction t JKind.xor j.2)).zip cs,
                (exp005Below (E t R o).edges (E t R o).edges.length ec.1.dst).Perm
                    ec.2.leafPlaces ∧
                  ((branchLabel ec.2).isSome = true →
                    (NodeRef.inPlaces R ec.1.dst = false →
                        (ec.1.dashed, ec.1.label) = exp005Head (branchLabel ec.2) ec.2) ∧
                      (NodeRef.inPlaces R ec.1.dst = true →
                        Option.any (fun s ↦ s != "") ec.1.label = true))
requirements.scope: every exporter, the output side of one transition
reading: For every transition name t, reset places R and output tree o without an empty group (OutTree.toOut o is some), and for every Xor group of o with two or more children cs, at any depth (exp005XorGroups), E draws some xor junction j of t with exactly as many edges out of it as cs has children; the k-th edge out, in the order drawn, is paired with the k-th child c;

the places reached from the end of the k-th edge, following the drawn edges down and counting the paths that end in a place (exp005Below, as deep as E draws edges), are the leaf places of c, one per leaf, up to order (List.Perm);

and when c is a Place, ForwardInput or Timeout child (glossary branchLabel is some), the k-th edge has the dash and the label of the edge EXP-012 draws into c below an Xor junction (exp005Head, from the branch label), unless it ends in a reset place, where its label is some text that is not empty.
quotes: XOR output branches should be labeled to indicate the branching structure.
Each branch of a XOR should be visually identifiable.
The mapper *shall* draw each `Xor` group with two or more children in an output spec as an `Xor` junction node with exactly one edge out of it for each child, in the order of the children.

The mapper *shall* draw the edges below the edge into a child of an `Xor` junction so that following them down reaches the places of that child's leaves, one path into a place for each leaf, and no other place.
The edge into a `Place`, `ForwardInput` or `Timeout` child of an `Xor` junction *shall* carry the label [EXP-012] gives it, and be dashed exactly when [EXP-012] draws it dashed.
*Where* [EXP-013] combines that edge into a reset place, the edge *shall* carry a label that is not empty in place of the one above.
assumes: The model is an output emitter E : Emitter (glossary), as for EXP-012: from a transition name t, its reset places R and its output tree o, the junctions, as (kind, index), and the edges the exporter draws for the output side of t. The block reads the drawn graph only: which edges leave a junction, in the order drawn, where they end, whether they are dashed and what label they carry.

The block is stated over the emitter, not over the exported graph. The glossary agreement ExportAgrees ties an exporter to its emitter: the output edges and the junction nodes of each transition are the emitter's up to order, and the edges out of each junction node are the emitter's in the emitter's order. So the order of the children reaches the exported graph through that agreement in the export consistency theorem, and an exporter that lists the branch edges of an Xor junction in reverse order does not agree with an emitter that meets this block.

Trees with an empty And or Xor group are out of scope (the hypothesis that OutTree.toOut o is some): IO-011 and IO-012 give every group children, and an empty group draws no edge, so its Xor parent has fewer edges than children (EXP-012 draws it so).

Line 1 asks for some xor junction of t for each group, not for one of its own: two groups whose children reach the same places with the same head labels, as two copies of XOR(a, b) under one And, may be shown by one junction. That each group has its own junction, of its kind and no other, that the junction hangs from the transition or from its parent junction by an edge into it, and the number of the junction (EXP-014) are EXP-012's lines, and EXP-012 rejects an emitter that drops the edge into a junction.

"Reach" follows drawn edges from a node to the ends of the edges out of it, stopping at a place, at most as many edges deep as the emitter draws (exp005Below). A path that ends at a node other than a place, such as a junction with no edge out of it, reaches no place and is not counted: line 2 bounds the places reached, and the exact set of edges is EXP-012's line. A place shared by two branches, as in XOR(AND(a, b), AND(a, c)) (IO-012 allows overlapping branches), is reached from both: line 2 compares each branch with its own leaves, not the branches with each other (EXP_005_allows_shared).

The order of the children in line 1 is checked through lines 2 and 3: the k-th edge must reach the leaves of the k-th child and, for a Place, ForwardInput or Timeout child, carry its dash and label, so XOR(Timeout(5, a), a) drawn the other way round is rejected (EXP_005_forbids_reversed_sameLeaves). Two group children that reach the same places are not told apart by this block: in XOR(AND(a, b), AND(b, a)) the picture is the same either way round, and where they differ only below the edge into them, as XOR(AND(Timeout(5, a), b), AND(a, b)), the drawing below that edge is EXP-012's line. Two children whose edges EXP-013 combines into the same reset place both carry its label, so their order is not visible.

Line 3 asks for the dash and label of EXP-012 (exp005Head): for a Place child the place name, solid; for a ForwardInput child to P from F, P, a space and ⟵F, dashed; for a Timeout child the edge into its child as EXP-012 draws it, labelled ⏱<n>ms, or with the label of a Timeout or ForwardInput nested below it. Where EXP-013 combines the edge into a reset place, line 3 asks only for a label that is not empty, an empty label counting as none because the Rust and TypeScript DOT renderers write it as label="", which Graphviz draws as no label; which label and style it is belongs to EXP-013 (reset+out). A group child carries no label of its own and line 3 asks nothing of its edge, including a short group that EXP-012 passes through: in XOR(AND(a), b) the edge into a is unlabelled (EXP_005_allows_shortGroup, ruling D26 item 1).

The four EARS sentences are lines 1, 2 and 3, the Where sentence being the reset place case of line 3. The two body sentences say the same: branches labelled to indicate the structure is line 3, each branch visually identifiable is lines 1, 2 and 3. AC1 (branches have labels or visual grouping) is line 2 (grouping) and line 3 (labels). AC2 (the viewer can identify which outputs belong to which branch) is line 2. The test derivation (a net with an Xor output is exported and its branches are labelled) is EXP_005_nonvacuous.
Shapes, colours and the junction glyph are the exporter's and the style table's (EXP-012, kind Q).

Form: the EARS sentences use 'shall' inside a SHOULD requirement, as IO-016, TIME-015, CONC-023 and EXP-006 do. The priority stays SHOULD; the shall sentences say what an exporter that meets it draws, and the Java, TypeScript and Rust mappers all draw it: they walk the children of a group in order and append one edge per child, with the labels and dashes of EXP-012 (the walk refEmit models).

requirements.title: Cardinality Labels
requirements.statement:
fun L ↦
  L Card.one = none ∧
    (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → L (Card.exactly n) = some ("×" ++ toString n)) ∧
      L Card.all = some "*" ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ), L (Card.atLeast m) = some ("≥" ++ toString m)
requirements.scope: every exporter, on the input arcs of a net (the only arcs with a cardinality)
reading: For the cardinality labeller L of an export (none: no cardinality label):
One has no cardinality label;
for every count n of at least 1, Exactly(n) is labelled ×n;
All is labelled *;
for every minimum m, AtLeast(m) is labelled ≥m.
quotes: Multi-token arcs (Exactly(n), All, AtLeast(m)) display count notation on the arc label:
Exactly(n): label shows "×n"
All: label shows "*"
AtLeast(m): label shows "≥m"
The export *shall* give an input arc with cardinality `One` no cardinality label.
The export *shall* give an input arc with cardinality `Exactly(n)` the cardinality label `×n`.
The export *shall* give an input arc with cardinality `All` the cardinality label `*`.
The export *shall* give an input arc with cardinality `AtLeast(m)` the cardinality label `≥m`.
assumes: The model is the cardinality labeller L : Card → Option String of an export: the cardinality label it gives an input arc, from the arc's cardinality alone, none for no cardinality label. Only input arcs have a cardinality (glossary: Input arc; the output specs of IO-011 to IO-014 carry none), so the opening sentence 'Multi-token arcs (Exactly(n), All, AtLeast(m)) display count notation on the arc label:', which names no arc kind, is read as input arcs, and the four shall sentences name input arcs to say so. Output, inhibitor, read and reset arcs are out of scope. Correlation (EXP-018, NU-020) plays no part in L: the ⟨n⟩ prefix is not a cardinality label.

Where the label is drawn is not encoded here. The sentence 'The export shall draw the cardinality label of an input arc on the edge of the arc.' needs the export model RefExport and is carried by EXP-018's label lines: the label of an uncorrelated input edge of an arc with cardinality c is refCardLabel c, and the label of a correlated one is ⟨n⟩, followed by a space and refCardLabel c when that is a label. The glossary agreement ExportAgrees ties the exporter's input labels to the labeller L of this block in the export consistency theorem. This block alone does not rule out an export that draws no label, or a label other than L's, on an input edge, nor a mapper that writes ⟨n⟩ alone on a correlated Exactly(2) edge (its uncorrelated labeller is the correct one); EXP-018 rejects both (EXP_018_forbids_replace).

'×n' is read as the character × (U+00D7) followed by n in decimal, 'n' as n in decimal alone, '≥m' as ≥ (U+2265) followed by m in decimal, as every runtime writes them (Lean toString on Nat); an ASCII lookalike such as x3 or >=5 is a different label (EXP_006_forbids_ascii). 'No cardinality label' is none: some "" is a label, although DOT draws label="" like no label; no runtime writes it (EXP_006_forbids_emptyOne).

Line 2 ranges over counts of at least 1, since IO-002 defines Exactly(n) only for N >= 1 and its AC1 rejects N < 1, so no export labels Exactly(0). Line 4 has no such guard: IO-004 states no lower bound on the minimum (only the runtimes reject a minimum below 1), so the bullet 'AtLeast(m): label shows ≥m' is taken for every m, AtLeast(0) included; the reference labeller meets it, and a labeller that drops the label of AtLeast(0) violates the block (EXP_006_mutant_atLeastGuard_killed).

Lines 2 and 3 are the forms ruling D41 (a) pins, the ones all three runtimes write (×n, *, ≥m). The spec once allowed a second form for each (bare n for Exactly(n), all for All); that reading is the mutant EXP_006_mutant_eitherForm, and a labeller with the bare forms meets it and violates the block (EXP_006_mutant_eitherForm_killed). A labeller that mixes the forms per value (bare 1 for Exactly(1), ×n for larger counts, all for All) violates line 2 at n = 1 (EXP_006_forbids_mixed).

The opening sentence names Exactly(n) as a multi-token arc for every n; Exactly(1) moves one token and is still labelled, by AC1 ('Non-One cardinality is displayed on the arc') and by every runtime (×1). Line 2 therefore holds at n = 1, and the reading that labels only arcs moving more than one token is a mutant (EXP_006_mutant_multiOnly_killed).

AC1 (non-One cardinality is displayed on the arc) is encoded in its label half by lines 2, 3 and 4: every buildable non-One cardinality has a cardinality label (EXP_006_labels_nonOne). Its 'on the arc' half is EXP-018's label lines (see above).

AC2 (One cardinality has no cardinality label, by default) is line 1. The edge label is not modelled here, so this block does not rule out a One input edge drawn with some other label (for example 1); EXP-018's line 3 does, under which an uncorrelated One edge carries no label. EXP-018 labels a correlated One input edge ⟨n⟩, which is not a cardinality label, so it does not contradict AC2 (ruling D41 (a), clash exp-a#6, clashExport_corrOne). The word 'default' is read as 'the label of an uncorrelated One input edge'; no configuration option of EXP-007 changes the cardinality label in any runtime.
The test derivation (a net with Exactly(3) and AtLeast(5) inputs, labels show the counts) is EXP_006_nonvacuous on the reference labeller: ×3 and ≥5.

requirements.title: Export Configuration
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),
    (E cfg X).dir = cfg.dir ∧
      (∀ (b : Bool),
          E
              { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := b, showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals,
                showPriority := cfg.showPriority, env := cfg.env, cluster := cfg.cluster }
              X =
            E cfg X) ∧
        ∀ (cfg' : ExportCfg),
          cfg.env = cfg'.env →
            cfg.cluster = cfg'.cluster →
              (E cfg X).edges = (E cfg' X).edges ∧
                (E cfg X).clusters = (E cfg' X).clusters ∧
                  (E cfg X).compound = (E cfg' X).compound ∧
                    List.map XNode.eraseTransLabel (E cfg X).nodes =
                      List.map XNode.eraseTransLabel (E cfg' X).nodes
reading: For the exporter E, every configuration cfg and every net X:
the drawing E cfg X has the layout direction of cfg;
for every value b, E draws X under cfg with show-types set to b exactly as under cfg;

for every configuration cfg' with the environment places and cluster source of cfg, E cfg X and E cfg' X have the same edges, the same clusters, the same compound attribute, and the same nodes once the label inside each transition node is blanked.
quotes: The export supports configuration options:
**Layout direction**: top-to-bottom, left-to-right, etc.
The export *shall* lay out the drawing in the layout direction the configuration names.

The export *shall* draw the same graph, apart from its layout direction and the label drawn inside each transition node, under two configurations that differ only in the layout direction and the show options.
*Where* a configuration carries a show-types option, the export *shall* draw the same graph whichever value the option has.
The default configuration names the top-to-bottom layout direction and shows timing and priority.
assumes: The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): the drawn graph (glossary XGraph: layout direction, compound attribute, nodes, edges and clusters) of a configuration and a net. Line 3 compares two configurations that agree on the environment places and the cluster source, which the configuration also carries (EXP-008 and EXP-016 read them), so they differ only in the layout direction and the three show options; they have the same edges, clusters and compound attribute, and their nodes are compared after XNode.eraseTransLabel, which blanks the inner label of a transition node and keeps every other field (identity, category, external label) and every other node. So the graph is compared field by field except for the layout direction, which line 1 fixes per configuration. Lists are compared with their order: no option changes the order in any runtime. What the transition labels are is the label block, joined to E by the second clause of ExportAgrees.

Line 2 is the show-types sentence, which is ruling D41 (a): the option stays in the configuration types of all three runtimes (Rust DotConfig.show_types, Java ExportConfig.showTypes, TypeScript DotConfig.showTypes) and no mapper reads it, so the 'Show/hide types' bullet is dropped and the sentence says the option changes nothing. A mapper that lets show-types hide the timing and priority of transition labels meets line 3, which allows label changes, and violates line 2 (EXP_007_forbids_typesHide); a mapper that ignores the direction violates line 1 (EXP_007_forbids_fixedDir); a mapper that also drops the timeout labels of output edges when timing is hidden violates line 3 (EXP_007_forbids_hideTimeoutLabels), and so does one that sets the compound attribute from a show option (EXP_007_forbids_compoundFlag).

The 'etc.' of the layout direction bullet is the four directions every runtime has (glossary RankDir: TB, LR, BT, RL; Rust graph RankDir, Java export.graph.RankDir, TypeScript RankDir); line 1 holds for each. The DOT text is not modelled: that the rankdir attribute of the DOT text carries the typed graph's direction (the renderers' RankDir tables, TB, LR, BT and RL each to itself) is kind Q, checked by the renderer tests.

The default sentence states no export behaviour: it describes the configuration type, so an exporter cannot break it and the statement has no line for it. The glossary's default ExportCfg is TB with timing and priority shown (EXP_007_default, which cites the sentence), as are Rust DotConfig::default(), Java ExportConfig.DEFAULT and TypeScript DEFAULT_DOT_CONFIG; that the runtime defaults match the glossary is checked by their tests, not here. What the export does under the default is line 1 and the label block at cfg = {}: the drawing is top to bottom (EXP_007_config_nonvacuous) and transition labels carry the interval and the non-zero priority (EXP_007_label_nonvacuous).

AC1 (configuration controls what information is displayed) is line 1 for the direction and the label block for the transition labels; line 3 says the show options change nothing else in the drawn graph (edges, clusters, compound attribute and every node field but the inner transition label). AC2 (default configuration shows all information) is the default sentence together with line 1 and the label block's lines 2 and 4 at the default. AC3 (minimal configuration hides timing and priority) is the label block's line 1; the preset name is kind N (Java only). The test derivation is EXP_007_config_nonvacuous: the worked net of EXP-013 under the default configuration and with timing and priority hidden, same edges, transition labels RefreshCache [1, 5]ms prio=3 against RefreshCache.

requirements.title: Export Configuration, the transition label
requirements.statement:
fun TL ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (name : String) (τ : Novel.TimedScg.Timing) (n : ℤ),
    (cfg.showIntervals = false → cfg.showPriority = false → TL cfg name τ n = name) ∧
      (cfg.showIntervals = true →
          cfg.showPriority = false →
            TL cfg name τ n =
              (name ++ " [" ++ toString τ.earliest ++ ", " ++
                  if τ.hasDeadline = true then toString τ.latest else "∞") ++
                "]ms") ∧
        (n = 0 →
            TL cfg name τ n =
              TL
                { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := cfg.showTypes,
                  showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals, showPriority := false,
                  env := cfg.env, cluster := cfg.cluster }
                name τ n) ∧
          (cfg.showPriority = true →
            n ≠ 0 →
              TL cfg name τ n =
                TL
                      { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := cfg.showTypes,
                        showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals, showPriority := false,
                        env := cfg.env, cluster := cfg.cluster }
                      name τ n ++
                    " prio=" ++
                  toString n)
requirements.scope: every exporter, the label of a transition node
reading: For the transition labeller TL of an export, every configuration cfg, transition name, timing τ and priority n:
with timing and priority hidden, the label is the name;
with timing shown and priority hidden, the label is the name, then ' [e, l]ms' with e = earliest τ, and l = latest τ when τ has a deadline, else ∞;
when n is 0, the label is the label under cfg with priority hidden;
with priority shown and n not 0, the label is the label under cfg with priority hidden, then ' prio=n'.
quotes: **Show/hide timing**: toggle timing interval display on transitions
**Show/hide priority**: toggle priority display on transitions
*Where* the configuration hides timing and priority, the export *shall* label a transition node with the transition's name alone.

*Where* the configuration shows timing and hides priority, the export *shall* label a transition node with the transition's name, a space and `[e, l]ms`, where e is `earliest()` and l is `latest()` of the transition's timing, in milliseconds and in decimal, and l is written `∞` when `hasDeadline()` is false ([TIME-001]).

*Where* the configuration shows priority and the transition's priority n is not 0, the export *shall* label the transition's node with the label it would have if the configuration hid priority, followed by a space and `prio=n`, with n in decimal.
*Where* a transition's priority is 0, the export *shall* label its node with the label it would have if the configuration hid priority.
assumes: The model is a transition labeller TL : TransLabeller (glossary): the label of a transition node from the export configuration (glossary ExportCfg), the transition's name, its timing (the Timing of TIME-001: earliest, latest, hasDeadline, in whole milliseconds) and its priority. That every transition node of a drawn graph carries this label is the second clause of ExportAgrees, which the export consistency theorem takes; that the label starts with the name is EXP-003's line. ExportAgrees constrains only nets with X.Distinct (distinct transition names, at most one input arc per place), so the four sentences reach the drawing of such nets only; on a net with two transitions of one name the label of each node is left open, as in the other export blocks (the W4 shape).

The four lines determine the label for every configuration: EXP_007_label_determined shows that refTransLabel is the only labeller that meets the block. So the show-types option, the layout direction, the environment places and the cluster source never change a transition label. This is the label half of the show-types sentence of the config block (ruling D41 (a)); a labeller that reads show-types as a master switch for the whole label violates line 2 (EXP_007_forbids_typesMaster).

Numbers are written as Lean's toString writes Nat and Int: decimal digits, a minus sign before a negative priority (t [7, ∞]ms prio=-1), and ∞ is U+221E. A timing without a deadline is labelled with ∞ and never with its latest() value MAX_DURATION_MS (rulings D2 and D11: the label reads hasDeadline by timing variant); a mapper that prints the maximum is killed (EXP_007_forbids_printsMax). Java's Unconstrained timing, which the Lean Timing lacks, has earliest 0 and no deadline, so the same sentence labels it [0, ∞]ms. Sub-millisecond durations are out of scope: the model's durations are whole milliseconds, Java prints toMillis() and TypeScript the raw number.

The parts are in the order name, interval, priority, each after one space; a mapper that writes the priority before the interval violates line 4 (EXP_007_forbids_prioFirst). A mapper that ignores the hide-timing option violates line 1 (EXP_007_forbids_alwaysInterval), and one that writes prio=0 violates line 3 (EXP_007_forbids_prioZero).

AC1 (configuration controls what information is displayed) is these four lines for the transition label, and line 1 and line 3 of the config block for the rest of the drawing. AC2 (default configuration shows all information) is lines 2 and 4 at the default configuration: the interval of every transition, Immediate included as [0, ∞]ms, and the priority when it is not 0 (EXP_007_label_nonvacuous); token types are never drawn (ruling D41 (a)), so they are not part of all information. AC3 (minimal configuration hides timing and priority) is line 1 (export design, skeptic correction S-5): with timing and priority hidden the label is the bare name. The name 'minimal configuration' is kind N: only Java has such a preset (ExportConfig.minimal()), so the block quantifies over configurations instead.

The test derivation (export with the default and with the minimal configuration, verify the difference) is EXP_007_label_nonvacuous: t [5, 10]ms prio=3 under the default against t when timing and priority are hidden.

requirements.title: Styling
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] C ↦
  ∀ (X : Reference.Net N) (env term : N → Bool) (p : N),
    (term p = true → C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.terminal) ∧
      (term p = false → env p = true → C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.environment) ∧
        (term p = false →
          env p = false →
            (C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.start ↔ HasOutputArc X p = false) ∧
              (HasOutputArc X p = true →
                  HasInputArc X p = false →
                    HasReadArc X p = false → C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.end) ∧
                (HasInputArc X p = true → C X env term p ≠ Export.NodeCat.end) ∧
                  (C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.start ∨
                      C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.end ∨
                        C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.place) ∧
                    (HasOutputArc X p = true →
                      HasInputArc X p = false →
                        HasReadArc X p = true →
                          ∀ (X' : Reference.Net N) (env' term' : N → Bool) (p' : N),
                            term' p' = false →
                              env' p' = false →
                                HasOutputArc X' p' = true →
                                  HasInputArc X' p' = false →
                                    HasReadArc X' p' = true →
                                      C X' env' term' p' = C X env term p))
requirements.scope: every exporter's mapper, on the place nodes of a net (before a documentation generator restyles interface ports)
reading: For the place classifier C, every net X with environment places env and terminal places term, and every place p:
a terminal place is terminal;
an environment place that is not terminal is environment;
for a place that is neither (an ordinary place): it is start exactly when no transition has an output arc on it;
it is end when some transition has an output arc on it and none has an input arc or a read arc on it;
it is not end when some transition has an input arc on it;
it is start, end or the regular place row;

and if some transition has an output arc on it, some has a read arc on it and none has an input arc on it, then every ordinary place p' of every net X' (with any env' and term') of which the same holds gets the same row as p.
quotes: The export applies visual styling to distinguish node categories:
The export *shall* give a terminal place the terminal category.
The export *shall* give an environment place that is not a terminal place the environment category.
The export *shall* give an ordinary place the start category exactly when no transition's output spec names it.
The export *shall* give the end category to an ordinary place that some transition's output spec names and on which no transition has an input arc or a read arc.
The export *shall not* give the end category to an ordinary place on which some transition has an input arc.
The export *shall* give an ordinary place the start, the end or the regular place category.

The export *shall* give the same category to all ordinary places, in one net or in different nets, that some transition's output spec names, on which some transition has a read arc and on which no transition has an input arc.
assumes: The model is a place classifier C : PlaceClassifier N: the node row (glossary of the style table, Libpetri.Export.NodeCat) the export's mapper gives place p of net X, given the environment places env (ENV-001) and the terminal places term (EXEC-042) as predicates. C reads only the arcs of X, as every runtime's analysis does (analyze_places in the Rust crate libpetri-export, PlaceAnalysis.java, analyzePlaces in petri-net-mapper.ts); the marking, the timing and the configuration play no part. Lines 1 to 6 fix C from the arc kinds on p in every case but one, and line 7 makes that one case, too, the same answer for every place and every net, so C reads no more of X than whether p has an output arc, an input arc and a read arc. That the exporter draws each place node with the row C gives, and that a place row is not a transition shape, is EXP-002's join line on the export model (RefExport, wave W4), cited there; this block does not see the graph.

C is the mapper's classification, the one the production export pipeline gives. The three documentation generators (SubnetDotExport.java, subnet-dot-export.ts, and the Rust subnet_dot_export module; compile-time diagrams, EXP-011) afterwards rewrite the DOT of a subnet body and redraw its interface-port places with the interface-port row; that rewrite is a later step on the DOT text, not C's answer, and is out of scope. The markdown says so in the sentence after the bullets. A mapper that gives an ordinary place the interface-port row itself violates line 6 (EXP_008_forbids_otherRow).

Which places get a node at all is EXP-001's subject (ruling D60): Rust draws every declared place, Java and TypeScript only places some arc touches. Line 3 gives a place that no arc touches the start category, which is what Rust draws; Java and TypeScript draw no node for it, so their answer for it is never seen (PlaceAnalysis.category answers place for an unknown name). The reference classifier answers start, as Rust does.
