The words 'incoming' and 'outgoing' of the body bullets ('no incoming arcs', 'no outgoing arcs') are read as the markdown's sentence after the bullets defines them, which is how all three runtimes count: an incoming arc of a place is an output arc of some transition on it (glossary: Output arc, the target of a ForwardInput included), and an input arc on it is an outgoing arc. Whether a read arc is an outgoing arc is the open case of ruling D51 (next assumption). Inhibitor arcs and reset arcs count as neither, although the glossary draws them from the place to the transition and the reset edge of EXP-004 and EXP-013 is drawn from the transition to the place (clash exp-a#5 and exp-a#9): a classifier that counts them as outgoing violates line 4 (EXP_008_forbids_glossaryDirections), one that counts a reset arc as incoming violates line 3 (EXP_008_forbids_resetIncoming).

Ruling D51 (a): the common form of 'end place'. A place that an output spec names, on which no transition has an input arc and some transition has a read arc, is regular in Java and TypeScript (a read arc counts as outgoing) and end in Rust (only input arcs count). Lines 4 and 5 hold of both shapes and leave that place open (EXP_008_readOnly_open); the Rust shape is an allowed classifier (EXP_008_allows_inputsOnly). The case is open per classifier, not per place: line 7 says a classifier answers it the same way for every such place of every net, so a mix of the two shapes is rejected, whether the answer hangs on whether the reader writes elsewhere (EXP_008_forbids_readByWriter) or on whether the reader is the place's own writer (EXP_008_forbids_selfReadSkipped). The end state of D51, that a read arc keeps a place from being an end place, is the reference classifier's answer; the later line that makes line 4 an 'exactly when' with read arcs counted waits for the Rust mapper to change and is not encoded. The markdown records the open case and the intended answer in a sentence without shall.

The precedence terminal, environment, start, end is all three runtimes' (ruling D51) and is lines 1 to 3 and 6: a terminal environment place is terminal (EXP_008_forbids_envFirst), an environment place no output spec names is environment, not start (EXP_008_forbids_startFirst), and a place with no arcs at all is start, not end (EXP_008_forbids_endFirst). EXEC-042 builds reject a terminal place with an input or read arc, which the precedence does not need.

AC1 (start places are visually distinct from other places) and AC2 (end places are visually distinct from other places) are read on the style table: the start row and the end row each differ from every other place row and from the transition row (EXP_008_rows_distinct, decided on the generated table), and lines 1 to 7 decide which places get the start and the end row. Until EXP-002's join line lands (wave W4), nothing ties the drawn style to C, so AC1 and AC2 are accounted for here but not yet proven; EXP_008_rows_distinct carries no evidence tag for that reason, and the W4 block for EXP-002 closes the dependency. The colours of the body bullets ('e.g., green', 'e.g., blue', 'e.g., yellow') are examples; the values are the table's and are checked by the runtimes' tests, not here. The bullet on transitions (a distinct colour) is the transition row's difference from the place rows in EXP_008_rows_distinct; that transitions are drawn with the transition row is EXP-003's subject.

The test derivation (a net with start and end places, export, styling applied) is EXP_008_nonvacuous on the reference classifier: a net with a start, a regular, an end, an environment, a terminal and an inhibitor-only place.

Out of scope: the rows of composition (interface-port, sync-channel), which only the documentation generators' rewrite of a subnet diagram uses (see the second assumption; MOD-040 and EXP-016 add grouping only), and the rows of junctions (EXP-012), which are synthetic nodes, not place nodes; ν correlation (NU-020, EXP-018) changes no place category. Places are compared by identity (DecidableEq N); export IDs and sanitising are EXP-014's (ruling D46).

requirements.title: XOR/AND Junction Nodes
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (t : String) (R : List String) (o : OutTree),
    ∃ ρ,
      (∀ (i j : ℕ), ρ i = ρ j → i = j) ∧
        (List.map (fun kj ↦ (kj.1, ρ kj.2)) (E t R o).junctions).Perm o.junctions.zipIdx ∧
          (List.map (XEdge.seen R ρ) (E t R o).edges).Perm
            (List.map (DrawnEdge.seen R) (Drawing t o))
requirements.scope: every exporter, the output side of one transition
reading: For every transition name t, reset places R and output tree o (any tree, short and empty groups included), there is a one-to-one renumbering ρ of the junction indices the emitter E uses, such that:
the junctions E draws, renumbered, are the groups of o with two or more children, one junction each, of the group's kind (OutTree.junctions), in any order;

the edges E draws, renumbered, are the edges of the drawing rule (Drawing t o), one each, in any order: both ends of every edge, and for every edge that does not end in a reset place also its arc type output, style row output, dash and label as the rule gives them.
quotes: For every `Out.Xor` or `Out.And` group with **two or more children**, the mapper MUST insert a synthetic *junction node* between the transition and the children.
A group with fewer than two children MUST NOT produce a junction (it is a pass-through).
The mapper *shall* draw one junction node for each `And` or `Xor` group of an output spec that has two or more children, of the group's kind, and no other junction node.
*Where* an `And` or `Xor` group has fewer than two children, the mapper *shall* draw its child, if it has one, from the group's parent and with the label the edge into the group would carry.

The mapper *shall* draw exactly one solid output edge into each junction node, into the place of each `Place` leaf and into the target place of each `ForwardInput` leaf, from the nearest junction node above it, or from the transition when there is none, and no other edge for the output spec.
The edge into a child of an `Xor` junction *shall* carry the child's branch label: the place name of a `Place` child, `⏱<n>ms` for a `Timeout` child of n ms, and no label for an `And` or `Xor` child.
The edge into a child of an `And` junction, and the edge from the transition into the output spec, *shall* carry no label of their own.
*Where* a `Timeout` node of n ms is in an output spec, the edge drawn into its child *shall* carry `⏱<n>ms` in place of the label the edge into the `Timeout` would carry.

*Where* a leaf is a `ForwardInput` from place F to place P, the mapper *shall* draw its edge as the edge of a `Place` leaf for P at the same position, dashed instead of solid, and with `⟵F` after its label and a space, or as its only label when it has none.
*Where* [EXP-013] combines a leaf edge into a reset place, that edge *shall* take the arc type, label and style [EXP-013] gives it in place of the ones above.
assumes: The model is an output emitter E : Emitter (glossary): from a transition name t, its reset places R and its output tree o (glossary OutTree: n-ary And and Xor groups, a Timeout with its duration in ms, Place and ForwardInput leaves), the junctions, as (kind, index), and the edges (glossary XEdge: ends, arc type, style row, dash, label) the exporter draws for the output side of t. The input, inhibitor, read and standalone reset edges and the place and transition nodes are drawn outside the emitter and are other blocks' subject (EXP-001 to EXP-004, EXP-013).

The drawing rule Drawing t o is the glossary's drawOut from the transition, with no inherited label, junctions numbered from 0, one clause per sentence: a group with two or more children gives one junction of its kind and one solid output edge into it from the parent with the inherited label, then its children below it (the first and third shall sentences); a shorter group gives no junction and draws its children from the parent with the inherited label (the second); a Place leaf gives one solid edge into its place from the parent with the inherited label (the third); below an Xor junction a child inherits its branch label (glossary branchLabel), below an And junction and from the transition nothing (the fourth and fifth); a Timeout hands its child the label ⏱<n>ms in place of the inherited one (the sixth); a ForwardInput leaf from F into P is the Place leaf for P, dashed, labelled forwardLabel (⟵F after the inherited label and a space, or ⟵F alone) (the seventh). The two body sentences that open the section say what the first two shall sentences say.

Junction indices are compared up to a one-to-one renumbering ρ: which index each junction gets (pre-order from 0) is EXP-014's line, so an emitter that numbers its junctions in post-order still meets this block. The renumbering must be one to one, so an emitter that draws the edge into a junction at one index and the edges out of it at another (two nodes in the graph for one group) violates the block (EXP_012_forbids_split).

Order is not stated: the junctions and edges are compared as lists up to permutation (List.Perm), membership and multiplicity only. Node and edge order across languages is open ruling R2 (exp-b) and kind Q; the order of an Xor junction's children is EXP-005's line.

The last shall sentence is the guard of the third line: for an edge that ends in a place of R only its two ends are compared, and its arc type, style row, label and dash are EXP-013's. Its ends and the count, one edge per leaf, still bind, so an emitter that draws a combined edge next to an output edge for one leaf violates this block.

The block quantifies over every output tree, including a group with fewer than two children (Rust's Out::Xor is a public variant and a TypeScript node a plain object, so a short Xor reaches the mappers' pass-through arm), an empty group (no junction and no edge, as all three mappers draw it) and a ForwardInput below an Xor junction, which no transition that builds has (IO-013, IO-014): the seventh shall sentence draws it as the Place leaf for its target, so its label is the target name, a space and ⟵F, which is what all three mappers draw.

The junction node attributes (shape diamond, fill, stroke, pen width, size, the glyphs ✕ and ✚, font size, fixed size) and the node categories xor-junction and and-junction belong to the exporter's nodes and the style table (Libpetri.Export.Styles, JKind.cat), not to the emitter: the category line of a junction node is a later line of the exporter blocks in wave W4, and the constants are checked by tests (kind Q).

AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 are EXP_012_nonvacuous on the reference emitter: XOR(P_a, P_b) gives one xor junction and the edges junction to P_a and junction to P_b; AND(P_c, P_d) one and junction and two edges; AND(P_a) a direct edge from the transition to P_a and no junction (AC3 is stated with AND by ruling D26 item 1, since IO-012 gives every Xor two or more children); XOR(AND(P_a, P_b), P_c) an and junction nested below the xor junction. Their junction attributes (diamond, ✕, ✚) are the exporter's, as above.

AC5 (Java, TypeScript and Rust mappers produce byte-identical junction nodes and edges) is kind Q: a Lean function is deterministic and cross-language equality is a property of three programs (export design P3, ruling D60 (c)); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration. The test derivation is AC1 to AC4.

requirements.title: Combined reset+output Edge
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),
    ((List.map ExportTrans.name X.trans).Nodup →
        ∀ t ∈ X.trans,
          ∀ (P : String),
            (P ∈ t.core.resets →
                ∀ e ∈ exp013OutInto (E cfg X) t.name P,
                  e.arc = ArcType.resetOutput ∧
                    e.row = Export.EdgeRow.resetOutput ∧
                      e.dashed = false ∧ e.label = some "reset+out") ∧
              (P ∈ t.core.resets →
                  P ∈ t.outLeaves → exp013ResetInto (E cfg X) t.name P = []) ∧
                (P ∈ t.core.resets →
                    P ∉ t.outLeaves →
                      (exp013ResetInto (E cfg X) t.name P).length =
                          List.count P t.core.resets ∧
                        ∀ e ∈ exp013ResetInto (E cfg X) t.name P,
                          e.src = NodeRef.trans t.name ∧
                            e.row = Export.EdgeRow.reset ∧
                              e.dashed = false ∧ e.label = some "reset") ∧
                  (P ∉ t.core.resets →
                      ∀ e ∈ exp013OutInto (E cfg X) t.name P,
                        e.arc = ArcType.output ∧ e.row = Export.EdgeRow.output) ∧
                    (exp013OutInto (E cfg X) t.name P).length =
                      List.count P t.outLeaves) ∧
      ∀ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
        e.arc = ArcType.resetOutput →
          ∃ t ∈ X.trans,
            e.src.owner? = some t.name ∧ ∃ P ∈ t.core.resets, e.dst = NodeRef.place P
requirements.scope: every exporter, the edges of one transition into one place
reading: For every configuration cfg and net X, in the graph E cfg X, when the transitions of X have distinct names, for every transition t of X and every place name P:

if t resets P, every output-side edge of t into P (exp013OutInto: arc type output or resetOutput, from the node of t or one of its junctions, into the node of P) has arc type resetOutput, style row resetOutput, is not dashed and is labelled reset+out;
if t resets P and a leaf of t's output spec ends in P, there is no reset edge of t into P (exp013ResetInto);

if t resets P and no leaf of t's output spec ends in P, the reset edges of t into P are as many as t's reset arcs on P, and each starts at the node of t, has style row reset, is not dashed and is labelled reset;
if t does not reset P, every output-side edge of t into P has arc type output and style row output;
the output-side edges of t into P are as many as the leaves of t's output spec that end in P (t.outLeaves, a ForwardInput leaf counted by its target);

and, whatever the names of the transitions, every edge of the graph of arc type resetOutput starts at the node of some transition t of X or one of its junctions and ends at the node of a place t resets.
quotes: When a transition has both an output arc and a reset arc to the same place P, the mapper MUST draw every output edge to P as a combined edge, styled as the reset-output category (color `#fd7e14`, style `bold`, penwidth `2.0`, arrowhead `normal`) and labelled `"reset+out"`.
The standalone output edge to P MUST be suppressed in this case.
The standalone reset edge to P MUST be suppressed in this case.
When the output spec names P in more than one leaf (for example `Xor(P, And(P, Q))`), each such leaf gives one combined edge.
If a transition resets place P but does not output to P, the standalone reset edge with label `"reset"` MUST still be emitted (existing behavior preserved).
If a transition outputs to P but does not reset P, the standalone output edge MUST be emitted (existing behavior preserved).
The combination applies regardless of whether the output edge originates at the transition directly or at an XOR/AND junction underneath the transition (per EXP-012).
When the output is a leaf under a junction, the *junction → P* edge is the one that becomes reset-styled with the `"reset+out"` label.

The combined edge carries the label `"reset+out"` alone and is never dashed: it replaces the branch label, the timeout label and the `ForwardInput` label and dash the leaf edge would carry under [EXP-012].

*Where* the transitions of a net have pairwise distinct names and a transition of the net resets place P, each edge the mapper draws for a `Place` leaf for P or a `ForwardInput` leaf into P of its output spec *shall* be an undashed edge of arc type reset-output, in the reset-output style and labelled `reset+out`, whether it starts at the transition or at a junction node.

*Where* the transitions of a net have pairwise distinct names, a transition of the net resets place P and its output spec has a `Place` leaf for P or a `ForwardInput` leaf into P, the mapper *shall* draw no reset edge from that transition to P.

*Where* the transitions of a net have pairwise distinct names, a transition of the net resets place P and its output spec has no `Place` leaf for P and no `ForwardInput` leaf into P, the mapper *shall* draw one undashed reset edge from the transition to P for each reset arc of the transition on P, in the reset style and labelled `reset`.

*Where* the transitions of a net have pairwise distinct names and a transition of the net does not reset place P, each edge the mapper draws for a `Place` leaf for P or a `ForwardInput` leaf into P of its output spec *shall* be of arc type output, in the output style.

*Where* the transitions of a net have pairwise distinct names, for each transition and place P the mapper *shall* draw exactly as many edges of arc type output or reset-output from the transition and its junction nodes into P as the transition's output spec has `Place` leaves for P and `ForwardInput` leaves into P.
The mapper *shall* draw every edge of arc type reset-output from a transition or one of its junction nodes into a place that transition resets.
assumes: The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): from a configuration and the export view of a net (ExportNet: declared places, transitions in declaration order with their input, inhibitor, read and reset arcs and their n-ary output tree), the typed graph a mapper builds before DOT text. The block reads only its edges: the output-side edges and the reset edges of one transition into one place, and the edges of arc type resetOutput of the whole graph. The edges of a transition are found by their ends (the node of t or a junction of t), and the exporter keys transition nodes by name, so the five per-transition lines, like the five EARS sentences they encode, bind only nets whose transition names are pairwise distinct: with two transitions named T, each with Out.Place(P), every mapper draws two edges from t_T into p_P where each transition has one leaf. The sixth line needs no such condition and binds every net. Ghost edges between clusters (EXP-017) have their own arc type and are in none of the three.

Which leaves end in P is read off the output tree: a Place leaf for P and a ForwardInput leaf into P (t.outLeaves). Which edge belongs to which leaf, where each edge starts (the transition or the nearest junction above the leaf, so the junction edge of the sentence on a leaf under a junction) and the order of the edges are EXP-012's lines, carried to the exporter by the agreement ExportAgrees; this block fixes their number per place and their arc type, style row, dash and label. The combined edge is never dashed and carries reset+out alone, so it replaces the branch label of an Xor child, the timeout label and the ForwardInput label and dash (ruling D26 item 3), which is the last shall sentence of EXP-012. The sixth line keeps the combined style off every other edge: an edge into a junction (the parent edge of a group, an output edge of EXP-012) and an edge from the place back to the transition are never of arc type resetOutput.

For an edge into a place t does not reset, this block fixes the arc type output and the style row output: that is the black output edge of AC2 and the plain output style of AC4, whose colour is a constant of the style table. Its label and dash (the branch label Q of AC4, a timeout label, the ForwardInput label and dash) are EXP-012's, and that the row of an output edge is output is also EXP-004's output line.

An output spec may name P in more than one leaf (Xor(P, And(P, Q)) builds: its branches differ). Then all three mappers draw one combined edge per leaf, and the first line and the fifth line say so (ruling D26 item 4: every output edge to P becomes a reset+out edge).

A transition may hold two reset arcs on one place (the TypeScript and Rust builders append without removing duplicates); the third line then asks for one standalone reset edge per arc, as all three mappers draw them. That a reset arc is drawn transition to place is the drawing convention of all three mappers (EXP-004).

The style rows name the rows of the style table (Libpetri.Export.Styles, generated from spec/petri-net-styles.json): the colour #fd7e14, the bold line, the pen width 2.0 and the arrowhead of the reset-output and reset rows are constants of that table, checked by tests (kind Q). The worked DOT of the section is illustrative: its four edges are among refExportFlat_example_edges (Reference/Export.lean) at the level of IDs, arc types and labels, where the example net has further arcs (two input arcs, an inhibitor arc, a read arc and a reset arc on a second place) and the edges come in declaration order, those of Try before those of RefreshCache.

AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 are EXP_013_nonvacuous on the reference exporter: Out.Place(P) with reset(P) gives one reset+out edge from the transition and no reset edge; Out.Place(P) without a reset one plain output edge; reset(P) without an output to P one reset edge labelled reset; Out.Xor(P, Q) with reset(P) a combined edge from the junction to P and a plain edge, labelled Q, from the junction to Q.

AC5 (Java, TypeScript and Rust mappers produce byte-identical edges) is kind Q: a Lean function is deterministic and cross-language equality is a property of three programs (export design P3, ruling D60 (c)); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration. The test derivation is AC1 to AC4.

requirements.title: Junction ID Format and Layout Stability
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),
    (∀ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes, AsciiName n.ref.refName → n.id = nodeId n.ref) ∧
      ((List.map ExportTrans.name X.trans).Nodup →
          ∀ t ∈ X.trans,
            ((E cfg X).junctionsOf t.name).Perm
              ((Option.map OutTree.junctions t.out).getD []).zipIdx) ∧
        ((List.map ExportTrans.name X.trans).Nodup →
            ∀ t ∈ X.trans,
              (List.map (fun e ↦ (e.src, e.dst)) ((E cfg X).outEdges t.name)).Perm
                (List.map (fun d ↦ (d.src, d.dst))
                  ((Option.map (Drawing t.name) t.out).getD []))) ∧
          (∀ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
              ∀ (u : String) (k : JKind) (i : ℕ),
                e.src = NodeRef.junction u k i ∨ e.dst = NodeRef.junction u k i →
                  ∃ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes, n.ref = NodeRef.junction u k i) ∧
            ((List.map ExportTrans.name X.trans).Nodup →
                X.IdNames → (List.map XNode.id (E cfg X).nodes).Nodup) ∧
              ∀ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,
                ∀ m ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,
                  n.ref.isJunction = true → m.ref.isJunction = false → n.id ≠ m.id
requirements.scope: every exporter, the DOT IDs and junction numbering of the exported graph
reading: For every configuration cfg and net X, the graph E cfg X satisfies:

every node whose name (the place's, the transition's, or for a junction its transition's) is ASCII has the ID nodeId of what it stands for: p_<sanitize p>, t_<sanitize t> or j_<sanitize t>__<kind>_<idx>, the index in decimal without leading zeros;

on a net with pairwise distinct transition names, the junction nodes of each transition t, as (kind, index), are the kinds of the groups of t's output spec with two or more children in depth-first pre-order, numbered 0, 1, 2 in that order, one node per group and no other, in any order of drawing (List.Perm);

on such a net, the output side of each transition t (its output and reset+output edges from t or a junction of t), as (source, target) pairs, is the drawing rule of EXP-012 for t's output spec with these junction numbers (Drawing, no renumbering), each pair as often as Drawing has it, in any order;
every junction an edge starts or ends at is the reference of a node of the graph;
on such a net whose names meet the name assumption (ExportNet.IdNames: ASCII place and transition names, pairwise distinct after sanitize), the node IDs are pairwise distinct;
for every net, whatever its names, no junction node has the ID of a node that is not a junction (a place or a transition node).
quotes: Synthetic junction nodes MUST use IDs of the form `j_<transitionSanitized>__<kind>_<idx>`, where:
`transitionSanitized` is the transition's name with non-`[A-Za-z0-9_]` characters replaced by `_` (the same `sanitize` function used for place and transition IDs).
`<kind>` is `xor` or `and`.

`<idx>` is a non-negative integer. Junctions in a single transition's `Out` tree are numbered in depth-first pre-order, with the counter starting at `0` and incrementing once per emitted junction. Single-child XOR/AND groups collapse (per EXP-012) and consume no counter slot. Example: `t_Nested` with output `AND(XOR(a,b), XOR(c,d))` produces three junctions in the order `j_Nested__and_0`, `j_Nested__xor_1`, `j_Nested__xor_2`.
Junction IDs do not collide with place IDs (`p_…`) or transition IDs (`t_…`).

*Where* a node's name (the place's, the transition's, or for a junction its transition's) holds only ASCII characters, the mapper *shall* give the node the ID `p_<s>`, `t_<s>` or `j_<s>__<kind>_<idx>` according to what it stands for, with `<s>` that name with each character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` replaced by `_`, `<kind>` the kind of the junction and `<idx>` its index written in decimal without leading zeros.
The ID of a node whose name holds a character outside ASCII is implementation-defined, within the rule of the next sentence.
The mapper *shall* give no junction node the ID of a place node or a transition node, whatever the names.

*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, the mapper *shall* draw for each transition one junction node for each group with two or more children in its output spec, of the kind of that group, and no other junction node for the transition.

*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, the mapper *shall* give the junction node of a group with two or more children the index of that group in the depth-first pre-order of such groups in the transition's output spec, counting from 0, with one counter for both kinds.

*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, the mapper *shall* draw as the output edges of a transition, compared by their ends, exactly the edges [EXP-012] draws for its output spec, each as often as [EXP-012] draws it, with each junction numbered by the index of its group.
The mapper *shall* draw no edge that starts or ends at a junction node it does not draw.

*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, its place and transition names hold only ASCII characters, and no two different place names, nor two different transition names, become equal when each character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` is replaced by `_`, the mapper *shall* give no two nodes of the graph the same ID.
AC1 covers the junctions of transitions whose name is not empty and holds only ASCII characters.
assumes: The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): the typed graph (nodes with reference, ID, category and labels; edges; clusters) a configuration and a net are drawn as, before DOT text. The node references (place, transition, junction (t, kind, index)) are the graph's own data; this block constrains the IDs it gives them, the junction indices and kinds it uses and the ends of the output edges. Every other attribute of a node or edge is another block's subject (EXP-001 to EXP-013).

The ID function is the glossary's nodeId over sanitize, which keeps an ASCII letter, digit or underscore and replaces every other character by an underscore, and writes the index with toString (decimal, no leading zeros). By ruling D46 (a) the first line binds only nodes whose name is ASCII: on other names the runtimes differ (Rust keeps every Unicode letter and digit, Java replaces per code point as the model does, TypeScript per UTF-16 code unit, so a character outside the basic plane becomes two underscores) and the spec leaves them implementation-defined, which is the plain sentence quoted after the first shall sentence.

The sixth line is guarantee 1 and the second shall sentence, for every name: all three runtimes keep the prefixes p_, t_ and j_ for every name, so a junction ID, which starts with j_, is no place or transition ID. Without it a mapper that writes non-ASCII names verbatim, without a prefix, meets the other five lines and gives the transition Ü and its junction one ID (EXP_014_forbids_rawNonAscii, exp014_rawNonAscii_rest). The reference meets it by EXP_014_guarantee1.

The second and third lines restate the numbering bullet and the third, fourth and fifth shall sentences: the junction nodes of a transition are one per group with two or more children, of that group's kind (and for And, xor for Xor, which the spec's example implies and the third shall sentence states), the index of a junction is the position of its group in the pre-order of those groups (OutTree.junctions, which skips a short group, so a collapsed group consumes no counter slot), and the output edges are exactly the edges of EXP-012's drawing rule wired to those indices, so an extra, missing or repeated output edge breaks the third line (EXP_014_forbids_dupOutEdge). EXP-012 compares junctions and edges only up to a one-to-one renumbering; these two lines fix the renumbering to the identity. Both lines read a transition by its name, so they are stated on nets with pairwise distinct transition names, which every net that builds has and which the shall sentences state as their condition; the input-arc half of X.Distinct (CORE-030) plays no part here.

The third line reads the output side by arc type: an output or reset+output edge from the transition or one of its junctions. An edge from a junction drawn with another arc type escapes it but not the fourth line, which still requires its junction end to be drawn; arc types are EXP-012's subject and the export agreement's (ExportAgrees).
The fourth line is the sixth shall sentence: an edge whose end is a junction no node stands for would make Graphviz invent an unstyled node with a junction ID. Ghost edges (EXP-017) are included.

The fifth line is the uniqueness shall sentence, the uniqueness that 'uniquely determined' claims, under the name assumption of ruling D46 (a) (kind A, ExportNet.IdNames, on a net with pairwise distinct transition names): ASCII names, and no two place names nor two transition names equal after sanitize. Without it two names such as b1/x and b1_x get one ID in every runtime. A place and a transition never share an ID (prefixes p_ and t_), and a junction ID is no place or transition ID (prefix j_) and determines its transition's sanitised name, kind and index (EXP_014_junctionId_inj, by reading the ID from its end: the index has no underscore, the kind word is three letters after a double underscore). Ruling D46 (a) also names non-empty names; uniqueness does not need that (an empty place name, an empty transition name and their junctions still get the IDs p_, t_ and j___<kind>_<idx>), so ExportNet.IdNames leaves it out and only AC1 is scoped to non-empty names. The assumption's 'no empty / segment' clause is EXP-016's and plays no part here.
The 'uniquely determined by the depth-first traversal' clause of the flat-counter paragraph is the second and third lines.

AC1 (all junction IDs match j_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__(xor|and)_[0-9]+) follows from the first line, for every exporter meeting EXP-014, for a junction of a transition whose name is non-empty and ASCII (EXP_014_ac1), which is what the last quoted plain sentence scopes AC1 to. An empty transition name builds in every runtime and gives j___xor_0, which the regex rejects; a non-ASCII name gives an implementation-defined ID, and Rust's j_é__xor_0 does not match the regex either.

Guarantee 2 and AC2 (two exports of one net are byte-equal) have no content over a Lean function, which is deterministic; across processes they fail today for Java and Rust (HashSet order, ruling R2 (exp-b)); kind Q. Guarantee 3 and AC3 (Java, TypeScript and Rust exports are byte-equal) are a property of three programs and kind Q by ruling D60 (c); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration. The order of nodes and edges is not stated (List.Perm), only the numbering the spec pins.

The test derivation (export twice and diff; export in three languages and diff) is AC2 and AC3, kind Q. EXP_014_nonvacuous decides the spec's example AND(XOR(a,b), XOR(c,d)) on t Nested, a deeper tree that separates pre-order from breadth-first numbering, a collapsed group, sanitised place, transition and junction IDs, and a junction ID apart from the transition ID on a non-ASCII name, on the reference.

requirements.title: Subnet Instance Cluster Subgraphs
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),
    ExportNet.ClusterNames cfg.cluster X →
      (∀ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,
          ∀ c ∈ (E cfg X).clusters,
            n.ref ∈ c.members ↔ nodeKey cfg.cluster X.member n.ref = some c.key) ∧
        (∀ c ∈ (E cfg X).clusters,
            (∀ r ∈ c.members, ∃ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes, n.ref = r) ∧
              ((List.map ExportTrans.name X.trans).Nodup → c.members.Nodup)) ∧
          (∀ (q : String),
              q ∈ List.map XCluster.key (E cfg X).clusters ↔
                ∃ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,
                  ∃ K,
                    nodeKey cfg.cluster X.member n.ref = some K ∧
                      (q = K ∨ IsSlashPrefix q K)) ∧
            (List.map XCluster.key (E cfg X).clusters).Nodup ∧
              (∀ c ∈ (E cfg X).clusters, c.parent = instancePrefix c.key) ∧
                (∀ c ∈ (E cfg X).clusters, c.id = clusterId c.key ∧ c.label = c.key) ∧
                  (E cfg X).nodes.Perm
                      (E
                          { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := cfg.showTypes,
                            showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals,
                            showPriority := cfg.showPriority, env := cfg.env,
                            cluster := ClusterSource.none }
                          X).nodes ∧
                    (List.filter (fun e ↦ e.arc != ArcType.ghost) (E cfg X).edges).Perm
                      (List.filter (fun e ↦ e.arc != ArcType.ghost)
                        (E
                            { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := cfg.showTypes,
                              showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals,
                              showPriority := cfg.showPriority, env := cfg.env,
                              cluster := ClusterSource.none }
                            X).edges)
requirements.scope: every exporter, the clusters of the exported graph
reading: For every configuration cfg and net X that meets the name assumption (ExportNet.ClusterNames: EXP-014's ExportNet.IdNames, ASCII place and transition names with no two place names and no two transition names equal after sanitize, and every cluster key of a place or transition name of X under cfg.cluster ASCII and non-empty with no empty /-segment), with key the glossary's nodeKey cfg.cluster X.member (membership entry, else instancePrefix, per cluster source; a junction takes its transition's key), the graph E cfg X satisfies:

every drawn node is a direct member of a cluster exactly when the cluster's key is the node's key (so a node with a key is in the cluster of its key and no other, and a node without a key is in no cluster);
every member of a cluster is the reference of a drawn node, and when the transition names of X are pairwise distinct no cluster lists a member twice;
a string is the key of a cluster exactly when it is the key of a drawn node or a /-prefix of such a key (IsSlashPrefix: a non-empty initial segment of the key that is followed by / in it);
no two clusters have the same key;
the parent of every cluster is the instance prefix of its key (the part before its last /, none without one);
every cluster has the ID clusterId of its key (cluster_ followed by sanitize of the key) and its key as label;

the nodes are those E draws for cfg with cluster source none, and the edges other than ghost edges are those E draws for cfg with cluster source none, each up to order (List.Perm: the same multiset, every field of each node and edge included).
quotes: DOT export of a net produced by modular composition (per [MOD-020]) SHOULD emit a `subgraph cluster_<sanitizedKey>` block grouping each subnet's nodes.

**Subnet-membership metadata** ([MOD-026]) carried by a directly-composed net — a node mapped to subnet `S` clusters under `cluster_<sanitize(S)>`; a shared (multi-subnet) place has no entry and is not grouped by metadata.

**Instance-prefix detection** — a node whose name begins with `<prefix>/` (the separator established by [MOD-010]) clusters under `cluster_<sanitize(prefix)>`. Nested instance prefixes (per [MOD-013]) MUST produce nested cluster subgraphs.
When the net carries membership metadata the exporter SHOULD prefer it and fall back to instance-prefix detection for any node without an entry, so direct and instance composition coexist.
The cluster source MAY be caller-selectable (metadata-only, prefix-only, or no clustering); the default SHOULD be metadata-when-present.

The sanitization function applied to the key MUST match the existing DOT ID sanitization per [EXP-014] (non-`[A-Za-z0-9_]` characters, including `/`, replaced by `_`). The cluster `label` attribute SHOULD carry the original (un-sanitized) key string for human readability.

This requirement does NOT alter the styling, junction, or arc rendering rules of EXP-002..EXP-015; it adds grouping structure only. A net with neither composed instances nor membership metadata (no `/` in any node name) MUST produce no cluster subgraphs.

The SHOULD priority is whether an exporter draws cluster subgraphs at all. For an exporter that draws them, every MAY, SHOULD and MUST sentence of this requirement reads as *shall*: it lets the caller select each cluster source named above, takes the default source when the caller selects none, and follows the sentences below.

Under the default cluster source the cluster key of a place or a transition is its membership entry when it has one and otherwise its instance prefix; under the metadata-only source it is the membership entry alone, under the prefix-only source the instance prefix alone, and under no clustering there is none. The instance prefix of a name is the part before its last `/`; a name without `/`, or whose only `/` is its first character, has none. A junction node has the cluster key of its transition. A node without a cluster key is a top-level node. A `/`-prefix of a key is the non-empty beginning of the key up to, and not including, one of its `/` characters.

These sentences cover nets whose place names and transition names are ASCII, in which no two place names and no two transition names become equal under the sanitization of [EXP-014], and in which every cluster key of a place or transition name is ASCII, non-empty and has no empty `/`-segment: it neither starts nor ends with `/` and holds no `//`. On other nets the clustering, and whether it changes the nodes and edges drawn, is implementation-defined.
The mapper *shall* make each node that has a cluster key a direct member of the cluster of that key and of no other cluster, and a top-level node a member of no cluster.
The mapper *shall* list as a member of a cluster only a node it draws, and, on a net whose transition names are pairwise distinct, list each such node at most once.
The mapper *shall* draw exactly one cluster for each cluster key of a drawn node and for each `/`-prefix of such a key, and no other cluster.
The mapper *shall* nest each cluster directly in the cluster whose key is the part of its own key before the last `/`, and draw a cluster whose key has no `/` at the top level.
The mapper *shall* give the cluster of key K the ID `cluster_` followed by K with each character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` replaced by `_`, and the label K.
The mapper *shall* draw, in any order, the same nodes, and the same edges other than the ghost edges of [EXP-017], as it draws for the same net and configuration under no clustering.
assumes: The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): the typed graph a configuration and a net are drawn as, before DOT text. Clusters are the graph's XCluster list (key, ID, label, parent key, direct members). Which subgraph block an edge is written in (deepest_common_prefix in the runtimes), cluster styling and the order of sibling clusters are properties of the DOT text, not stated (ruling R2 (exp-b) on order); the block states membership, nesting, IDs and labels.

The key rule is a fixed glossary definition (clusterKey, nodeKey, instancePrefix in Reference/ExportCluster.lean), the same three lines in all three mappers (cluster_key_of in Rust, autoClusterKeyOf and its switch in TypeScript, PetriNetGraphMapper in Java), so a mapper with another key rule breaks the first and third lines: the first-/ key (EXP_016_forbids_firstSlash), metadata only under the default source (EXP_016_forbids_metadataDefault), MOD-040's subnetOf walk-up used for clustering (EXP_016_forbids_walkUp; MOD-040 itself says the exporter still clusters s1/obs/TURN under s1/obs) and junctions left at the top level (EXP_016_forbids_junctionTop).

The membership bullet, the prefix bullet and the fall-back sentence are the key rule under the default source auto. By ruling D26 item 7 a shared place has no membership entry and is therefore not grouped by metadata; under the default source it falls back to its instance prefix like every node without an entry, so it is at the top level only when its name has no instance prefix (the old wording 'stays top-level' contradicted the fall-back sentence). The junction sentence is ruling D26 item 5 (all three mappers put a junction in its transition's cluster).

The SHOULD priority is whether an exporter clusters at all (ruling D26 item 7: the MUST sentences inside a SHOULD requirement read 'an exporter that clusters shall'). The scoping sentence extends that reading to the MAY and SHOULD sentences: for an exporter that clusters, 'MAY be caller-selectable', 'the default SHOULD be metadata-when-present', 'SHOULD prefer it and fall back' and 'the cluster label attribute SHOULD carry the original key' are obligations, as the block states them (all three runtimes meet them). The model takes the caller's choice as cfg.cluster and the statement quantifies over all four sources, so an exporter that ignores the choice fails the first and third lines; the glossary's ExportCfg defaults cfg.cluster to auto (metadata when present, else the prefix), which is the default-source sentence. An exporter that never draws clusters does not meet the predicate and is outside the requirement.

Ruling D46 (a) with (x), kind A: the block covers nets that meet ExportNet.ClusterNames. Its first half is EXP-014's name assumption ExportNet.IdNames (ASCII names, no two place names and no two transition names equal after sanitize). The first line depends on it: all three runtimes look a node's key up by its DOT ID (node_id_to_prefix in Rust, nodeIdToPrefix in Java and TypeScript), so on b1/t from b1/x to b1_x the two places are one node p_b1_x, which no exporter can put both in cluster_b1 and at the top level (exp016_collide_outside); under IdNames the ID is one to one on the nodes the reference draws (exp014_nodeId_inj), so looking a key up by ID finds the node's own key. Its second half (ExportNet.ClusterKeysWellFormed, over the declared places, the places the arcs touch and the transition names of X) is that every cluster key is ASCII and non-empty with no empty /-segment. The ASCII half is needed because a membership key is a subnet name (MOD-026), not a node name, so it can hold other characters while every node name is ASCII; Rust's sanitize keeps Unicode letters (ruling D46 (a) makes them implementation-defined), so for a key Größe Rust draws the cluster ID cluster_Größe where Java and TypeScript draw cluster_Gr__e, and the sixth line, which states the ID through the glossary's ASCII sanitize, would bind Rust on a character D46 leaves open (exp016_nonAsciiKey_outside). On a key with an empty segment (a name such as a//x or http://host/x) the Rust builder panics (register_prefix_chain skips the empty segment, then expect fails) and the Java builder throws; TypeScript draws the clusters the model draws. Those are recorded runtime defects outside the migration (RD-12 in spec/runtime-defects.md; the Unicode cluster ID is RD-13 and the lookup by DOT ID RD-14). On a net outside the assumption the whole predicate is silent, the seventh line included. The reference model stays total there (registerChain in Reference/ExportCluster.lean decides both facts).

Two membership keys whose sanitised forms are equal (a/b and a_b) get one cluster ID; the sixth line states that ID as the runtimes draw it, and no line depends on the keys' sanitised forms being distinct.

The second line's at-most-once half (EXP_016_forbids_dupJunction) carries the premise that the transition names of X are pairwise distinct, as EXP-014's uniqueness line does: two transitions with one name draw one node reference twice, and the members of a cluster list each drawn reference in node order.

The sixth line is the sanitisation sentence and the label sentence: sanitize is EXP-014's (each character outside [A-Za-z0-9_], / included, replaced by _). The seventh line is 'does NOT alter the styling, junction, or arc rendering rules of EXP-002..EXP-015; it adds grouping structure only' together with the last shall sentence: ghost edges are excluded because EXP-017 adds them only when there are clusters (export design, skeptic correction S-4), and EXP-017 itself keeps the visible edge set. The statement reads ghost edges as the glossary's ArcType.ghost, so the [EXP-017] in the shall sentence is a citation, not a dependency (EXP-017 depends on EXP-016); likewise MOD-040 in the Depends-on line is a spec cross-reference (MOD-040, wave W8, cites this block), not a Lean import. 'MUST produce no cluster subgraphs' on a net without metadata and without / is a consequence of the first and third lines (EXP_016_ac4).

AC1 (cluster_b1 and cluster_b2 for instances b1 and b2) and AC3 (cluster_outer containing cluster_outer_inner) are decided on the reference in EXP_016_nonvacuous, and follow from the third, fifth and sixth lines for every exporter meeting the block. AC2, restated by ruling D26 item 5 to count nested cluster blocks and the junctions of a cluster's transitions, follows from the first and third lines (EXP_016_ac2): a node is inside the cluster of K, directly or through a nested cluster, exactly when its key is K or has K as a /-prefix.

AC4 (no / in any node name and no membership metadata gives no cluster) is EXP_016_ac4, for every exporter meeting the block on a net meeting EXP-014's name assumption. AC5: the regex half (cluster_[A-Za-z0-9_]+) is EXP_016_ac5 for every cluster with a non-empty key, and the name assumption makes every key of the net's names non-empty; the determinism half has no content over a Lean function, which is deterministic, and is kind Q. AC6 (Java, TypeScript and Rust produce byte-identical cluster blocks) is a property of three programs and kind Q by ruling D60 (c); the runtimes differ today in the order of sibling clusters (ruling R2 (exp-b)). AC7, restated by ruling D26 item 7 to shared places whose names carry no instance prefix, is the first line under a membership map, decided on a directly composed net in EXP_016_nonvacuous.

The test derivation (compose two instances, nested instances and a direct composition; assert blocks, members and sanitised IDs) is AC1, AC3, AC2, AC5 and AC7 on composed nets; how compose builds names and the membership map is MOD-010, MOD-013 and MOD-026 on the composition model (W8), and the block quantifies over every net and membership map the mapper can see.

requirements.title: Compound Cluster Layout Hints
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),
    (E cfg X).compound = true ∧
      (ExportNet.ClusterNames cfg.cluster X →
        (∀ w ∈ exp017Bridges cfg X (E cfg X),
            ∃ e ∈ exp017Ghosts (E cfg X),
              Option.map exp017Hint (exp017First (exp017Bridges cfg X (E cfg X)) w.1) =
                some (exp017Ends e)) ∧
          (∀ e ∈ exp017Ghosts (E cfg X),
              ∃ p ∈ exp017Bridges cfg X (E cfg X),
                exp017First (exp017Bridges cfg X (E cfg X)) p.1 = some p ∧
                  exp017Ends e = exp017Hint p) ∧
            (List.map (exp017KeyPair cfg X) (exp017Ghosts (E cfg X))).Nodup ∧
              (exp017Real (E cfg X)).Perm
                (exp017Real
                  (E
                    { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := cfg.showTypes,
                      showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals,
                      showPriority := cfg.showPriority, env := cfg.env,
                      cluster := ClusterSource.none }
                    X)))
requirements.scope: every exporter, the graph attribute compound and the ghost edges between clusters
reading: For every configuration cfg and net X, in the graph E cfg X, with the bridges ws read off that graph (exp017Bridges: the bridge witnesses over its nodes in their order and its non-ghost edges in their order, keys by EXP-016's nodeKey under cfg's cluster source and X's membership map):
the graph attribute compound is true;
and, when X meets EXP-016's name assumption under cfg's cluster source (ExportNet.ClusterNames), the following four lines hold:

for every bridge w in ws, some ghost edge of the graph (an edge of arc type ghost) runs from the anchor a to the anchor b of the first bridge in ws with w's ordered key pair, with ltail the cluster ID of its first key and lhead the cluster ID of its second (exp017Hint);
every ghost edge of the graph is, in its ends, ltail and lhead, the ghost edge of a bridge p in ws that is the first bridge with its ordered key pair;
the ordered pairs of cluster keys of the two ends of the ghost edges are pairwise distinct;
and the edges other than ghost edges are, up to order (List.Perm), those of E drawn for X under cfg with cluster source none.
quotes: DOT export SHOULD set `compound=true` at the digraph level unconditionally so Graphviz honours `lhead` and `ltail` attributes on edges that cross cluster boundaries.

In this requirement the cluster key of a node is its key under [EXP-016], so a node with a key lies in the deepest cluster of that key, and an orphan is a node with no key, which is drawn at the top level.
An edge is an edge of the exported graph other than a ghost edge, of any arc type, in the direction it is drawn, and either end of it may be a junction node ([EXP-012]).

A bridge for an ordered pair of distinct keys (X, Y) is an orphan `o` together with an edge `a → o` from a node `a` with key X and an edge `o → b` to a node `b` with key Y, so one orphan with several such pairs of edges gives several bridges.
A cluster and a cluster nested in it, such as `outer` and `outer/inner`, have two distinct keys, so an orphan between them bridges them.
For every ordered pair of distinct cluster keys (X, Y) that at least one bridge connects, the exporter MUST emit exactly one invisible ghost edge with:
`ltail = "cluster_" + sanitize(X)` (matches the cluster id defined by [EXP-016])
`lhead = "cluster_" + sanitize(Y)`

The ghost edge's source and target node ids MUST be the `a` and the `b` of the first bridge for (X, Y) in this scan order: the nodes in the order they are drawn, for each orphan the edges into it in the order they are drawn, and for each of those the edges out of it in the order they are drawn.
Because every drawn edge counts, a reset edge into an orphan place and a read edge out of it bridge two clusters although no token moves between them.
An orphan transition whose output spec has a junction bridges nothing through that junction, since the junction is itself an orphan.
Multiple orphans bridging the same ordered cluster pair `(X, Y)` collapse to one ghost edge (dedup by ordered pair).
The reverse direction `(Y, X)` is a separate ghost edge when its own 1-hop path exists.
Orphan paths that fall entirely inside a single cluster (`X == Y`) or that only touch one clustered neighbour MUST NOT produce a ghost edge.
This requirement does NOT change [EXP-016] cluster membership, the visible edge set, or styling rules.

Apart from the `compound` attribute, these sentences cover the nets that the sentences of [EXP-016] cover; on other nets the ghost edges, and whether clustering changes the other edges drawn, are implementation-defined.
The exporter *shall* set the graph attribute `compound` to true in every export.

*Where* a bridge connects an ordered pair of distinct cluster keys (X, Y), an exporter that clusters *shall* draw a ghost edge from the `a` to the `b` of the first bridge for (X, Y), with `ltail` the cluster ID of X and `lhead` the cluster ID of Y.

Each ghost edge that an exporter that clusters draws *shall* run from the `a` to the `b` of the first bridge for some ordered pair of distinct cluster keys (X, Y), with `ltail` the cluster ID of X and `lhead` the cluster ID of Y.
An exporter that clusters *shall* draw at most one ghost edge for each ordered pair of cluster keys.
The exporter *shall* draw the same edges other than ghost edges as it draws for the same net with no clustering.
assumes: The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): from a configuration (with its cluster source, EXP-016) and the export view of a net (with its membership map, MOD-026), the typed graph a mapper builds before DOT text. The block reads the compound attribute, the nodes in their order and the edges in their order; a ghost edge is an edge of arc type ghost, and of it the block reads its source, target, ltail and lhead.

The cluster key of a node is EXP-016's (nodeKey: the membership entry, else the part of the name before its last /, per cluster source; a junction has its transition's key). So the key of a node is its deepest cluster: outer/inner/a to an orphan to other/b bridges (outer/inner, other) and not (outer, other), and outer/a to an orphan to outer/inner/b bridges a cluster to its own child (ruling D26 item 6; exp_b probe cases 8 and 9; exp017NetE in EXP_017_nonvacuous, EXP_017_forbids_skipNested). The sentence 'Orphan paths that fall entirely inside a single cluster (X == Y)' compares keys, not the drawn boxes: both ends of outer/a to o to outer/inner/b lie inside the box of outer, yet the keys differ and the pair is bridged, as the quoted sentence on nested clusters says. Graphviz may warn about and ignore ltail and lhead when one cluster contains the other, so such a ghost edge may constrain less than a ghost edge between two sibling clusters; whether to keep drawing it is a feature question outside the migration. A place shared by two subnets of a direct composition has no membership entry and no prefix, so it is an orphan too. Cluster IDs are compared as EXP-016 draws them (clusterId, cluster_ followed by the sanitised key).

Ruling D46 (a) with (x), kind A: lines 2 to 5 cover the nets EXP-016 covers, as the scope sentence of the requirement says: nets that meet ExportNet.ClusterNames under cfg's cluster source (EXP-014's name assumption, and every cluster key ASCII and non-empty with no empty /-segment). The compound line binds every net, since its sentence says 'in every export'. On other nets the runtimes do not draw what lines 2 to 5 would ask. All three look a node's key up by its DOT ID (node_id_to_prefix in Rust, nodeIdToPrefix in Java and TypeScript), so on a net where b1/t outputs to b1_x, b2/u consumes b1_x and b1/v consumes b1/x, the place b1/x gives the shared ID p_b1_x the key b1, the orphan b1_x is not seen as an orphan, and no runtime draws the ghost edge for (b1, b2) that the bridges keyed by node reference ask for. On a key with an empty segment (a name such as a//x) the Rust builder panics and the Java builder throws, and on a non-ASCII membership key Rust draws a cluster ID that the glossary's clusterId does not give. Those are recorded runtime defects (RD-12 to RD-14 in spec/runtime-defects.md) or implementation-defined cases of ruling D46, and the block is silent on such nets. The reference meets the block without the premise (EXP_017_reference does not use it), and every mutant below fails it on a net that meets the premise.

Bridges are read over the drawn edges of every arc type in the direction drawn (ruling D26 item 6), as all three mappers scan them: a reset edge into an orphan place and a read edge out of it bridge two clusters although no token moves between them (exp_b probe case F, EXP_017_forbids_tokenFlow), and an orphan transition whose output spec has a junction bridges nothing through it, since its junction is itself an orphan whose only incoming edge leaves the keyless transition. Whether these should change is a feature question outside the migration. The ghost edges are left out of the scan; they join two nodes with keys, so they would bridge nothing anyway, and the quoted definition of an edge leaves them out, so the definition does not refer to itself.

The scan order is the graph's own node and edge order, so the first bridge depends on the order the exporter draws its nodes and edges, which differs between the runtimes (ruling R2 (exp-b)) and is stated by no requirement. The block fixes the anchors relative to the drawn order, which is what each mapper computes.

Order of the ghost edges is not stated: the second and third lines are membership statements and the fourth line counts, so the ghost edges are compared up to order. Order of the other edges is not stated either: the fifth line compares them with the edges drawn under cluster source none up to order (List.Perm), the visible edge set of the body, as EXP-016's seventh line does. The first bridge is read in the order of the graph drawn under cfg, so an exporter that draws its edges in another order when it clusters anchors at the first bridge of that order.

The style of a ghost edge (style invis, arrowhead none) is a visual constant of the DOT renderer, checked by tests (kind Q); so is the claim that the line is a no-op for flat nets in Graphviz. That ghost edges change no cluster membership is EXP-016's (its members are read off node keys, not edges); the fifth line states that they change no other edge.

The header says SHOULD and the body MUST; the EARS sentences read an exporter that clusters shall (ruling D26 item 7). The SHOULD priority is whether an exporter clusters at all. The predicate is what an exporter that clusters draws: its bridges are read off the cluster keys (nodeKey under cfg's cluster source and X's membership map), which are the clusters an exporter meeting EXP-016 draws, not off the clusters the exporter happens to draw. An exporter that never draws clusters does not meet it on a net with a bridge and is outside the requirement, as in EXP-016. With cluster source none no node has a key, so there is no bridge and, by the third line, no ghost edge.

AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6 and AC7 are EXP_017_nonvacuous on the reference exporter: every export has compound true, a flat net has no ghost edge (AC1, AC7); the net exp017NetA has three orphan transitions bridging (left, right), one bridging (right, left), one with left on both sides and one with a single clustered neighbour, and gets exactly two ghost edges, one per direction, anchored at the first bridge (AC2 to AC6). AC2's literal net, exp017NetAC2 (left and right bridged by one orphan transition), gets exactly one ghost edge with ltail cluster_left and lhead cluster_right.

AC8 (anchor selection matches across Java, TypeScript and Rust byte for byte) is kind Q: a Lean function is deterministic and cross-language equality is a property of three programs (export design P3, ruling D60 (c)); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration. The test derivation is AC2 to AC7.

requirements.title: ν-Match Edge Decoration
requirements.statement:
fun E ↦
  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),
    (∀ t ∈ X.trans,
        ∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs,
          ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
            e.arc = ArcType.input ∧
              e.src = NodeRef.place s.place ∧ e.dst = NodeRef.trans t.name) ∧
      ((∀ t ∈ X.trans,
            ∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs,
              s.place ∈ t.corr →
                ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                  e.arc = ArcType.input ∧
                    e.src = NodeRef.place s.place ∧
                      e.dst = NodeRef.trans t.name ∧
                        e.row = Export.EdgeRow.matchInput ∧
                          e.label = some (corrLabel (refCardLabel s.card))) ∧
          (X.Distinct →
            ∀ t ∈ X.trans,
              ∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs,
                s.place ∈ t.corr →
                  ∀ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                    e.arc = ArcType.input →
                      e.src = NodeRef.place s.place →
                        e.dst = NodeRef.trans t.name →
                          e.row = Export.EdgeRow.matchInput ∧
                            e.label = some (corrLabel (refCardLabel s.card)))) ∧
        ((∀ t ∈ X.trans,
              ∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs,
                s.place ∉ t.corr →
                  ∃ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                    e.arc = ArcType.input ∧
                      e.src = NodeRef.place s.place ∧
                        e.dst = NodeRef.trans t.name ∧
                          e.row = Export.EdgeRow.input ∧ e.label = refCardLabel s.card) ∧
            (X.Distinct →
              ∀ t ∈ X.trans,
                ∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs,
                  s.place ∉ t.corr →
                    ∀ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
                      e.arc = ArcType.input →
                        e.src = NodeRef.place s.place →
                          e.dst = NodeRef.trans t.name →
                            e.row = Export.EdgeRow.input ∧
                              e.label = refCardLabel s.card)) ∧
          ∀ e ∈ (E cfg X).edges,
            e.arc ≠ ArcType.ghost →
              e.row = Export.EdgeRow.matchInput →
                e.arc = ArcType.input ∧
                  ∃ t ∈ X.trans,
                    ∃ s ∈ t.core.inputs,
                      s.place ∈ t.corr ∧
                        e.src = NodeRef.place s.place ∧ e.dst = NodeRef.trans t.name
requirements.scope: every exporter, on the input edges of the graph it draws for a configuration and a net
reading: For the exporter E, every configuration cfg and every net X:
for every transition t of X and every input arc s of t, the graph E cfg X has an edge of arc type input from the place of s to the node of t;

for every input arc s of a transition t whose place t correlates, some such edge has the match-input style row and the label ⟨n⟩, followed by a space and the cardinality label of s when s has one (corrLabel of refCardLabel), and, when the transitions of X have distinct names and no transition has two input arcs on one place, every such edge has that row and that label;

for every input arc s of a transition t whose place t does not correlate, some such edge has the input style row and the cardinality label of s (refCardLabel), none for One, and, under the same condition, every such edge has that row and that label;

every edge of the graph that is not a ghost edge and has the match-input style row is an edge of arc type input from the place of an input arc s of some transition t of X to the node of t, and t correlates the place of s.
quotes: When a transition declares a ν-net join correlation ([NU-020]), each **input edge** to a correlated place is decorated to mark it as a name-matched input:
Label prefixed with the bound-name variable `⟨n⟩` (U+27E8 `n` U+27E9).
When the input also carries a cardinality label ([EXP-006]), the two are joined with a single space: `⟨n⟩ ×2`, `⟨n⟩ *`, `⟨n⟩ ≥3`.
A correlated `One` input shows `⟨n⟩` alone.
Non-correlated inputs of the same transition are unaffected.
The export *shall* draw each input arc of a transition as an edge of arc type input from the arc's place to the transition, whether or not the transition correlates the place.

*Where* the match specification of a transition ([NU-020]) correlates the place of one of its input arcs, the export *shall* draw the edge of that arc with the `match-input` style row and label it `⟨n⟩` if the arc's cardinality is `One`, and otherwise `⟨n⟩`, one space and the arc's cardinality label ([EXP-006]).

*Where* a transition does not correlate the place of one of its input arcs, the export *shall* draw the edge of that arc with the `input` style row and give it the arc's cardinality label alone, or no label if the cardinality is `One`.
Apart from ghost edges ([EXP-017]), the export *shall* draw only the input edges of correlated places with the `match-input` style row.
assumes: The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): from an export configuration (glossary ExportCfg) and a net as the exporter reads it (glossary ExportNet), the typed graph the runtimes' mappers build before DOT text (glossary XGraph). An edge (glossary XEdge) carries its ends, its arc type (glossary ArcType), its style row (Libpetri.Export.EdgeRow, generated from spec/petri-net-styles.json) and its label. A transition (glossary ExportTrans) carries in corr the places its ν-net match specification correlates (NU-020), empty without one; NU-020 makes every correlated place an input place of the transition, which is why the lines speak of input arcs only. The DOT text and its attribute syntax are not modelled.

Relay targets: corr holds the places of match keys only, never the relay targets of NU-054, as in every runtime: each mapper decorates an input when the correlates test of the match specification holds, and that test checks match keys only, never relay keys. So line 4 forbids drawing a relay edge (an output edge to a relay target) with the match-input row, as it forbids any teal output edge (EXP_018_forbids_outTeal); NU-054's API note is reworded to agree (spec edit NU-054-relay-export).

Colour: the colour bullet (#0d9488, teal, the match-input edge style in spec/petri-net-styles.json, distinguishing the edge from a plain input edge) is read as the match-input style row: an edge names a row of the generated style table and the colour is the row's. EXP_018_nonvacuous decides on the table that the match-input row has colour #0d9488 and that the input row has another colour (#333333). Which hex value the DOT text carries for a row is kind Q (the style generator's gate).

Arc type: all three mappers keep the arc type of a correlated edge as input and change only its style row, so line 1 asks for an edge of arc type input for every input arc, correlated or not, and a mapper that changes the arc type of a correlated edge (EXP_018_forbids_arcRead) or drops the edge (EXP_018_forbids_dropCorr) violates the block. Line 1 overlaps EXP-001's line on input edges and follows from the first halves of lines 2 and 3; it is kept as the line of the first EARS sentence, which states the arc type apart from the decoration, and the two mutants it names also fail the first half of line 2.

Labels: the cardinality label is EXP-006's, in the forms ruling D41 (a) pins (×n, *, ≥m, none for One), the function refCardLabel; the correlated label is glossary corrLabel: ⟨n⟩ (U+27E8, n, U+27E9) alone when the cardinality label is none, else ⟨n⟩, one space and the cardinality label. A correlated One edge is therefore labelled ⟨n⟩ and nothing else (EXP_018_forbids_trailingSpace); EXP-006's AC2 ('One cardinality has no cardinality label') names the cardinality label (ruling D41 (a), clash exp-a#6), and ⟨n⟩ is not one, so the ⟨n⟩ label does not contradict it.

Lines 2 and 3 have two halves each. The first half holds on every net: some input edge from the place of the arc to the transition has the row and the label. The reference meets it on every net, since it draws refInputEdge t s for every input arc s of every transition t. The second half asks the same of every input edge with those ends, and only on nets whose transitions have distinct names and at most one input arc per place (glossary ExportNet.Distinct): the exporter keys transition nodes by name, so with two transitions of one name, or two input arcs of one transition on one place, two arcs would share the ends of one edge and the half could ask two labels of it. Line 4 needs no such condition.

No builder gives ExportNet.Distinct to every net. Distinct transition names are the reading of CORE-020 (a name identifies the transition, see TIME-010); no runtime's net builder rejects two transitions of one name, and only composition does (MOD-025). One input arc per place is CORE-030's transition builder check, with the implementation's own Place equality (CORE-002), and in Java that equality is name-and-type (the MOD-024 divergence note).

On a net that is not Distinct the first halves still bind. A mapper that looks up a transition's match specification by its name, last write wins, draws a correlated input plain when a later transition of the same name has no match; the first half of line 2 rejects it (EXP_018_forbids_lastWinsCorr). With the two transitions in the other order it decorates an uncorrelated input; the first half of line 3 rejects it (EXP_018_forbids_lastWinsUncorr). A Java transition with two input arcs on places of one name and different types, only one of them correlated, is modelled as two input arcs on one place, both correlated, because the exporter names a place node by the place name: the first half of line 2 asks for one decorated edge, which Java draws, and Java's second, plain edge is not ruled out.

The second halves are needed on top of the first: an exporter that draws the decorated edge of a correlated input and also a plain copy of it meets the first half of line 2 and violates the second (EXP_018_forbids_dupPlain).

'Non-correlated inputs of the same transition are unaffected' is line 3: the edge keeps the input row and the plain cardinality label, so a mapper that decorates every input of a transition that has a match violates the block (EXP_018_forbids_allInputs), and so does one that keeps the input row of an uncorrelated input but writes ⟨n⟩ before its label (EXP_018_forbids_uncorrPrefix). Line 3 binds every uncorrelated input of every transition, including a transition with no match specification (corr empty), not only the other inputs of a transition with a match. For those it restates the input row of EXP-001 and the cardinality label of EXP-006, so it adds no obligation beyond them; it is what every runtime draws. 'No other edge changes' is line 4 for the style row: no output, inhibitor, read or reset edge, and no input edge of an uncorrelated place, is drawn with the match-input row (EXP_018_forbids_outTeal). Ghost edges (EXP-017) are drawn invisible and their style row is that requirement's, so line 4 excludes them. A label on another edge that happens to start with ⟨n⟩ (an Xor branch label of a place so named) is not ruled out: the label lines speak of input edges only.

The sentence 'The decoration is a mapper concern: it is emitted into the DOT by every exporter, so the canonical viewer and all three doc generators render it identically with no viewer change.' is a design note on where the decoration is computed: the block is a predicate over the exporter, which is that mapper, and what the viewer and the doc generators render from the DOT is kind Q.
No configuration option changes the decoration in any runtime, so the lines hold for every configuration.

AC1 (an input edge to a correlated place has color #0d9488 and a label beginning with ⟨n⟩) is line 2 with the colour reading above; line 2 asks for the whole label, so the literal reading 'begins with ⟨n⟩' is weaker and a mapper that writes ⟨n⟩×2 without the space meets it but not this block (EXP_018_forbids_noSpace). A mapper that writes ⟨n⟩ only when a cardinality label exists draws a correlated One edge with no label and violates line 2 (EXP_018_forbids_optionMap).
AC2 (a non-correlated input edge on the same transition keeps the default color and no ⟨n⟩ prefix) is line 3.
AC3 (the label combines with cardinality as ⟨n⟩ ×n, ⟨n⟩ *, ⟨n⟩ ≥m) is line 2 with EXP-006's pinned forms; a mapper that replaces the cardinality label by ⟨n⟩ violates it (EXP_018_forbids_replace).

AC4 (the emitted DOT for a ν-net is byte-identical across the Java, TypeScript and Rust exporters) is kind Q: a Lean function is deterministic and cross-language equality is a property of three programs (ruling D60 (c)); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration.

The test derivation (a join with match correlating two One inputs, both correlated edges teal and labelled ⟨n⟩, a third non-correlated input unchanged) is EXP_018_nonvacuous on the reference, with a second transition whose correlated Exactly(2), All and AtLeast(3) inputs show ⟨n⟩ ×2, ⟨n⟩ * and ⟨n⟩ ≥3 next to an uncorrelated Exactly(2) input labelled ×2.

requirements.title: Input One
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),
    InputArc t p Card.one →
      (while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧
        (∀ (m : CountMarking N),
            Marked m p →
              ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (io001_withoutInput t p) m m')) ∧
          (¬ResetArc t p →
            ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),
              F t m d m' →
                m' p + 1 = m p + Deposits d p ∧ (¬OutputArc t p → m' p + 1 = m p))
reading: For every transition t and place p such that the input arc of t on p is One:
t does not fire from a marking in which p is unmarked;
from a marking in which p is marked, t can fire exactly when t without its input arc on p can fire;

unless p is also a reset place of t, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) + 1 = m(p) + d(p): p loses exactly 1 token, besides what the firing deposits there; and if p is not an output place of t either, m'(p) + 1 = m(p): p loses exactly 1 token, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: `One(place)` is an input arc whose required count and consumption count are both 1.
*While* the input place of a `One` input arc is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.
*While* the input place of a `One` input arc is marked and is not a correlated input of the transition's match specification ([NU-020]), the arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.
*When* a transition with a `One` input arc fires, it *shall* consume exactly 1 token from the input place.

*When* a transition with a `One` input arc fires, and the input place is neither a reset place nor an output place of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing holding exactly 1 fewer token than it held before the firing.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking with its deposit (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enables' are both read as 'some firing exists'.

Correlated inputs (ruling D30, extending D16): the third quoted sentence excludes a correlated input of a ν-net match specification (NU-020), on which the arc also requires a token of the chosen name. The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so every input place is one that is not a correlated input, and the second line quantifies over every `One` input arc. How a correlated input counts and consumes is NU-020's, not encoded here.

The first quoted sentence and the bullets (`requiredCount()` returns 1, `consumptionCount(available)` returns 1) are IO-007's contract for `One`. Here it is observed through firing: the required count is the second and third lines, the consumption count the fourth. The bullet values themselves are `io001_counts`.

AC1 (enables when the place has >= 1 token) is the second line (not with 0 tokens) and the third line (with >= 1 token the arc does not stand in the way; whether the other arcs allow the firing is theirs to say, IO-005 and CORE-022).

AC2 (exactly 1 token consumed on firing) is the fourth line for the count. Which token is consumed (the oldest) is below the count granularity of the firing semantics and is the glossary's reading of Consume (CORE-030); it is not encoded here.
AC3 (remaining tokens stay in the place) is the fourth line: p holds m(p) - 1 tokens plus the firing's deposit there afterwards.

Consumption is observed through the marking: p loses 1 and gains what the firing deposits there (p may also be an output place). A place that is both the input place and a reset place of t ends holding what the firing deposited there (CORE-034), so the consumed token is not visible in the marking; the fourth line excludes that case.

The deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count: on a place that t's output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc) no firing of t can deposit ([CORE-035]), so there the consumed token shows in the marking alone, as exactly 1 token fewer. Without this a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit of 1 in the input place would pass the count.
The input arc of t on p is the first input arc on p (glossary: Input arc), and t without its input arc on p drops that arc only; CORE-030 rejects a second input arc on p at build.

requirements.title: Input Exactly
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦
  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (n : ℕ),
    InputArc t p (Card.exactly n) →
      (while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p < n, never Fire F t) ∧
        (¬ResetArc t p →
          ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),
            F t m d m' →
              m' p + n = m p + Deposits d p ∧ (¬OutputArc t p → m' p + n = m p))
reading: For every transition t, place p and count N such that the input arc of t on p is Exactly(N):
t does not fire from a marking in which p holds fewer than N tokens;

unless p is also a reset place of t, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) + N = m(p) + d(p): p loses exactly N tokens, besides what the firing deposits there; and if p is not an output place of t either, m'(p) + N = m(p): p loses exactly N tokens, whatever deposit the firing reports.
quotes: `Exactly(place, n)` is an input arc whose required count and consumption count are both N, where N >= 1.
*While* the input place of an `Exactly(n)` input arc holds fewer than N tokens, the transition *shall not* fire.
*When* a transition with an `Exactly(n)` input arc fires, it *shall* consume exactly N tokens from the input place.

*When* a transition with an `Exactly(n)` input arc fires, and the input place is neither a reset place nor an output place of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing holding exactly N fewer tokens than it held before the firing.
assumes: A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking with its deposit (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Enables' is read as 'some firing exists'.

The first quoted sentence (required count N, consumption count N; the bullets `requiredCount()` returns N and `consumptionCount(available)` returns N) is IO-007's contract for `Exactly(n)`. Here it is observed through firing: the required count is the second line, the consumption count the third. The bullets' qualifier 'when available >= N' is implied: by the second line no firing starts with fewer.

AC1 (construction with N < 1 rejected, also when the transition is built from a spec written out without the constructor): a property of construction, not of firing, so the formula does not encode it.
