A clock restarted in a firing ([TIME-012]) is stamped the same way, by the next enablement update that finds the transition enabled.
*When* a transition is newly armed, the executor *shall* stamp it with the firing-clock reading taken by the enablement update that newly arms it ([EXEC-001] step 3).

The executor *shall not* arm a transition or give an armed transition a different stamp in any step other than an enablement update ([EXEC-001] step 3); another step may only take a stamp away ([TIME-012], [TIME-013]).

*When* the executor runs the enablement update of a cycle ([EXEC-001] step 3), it *shall* take the current reading of the firing clock, and the deadline step of that cycle ([EXEC-001] step 4) *shall* judge expiry at that reading or at a later reading it takes itself.
The firing pass and the decision to wait of a cycle *shall* judge elapsed time at the reading of its deadline step, and no other step of the cycle *shall* take a new reading for these judgements.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A name's clock status is off, armed with a stamp and a restart flag, or reaped; stampOf reads the stamp of an armed status. The state holds two readings of the one firing clock: now, the host's present reading, which only the outside delay step advances (TIME-015's companion line 1), and cyc, the cycle reading, which the enablement update sets (line 3) and the deadline step may move to a later reading (line 4); the deadline step, the ready order of the pass and the park decision judge at it (design R21). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), whose update re-evaluates every name (updSt).

This is the companion of the Phase 1 block TIME_010 (ruling D33 (a), design NR-1). That block states the clock on the atomic timed step, where a firing and the update that arms what it enables are one step; it defers to the cycle relation the reading a new stamp takes. Line 1 is that reading: a transition is newly armed when the update finds it enabled while it is not armed (off or reaped), or finds it enabled with a restart pending ([TIME-012]), and the new stamp is the cycle reading of that update. An executor that stamps with the reading of the cycle in which the arming firing started (the reading of the previous update) breaks line 1 (TIME_010_cycle_forbids_stampAtStart).

Line 2 is the new sentence that only the enablement update arms: a deposit, an injection, a firing or the return of an action never arms a transition or moves its stamp, though a start, a drop or a reap may take a clock away (TIME-012, TIME-013). An executor that arms what a commit enables at the moment of the commit, the moment an action completed, breaks line 2 (TIME_010_cycle_forbids_armOnCommit). Together the two lines give the quoted sentences on when the update sees a deposit: a synchronous deposit inside the pass is first armed by the next cycle's update, an asynchronous completion or an injected token by the update of the cycle whose step 1 or step 2 takes it in. TIME_010_cycle_nonvacuous shows both: b, enabled by a synchronous deposit in the pass of cycle reading 0, is stamped 5 by the update at reading 5; enabled by an asynchronous completion that returned at 3 and was committed at 7, it is stamped 7.

That an update does arm an enabled transition that is off is EXEC-001's line 8 (UpdateExact), with re-entrancy CONC-002's; that a reaped transition stays reaped until a write is TIME-013's companion. The first case of 'newly armed', a transition enabled in the initial marking, is the first update of a run from the initial state (xinit has every name off, design R19), which stamps it with the start reading.

The quoted 'shall not fire' sentences of TIME-010 are not lines here: a start needs a stamp (EXEC-003 line 1), and the earliest bound is judged at the cycle reading by the ready order of the pass (TIME-014 line 1 and its consequence TIME_014_not_before_earliest). The elapsed time is the glossary definition, read at the cycle reading (viewAt s s.cyc). AC1 and AC2 are the Phase 1 block's examples; on the executor the restart of AC2 is TIME-011, and the stamp the update takes on re-enablement is line 1.

Lines 3 to 5 are the two sentences on readings, ruling D61 (c): the enablement update takes the present reading, which is the stamp of what it newly arms (line 1); the deadline step judges expiry at that reading or at a later reading it takes itself, never at an earlier one (line 4); from the deadline step on the cycle reading is fixed, so the firing pass and the decision to wait judge at the deadline step's reading (line 5), as the ready order of the pass (TIME-014 line 1) and the park decision (CONC-010) read it. An update that keeps the reading of an older cycle breaks line 3 (TIME_010_cycle_forbids_staleUpdate), a deadline step that judges at a reading earlier than the update's breaks line 4 (TIME_010_cycle_forbids_deadlineRewind), and a pass that reads the clock again when it begins breaks line 5 (TIME_010_cycle_forbids_rereadAtBegin). With TIME-015's companion line 1 (the host reading never goes back) the readings of successive cycles are non-decreasing. These lines are TIME-010's, a MUST, and not TIME-015's, a SHOULD on the injectable clock: they hold of every executor on any firing clock.

The reference stamps at the update's reading and takes a reading of its own at the deadline step, the host's present one or the update's when the present is earlier (atDeadline: the second case of line 4 on every reachable state, where the cycle reading is never ahead of the present). Rust takes one reading per cycle and judges the deadline step, the pass and the park decision at it (executor_core/executor.rs:1064, :1070, :1102, :1145): a reference run with no delay between the update and the deadline step. TypeScript takes the update's reading and a second reading that its deadline step and its pass share (bitmap-net-executor.ts:715, :553): a reference run with a delay between them. Java takes three readings per cycle (BitmapNetExecutor.java:1292, :1451, :1528): its update and its deadline step are instances of lines 3 and 4, but its firing pass judges readiness at a third reading, which line 5 with TIME-014 line 1 rules out; that is a recorded executor defect, RD-16 in spec/runtime-defects.md.
Transition names are taken to be pairwise distinct (ruling D10, Cfg.WF.names, which the statement does not assume): the status is kept per name.

requirements.title: Clock Restarts on Re-enablement
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (X : TimedNet N),
    (∀ (l : TLbl N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
        InNet X u →
          on fun s s' ↦ R X s l s', shall fun s s' ↦
            Armed s u → ¬Enabled u s'.m → s'.stamp u.core.name = none) ∧
      ∀ (l : TLbl N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
        InNet X u →
          on fun s s' ↦ R X s l s', shall fun s s' ↦
            ¬Armed s u → Armed s' u → s'.stamp u.core.name = some (ClockReading s')
reading: For every timed net X:
a transition of the net that is armed before a step and is not enabled at the marking after it holds no stamp after the step;
a transition of the net that is not armed before a step and is armed after it holds the reading of the firing clock after the step.
quotes: If a transition stops being armed and is later armed again, the clock restarts from zero.
The previous elapsed time is discarded.
*When* an armed transition stops being enabled, the executor *shall* discard its stamp.
*When* a transition that lost its clock is armed again, its elapsed time *shall* be measured from the moment it was armed again, not from any earlier stamp.
assumes: A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic: the step that starts a firing completes it. Armed, Enabled and Elapsed time are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean): a transition is armed when it is enabled at the marking and holds a stamp.

Line 1 is the first 'shall' sentence. 'Discard its stamp' is read on the state: the transition holds no stamp after the step (none), not merely that it is not armed, which a transition that is not enabled never is. The line is the hygiene of the state the sentence literally asks for: no glossary predicate reads the stamp of a transition that is not enabled (Armed, Ready and Expired all ask for it enabled), and a stale stamp cannot be resumed because line 2 overwrites it when the transition is armed again. TIME_011_mutant_disarm_killed shows the line is not implied by its weaker 'disarm' reading, and time011_lazy_TIME_010 that the stale-stamp step it kills satisfies TIME-010. The line reads only the marking after the step: a transition disabled in the intermediate marking of a firing and enabled again after it is TIME-012 (ruling D7), whose pre-6.0.0 mutant (keep a stamp when enabled before and after, the intermediate marking playing no part) TIME_012_mutant_survivesOld_killed kills.

Line 2 is the second 'shall' sentence and the restart of the opening paragraph. A transition that is not armed before a step may still hold a stamp (a stale one, or none after a reap, [TIME-013]); no resume is possible because the line asks every such transition armed after the step to hold the current reading, overwriting whatever it held, so its elapsed time is 0 after the step and is measured from that reading. It is the stamp value of TIME-010 line 1 without TIME-010's question of which steps may arm (time011_line2_of_time010): next to TIME-010, line 1 is the only line this block adds (time011_iff_line1), and the resuming mutant it kills is the one TIME-010 kills too. Which steps re-arm (a firing that writes an arc place, ruling D6) is TIME-010, not this block.

'Measured from the moment it was armed again' over the later steps is TIME-010 line 2: a transition armed before and after a step keeps its stamp unless a firing restarts its clock ([TIME-012]). This block does not restate it: TIME-011 alone admits a delay that backdates the stamp of a transition that stays armed, which TIME-010 line 2 forbids (time011_backdate_gap). time011_elapsed_from_rearm derives the elapsed time after a delay from TIME-010 and TIME-011 together, which is how ConsistencyTime conjoins them.

An injected token can also disable or re-arm a transition ([ENV-003], ruling D6). Injection is not a step of the Phase 1 relation, which has no environment places; the two lines are stated for the steps it has.

Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10): a stamp is kept per name, and both lines speak of the transition the net holds under the name (InNet). Under pairwise distinct names (NamesDistinct) InNet is membership in the net (inNet_iff_mem).

AC1 (Delayed(5 s), disabled at 3 s, re-enabled later, waits another 5 s) is TIME_011_nonvacuous in milliseconds: u is armed at 0, a consumer takes its token at 3000 and u holds no stamp (line 1), the source refills the place at 7000 and u is armed with the stamp 7000 (line 2), u cannot fire at 11999 and can at 12000. The resuming mutant would let u fire at 7000. For every relation satisfying TIME-010 and TIME-011 whose delay advances the clock by the delay, a transition armed again cannot fire after a delay shorter than its earliest bound (time011_no_early_fire).

requirements.title: Clock Restart on Intermediate Disablement
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (X : TimedNet N),
    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
        InNet X u →
          u.core.name ≠ t.core.name →
            on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.fire t d) s', shall fun s s' ↦
              Armed s u →
                ¬Enabled u (Mid t s.m) →
                  (Enabled u s'.m →
                      Armed s' u ∧ s'.stamp u.core.name = some (ClockReading s')) ∧
                    (¬Enabled u s'.m → s'.stamp u.core.name = none)) ∧
      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
          InNet X u →
            u.core.name ≠ t.core.name →
              on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.fire t d) s', shall fun s s' ↦
                Armed s u →
                  Enabled u (Mid t s.m) →
                    Enabled u s'.m → s'.stamp u.core.name = s.stamp u.core.name) ∧
        ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
          InNet X u →
            u.core.name = t.core.name →
              on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.fire t d) s', shall fun s s' ↦
                Armed s u →
                  (Enabled u s'.m →
                      Armed s' u ∧ s'.stamp u.core.name = some (ClockReading s')) ∧
                    (¬Enabled u s'.m → s'.stamp u.core.name = none)
reading: For every timed net X:

a firing of t from a state in which the net's transition u, named differently from t, is armed and not enabled in the intermediate marking of t (taken from the state's marking) leaves u armed with the reading of the firing clock after the firing if u is enabled after it, and leaves u without a stamp otherwise;
a firing of t from a state in which the net's transition u, named differently from t, is armed and enabled in the intermediate marking of t, and after which u is enabled, leaves u's stamp as it was;

a firing of t from a state in which the net's transition u named like t (t itself when t is the net's transition of its name) is armed leaves u armed with the reading of the firing clock after the firing if u is enabled after it, and leaves u without a stamp otherwise.
quotes: The marking between the halves is the intermediate marking `M - Pre(t)` of Berthomieu and Diaz.
This holds even when `t`'s own outputs refill the place, and it holds whether `t`'s action completes synchronously or asynchronously: a synchronous action MUST NOT hide the gap.
The intermediate marking comes from the live marking `t` fires from: the tokens in the places when `t` fires, minus what `t` consumes.
*When* a transition `t` fires, each armed transition other than `t` that is not enabled in the intermediate marking *shall* lose its clock.
*When* a transition `t` fires, each armed transition other than `t` that is enabled in the intermediate marking and after the firing *shall* keep its stamp.
*When* a transition fires, it *shall* lose its clock.
*When* a transition `t` fires and a transition that lost its clock in that firing is enabled after it, that transition *shall* be newly armed ([TIME-010]).
assumes: A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic: the step that starts a firing completes it. Armed, Mid (the intermediate marking: inputs consumed, reset places drained, nothing deposited) and Enabled are the glossary terms.

The intermediate marking is computed from the marking of the state the firing step starts from, which is the live marking (ruling D7, revised). In a firing pass of several firings each firing is its own atomic step, so a token a synchronous action deposited earlier in the pass is in that marking and counts, as the section says. This agrees with a pass only for arcs that take a fixed number of tokens: a draining arc (reset, all(), atLeast(n)) later in a pass takes only the tokens present when the pass began ([EXEC-003] AC5), while Mid drains the live place. The section's bullet on reset places now carries the exception for this case (ruling 2): a same-pass deposit that the reset does not take ([EXEC-003] AC5) and that keeps the transition enabled in the intermediate marking keeps its clock. The Phase 1 relation has no pass, so a same-pass deposit never arises in it, and Mid draining the whole live place is the bullet without its exception; the exception, and an intermediate marking that keeps a deposit the reset does not take, are deferred to Phase 2 (RefExec). Outputs of an asynchronous action still in flight do not exist in the Phase 1 relation, which has no asynchronous actions. The enablement recheck of the pass ([EXEC-003] AC3-AC5) is not part of this block; see the next line. A synchronous action does not hide the gap: in the atomic Phase 1 step its deposit is the step's deposit d, which Mid t s.m never sees, so line 1 applies to a refill by the firing's own outputs (AC1). The asynchronous half is AC5, deferred below.

The fifth 'shall' sentence, 'If the enablement recheck of a firing pass finds a transition disabled ([EXEC-003] AC3), then the transition shall lose its clock, even when a same-pass deposit keeps it enabled in the live marking.', and the body's sentences on it (a transition the recheck finds disabled is disarmed even when a same-pass deposit refilled its place, and is newly armed, with a fresh stamp, by a later enablement update that finds it enabled) are not encoded and not quoted (ruling 1). The recheck judges a transition on the marking of the pass, which the atomic Phase 1 relation does not have: each firing is its own step and sees the live marking. Deferred to Phase 2 (RefExec), with the order of the two rules inside one pass: the intermediate-marking rule is applied at each firing on the live marking, and the recheck afterwards on the pass's marking, so a transition can keep its stamp through a firing by sentence 2 and then lose its clock to the recheck later in the same pass. The two rules are applied in sequence, they do not contradict each other.

To lose a clock is to hold no stamp after the firing. Sentences 1 and 4 together are line 1 of the formula: an armed transition other than t that is not enabled in the intermediate marking holds no stamp after the firing, unless it is enabled after it, in which case it is newly armed, that is armed with the current reading of the firing clock ([TIME-010]). Sentences 3 and 4 together are line 3, for the fired transition itself; it presupposes, as sentence 4 does, a clock to lose, so it speaks of the transition armed before the firing. An unarmed transition does not fire ([TIME-010] line 5). Line 2 is sentence 2. An armed transition enabled in the intermediate marking but not after the firing is disabled by the firing's deposit; that case is [TIME-011], not this block.

Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10): 'other than t' is 'named differently from t', and lines 1-3 speak of the transition the net holds under the name (InNet). Line 3 picks it by t's name, so a fired t that is not the net's transition of its name (a foreign or duplicate-named t) still restarts the clock under that name. The section assumes pairwise distinct names (NamesDistinct), under which InNet is membership in the net.

Bullet 1 (removing tokens never disables through an inhibitor arc) is time012_inhibitor_never: a transition enabled before whose input and read arcs still hold in the intermediate marking is enabled there. Its ν-join clause is not encoded: the Phase 1 relation has no ν correlation, it belongs to the NU blocks.

Bullet 2 (a reset arc drains its place) is time012_reset_disables, read as an input arc with a positive required count or a read arc on a reset place of t; with line 1 such a transition restarts its clock. Its exception for a same-pass deposit the reset does not take is Phase 2, as said above. An input arc whose required count is 0 stays enabled in a drained place and keeps its clock (the time012_Tzero conjuncts of TIME_012_ac3). Bullet 3 (surplus tokens keep the clock) is AC4. Bullet 4 (the fired transition always starts a fresh clock) is line 3.

AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 are the examples TIME_012_ac1 (input refill), TIME_012_ac2 (read only), TIME_012_ac3 (reset drain with a positive requirement) and TIME_012_ac4 (surplus keeps), in milliseconds, with T Delayed(5) and the refresh transition Immediate. TIME-012 fixes only the stamp a firing leaves; AC1's lower bound (T fires no earlier than d after the refill) follows from TIME-012 together with [TIME-010] lines 2 and 4, which frame the stamps across the other steps and gate the firing. TIME_012_ac1 shows the bound for the reference step: T does not fire 4 ms after the refill. AC5 (an asynchronous action) and AC6 (TransitionClockRestarted or TransitionEnabled) need in-flight actions and the event log, and are deferred to the Phase 2 executor; AC4's event clause (no TransitionClockRestarted or TransitionEnabled for T) needs the event log and is deferred with AC6. The state class graph's persistence rule ([VER-010]) is in Novel/TimedScg/Run.lean: persistence_rule, fired_never_persists, reset_restarts and surplus_keeps cite this ID.

A firing is instantaneous on the firing clock: that frame is not a sentence of this section and is not in the statement. Without it a firing fused with a hidden delay satisfies TIME-012 (TIME_012_gap_fireAdvancesClock); the frame is time012_FramesClock, which the reference satisfies (TIME_012_reference_framesClock) and which ConsistencyTime conjoins.
Injected tokens are not steps of the Phase 1 relation, which has no environment places, so injection plays no part here.

requirements.title: Clock Restart on Intermediate Disablement (executor cycle)
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    (∀ (n : String) (sy : Bool) (t : Reference.Trans N) (rest : List (Reference.Trans N))
        (m : String) (u : Reference.Trans N) (k : ℕ) (r : Bool),
        m ≠ n →
          findT C m = some u →
            on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.start n sy) s', shall fun s s' ↦
              s.order = t :: rest →
                s.st m = Status.armed k r →
                  s'.st m =
                    Status.armed k
                      (r || !Novel.Seam.enabledNA (qCount (liveAfter s t)) u.core)) ∧
      (∀ (n : String) (sy : Bool),
          on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.start n sy) s', shall fun x s' ↦
            s'.st n = Status.off) ∧
        (∀ (m : String) (u : Reference.Trans N) (k : ℕ),
            findT C m = some u →
              on fun s s' ↦ R C s XLbl.update s', shall fun s s' ↦
                s.st m = Status.armed k true →
                  Novel.Seam.enabledNA (qCount s.M) u.core = true →
                    s'.st m = Status.armed s'.cyc false) ∧
          (∀ (m : String) (u : Reference.Trans N) (k : ℕ),
              findT C m = some u →
                on fun s s' ↦ R C s XLbl.update s', shall fun s s' ↦
                  s.st m = Status.armed k false →
                    Novel.Seam.enabledNA (qCount s.M) u.core = true →
                      s'.st m = Status.armed k false) ∧
            (∀ (n : String),
                on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.lose n) s', shall fun x s' ↦
                  s'.st n = Status.off) ∧
              ∀ (l : XLbl N T) (n : String) (k : ℕ) (r : Bool),
                (∀ (n : String) (sy : Bool), l ≠ XLbl.start n sy) →
                  (∀ (n : String), l ≠ XLbl.lose n) →
                    (∀ (ns : List String), l ≠ XLbl.deadline ns) →
                      l ≠ XLbl.update →
                        on fun s s' ↦ R C s l s', shall fun s s' ↦
                          s.st n = Status.armed k r → s'.st n = Status.armed k r
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C:

a start step of the name n from a state whose pass order begins with t leaves every other name m, whose transition u the net holds and which is armed with stamp k and restart flag r, armed with stamp k, its restart flag set exactly when r was set or u is not enabled in the live intermediate marking of t (the pass-visible marking with t's consumption and drains applied, followed by the tokens deposited earlier in the pass);
a start step of the name n leaves n off;

an update step from a state in which name m, whose transition u the net holds, is armed with a restart pending and u is enabled at the marking, leaves m armed with the update's cycle reading as its stamp and no restart pending;

an update step from a state in which name m, whose transition u the net holds, is armed with its clock running (no restart pending) and u is enabled at the marking, leaves m armed with the stamp it held and no restart pending;
a lose step of the name n leaves n off;
a step other than a start, a lose step, a deadline step or an update leaves every armed name armed with the same stamp and the same restart flag.
quotes: The intermediate marking comes from the live marking `t` fires from: the tokens in the places when `t` fires, minus what `t` consumes.
Inside a firing pass this includes tokens a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same pass, because they are really there and a transition they keep enabled was never disabled.
Outputs of an asynchronous action still in flight are not in the marking yet, so they do not count.
A transition that the recheck finds disabled ([EXEC-003] AC3) is disarmed and loses its clock as well, even when a same-pass deposit refilled its place and keeps it enabled in the live marking.
It is newly armed, with a fresh stamp, by a later enablement update that finds it enabled ([TIME-010]).
*When* a transition `t` fires, each armed transition other than `t` that is not enabled in the intermediate marking *shall* lose its clock.
*When* a transition `t` fires, each armed transition other than `t` that is enabled in the intermediate marking and after the firing *shall* keep its stamp.
*When* a transition fires, it *shall* lose its clock.
*When* a transition `t` fires and a transition that lost its clock in that firing is enabled after it, that transition *shall* be newly armed ([TIME-010]).

*If* the enablement recheck of a firing pass finds a transition disabled ([EXEC-003] AC3), *then* the transition *shall* lose its clock, even when a same-pass deposit keeps it enabled in the live marking.

A reset arc drains its place, so every armed transition with a read arc on a reset place, or an input arc on it whose required count is positive, starts a fresh clock when it is enabled again, unless a same-pass deposit that the reset does not take ([EXEC-003] AC5) keeps it enabled in the intermediate marking.

*When* a firing pass starts a transition `t`, each other armed transition that is not enabled in the intermediate marking of `t` *shall* lose its clock at the next enablement update ([EXEC-001] step 3), even when a deposit before that update refills its places, and that update *shall* stamp it with the reading the update takes if it is enabled ([TIME-010]), after which its clock runs from that stamp.

Until that update the transition keeps its old stamp, so it can still start later in the same pass on that stamp if the recheck finds it enabled; this needs an inhibitor arc, because without one a transition that is not enabled in the intermediate marking of `t` is not enabled in the pass-visible marking at a later start either.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A firing is split: its start in the firing pass consumes and drains (the first half of the section), and its outputs are deposited by a later settle step (the second half). A name's clock status is off, armed with a stamp and a restart flag, or reaped (glossary: Status). liveAfter s t (GlossaryExec) is the marking right after a start of t: the pass-visible marking with t's consumption and drains applied, followed by the tokens deposited earlier in the pass. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), whose start applies afterStart and whose update applies updSt.

This is the companion of the Phase 1 block TIME_012 (ruling D33 (a), design NR-1), which states the rule on the atomic timed step and defers to the cycle relation the live intermediate marking inside a pass, the exception of the reset bullet for a same-pass deposit, the fifth shall sentence (the recheck) and AC5 (an asynchronous action). On the executor, 'loses its clock' in a firing is a restart flag the start sets (ruling D7, the intermediate marking taken from the live marking, liveAfter), and the clock is taken away by the next update, which restamps the transition and ends the restart if it is enabled (line 3) and leaves it off if it is not (EXEC-001 line 8, TIME-011). Line 1 is the first and second shall sentences at the start, line 3 the fourth with the new sentence ('stamp it with the reading the update takes ... after which its clock runs from that stamp'), line 4 the second at the update ('keep its stamp'), line 2 the third ('When a transition fires, it shall lose its clock'), line 5 the fifth, and line 6 the new sentence's 'even when a deposit before that update refills its places': no step between the start and the update gives the clock back or moves it.

Line 1 reads the intermediate marking from the live marking, as the quoted sentences ask: the tokens a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same pass count, so a transition they keep enabled keeps its clock, and a reset arc drains only the pass-visible tokens (EXEC-003 AC5), so a same-pass deposit it does not take keeps a transition enabled (the reset bullet's exception). Outputs of an asynchronous action in flight are not in the marking, so they do not count. An executor that takes the marking before the start breaks line 1 (TIME_012_cycle_forbids_restartBefore: a refill by the firing's own outputs would hide the gap, which a synchronous action must not do), and so does one that takes the pass-visible marking without the same-pass deposits (TIME_012_cycle_forbids_restartOnVis, the reset exception).

Line 3 is what makes a restart a restart: an executor that keeps the old stamp of a marked transition at the update (the rule before 6.0.0, survivesOld) breaks it (TIME_012_cycle_forbids_survivesOld). An update that restamps a marked transition and leaves the mark set breaks it too (TIME_012_cycle_forbids_stickyRestart): every later update would restamp it again and its clock would never run; the runtimes clear the mark at the end of the enablement scan (Rust bitmap_backend.rs:636-639, Java BitmapNetExecutor.java:1334-1336, TypeScript bitmap-net-executor.ts:778-781). Line 4 keeps a running clock: an update that restamps every armed transition breaks it (TIME_012_cycle_forbids_restampAll). Line 6: a commit whose deposit refills the place and clears the mark, the rule before 6.0.0 put in the deposit, breaks it (TIME_012_cycle_forbids_commitHeals). Line 2: a start that keeps its own transition's clock breaks it (TIME_012_cycle_forbids_startKeepsClock); under re-entrancy (ruling D8 (b)) the started transition is armed again, with a fresh stamp, by the next update that finds it enabled, as bullet 4 says. Line 5 overlaps EXEC-003 line 4, which states the same for a drop; it is kept here because it is TIME-012's fifth sentence: a loser loses its clock even when a same-pass deposit keeps it enabled in the live marking (TIME_012_cycle_forbids_loseKeepsClock). The two rules apply in sequence in one pass: a transition can keep its stamp through a start by line 1 and lose its clock to the recheck later in the same pass by line 5; TIME_012_cycle_nonvacuous shows it. A marked transition keeps its old stamp until the update (line 1), and a start needs only a stamp and the recheck on the pass-visible marking (EXEC-003 line 1), so it can still start later in the same pass on that stamp, as the quoted sentence says; the runtimes do the same, as their pass reads no mark (Rust bitmap_backend.rs:425-440 sets it, :626-639 reads and clears it in the scan). This takes an inhibitor arc: a same-pass deposit into an inhibitor place disables the transition in the live intermediate marking, which counts the deposit, but not in the pass-visible marking, which does not; without an inhibitor arc a transition disabled in the intermediate marking stays disabled in every later pass-visible marking of the pass.

Bullet 1 (an inhibitor arc never disables by a removal) and bullet 2 (a reset place restarts the clocks of transitions with a positive requirement on it or a read arc on it) are enabledNA read on liveAfter, as in the Phase 1 block. The ν-join clause of bullet 1 is the NU blocks', deferred with the ν firing kernel. The paragraph on the state class graph and on the events ([VER-010], [EVT-005], [EVT-004]) is not encoded here.

AC1 (a synchronous refill restarts T) is TIME_012_cycle_nonvacuous's first case: R starts and marks T, the update at reading 2 stamps T 2; that T then fires no earlier than 5 after the refill is TIME-014 line 1 with the stamp. AC2 (T only reads P) is the reset example's read arc and the Phase 1 block's TIME_012_ac2. AC3 (a reset drain) is the Phase 1 block's TIME_012_ac3, and its same-pass exception is the reset example here. AC4 (surplus tokens keep the clock) is the surplus case: T is not marked and keeps stamp 0 through the update at 2; its event clause is EVT's. AC5 (an asynchronous action restarts T as well) is the asynchronous case: R starts asynchronously and marks T, the next update finds T disabled and leaves it off, and the update after the completion arms it with the reading 3. AC6 (each restart emits exactly one of TransitionClockRestarted or TransitionEnabled) is EVT-004 and EVT-005 over the update, on the event model (W7).
Transition names are taken to be pairwise distinct (ruling D10, Cfg.WF.names, which the statement does not assume): line 1 judges the transition the net holds under m (findT).

requirements.title: Deadline Enforcement
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (X : TimedNet N),
    (∀ (u : Reference.Trans N),
        on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.reap u) s', shall fun s s' ↦
          u ∈ X.net.transitions ∧
            Expired X s u ∧
              Reaped s' u ∧
                s'.m = s.m ∧
                  ClockReading s' = ClockReading s ∧
                    ∀ (n : String), n ≠ u.core.name → s'.stamp n = s.stamp n) ∧
      (∀ (u : Reference.Trans N),
          while fun s ↦ Reapable X u ∧ (TimingOf X u).latest + Tolerance X < Elapsed s u,
            never fun s s' ↦ ∃ d, R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧
        (∀ (u : Reference.Trans N),
            while fun x ↦ ¬Reapable X u, never fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.reap u) s') ∧
          (∀ (u : Reference.Trans N),
              while fun s ↦ Reaped s u, never fun s s' ↦ ∃ d, R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧
            (∀ (l : TLbl N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
                InNet X u →
                  on fun s s' ↦ R X s l s', shall fun s s' ↦
                    Armed s u →
                      Reaped s' u → ∃ v, l = TLbl.reap v ∧ v.core.name = u.core.name) ∧
              (∀ (l : TLbl N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
                  InNet X u →
                    on fun s s' ↦ R X s l s', shall fun s s' ↦
                      Reaped s u →
                        Armed s' u →
                          ∃ t d, l = TLbl.fire t d ∧ ∃ p, ArcPlace u p ∧ Writes t d p) ∧
                (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N) (u : Reference.Trans N),
                    InNet X u →
                      on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.fire t d) s', shall fun s s' ↦
                        Reaped s u →
                          (∃ p, ArcPlace u p ∧ Writes t d p) →
                            Enabled u s'.m →
                              Armed s' u ∧
                                s'.stamp u.core.name = some (ClockReading s')) ∧
                  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N),
                      on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.fire t d) s', shall fun x x_1 ↦
                        t ∈ X.net.transitions) ∧
                    ∀ (u : Reference.Trans N) (s : TSt N),
                      u ∈ X.net.transitions → Expired X s u → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.reap u) s'
reading: For every timed net X:

a reap of u is of a transition of the net, is taken only from a state in which u is expired, and leaves u reaped, the marking, the reading of the firing clock and the stamp of every other name as they were;
no transition fires from a state in which it is reapable and its elapsed time is greater than its latest bound plus the tolerance;
no transition is reaped from a state in which it is not reapable;
no transition fires from a state in which it is reaped;
a step that leaves the net's transition u reaped, from a state in which u is armed, is a reap of a transition of u's name;
a step that leaves the net's transition u armed, from a state in which u is reaped, is a firing that writes one of u's arc places;
a firing that writes an arc place of the net's transition u, from a state in which u is reaped, leaves u armed with the reading of the firing clock if u is enabled after it;
a firing is of a transition of the net;
from every state in which a transition of the net is expired, the step relation has a reap of it.
quotes: When a reapable transition is expired, that is, armed with an elapsed time strictly greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance, the executor reaps it: it disarms the transition without firing it and emits a `TransitionTimedOut` event.

Implementations MUST apply a deadline tolerance — a grace band beyond `latest` (default 5ms) that absorbs timer-resolution and scheduling jitter — and SHOULD expose it as a configurable per-executor option (e.g. `deadlineTolerance` / `deadline_tolerance_ms`); a value of `0` gives strict enforcement.
Only `Deadline` and `Window` transitions are reaped here.
*If* a reapable transition's elapsed time is greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance, *then* the transition *shall not* fire.
The executor *shall not* reap a transition that is not reapable.
*While* a transition is reaped, the transition *shall not* fire.

*If* a reapable transition is armed and its elapsed time is greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance, *then* the executor *shall* reap it in the deadline step of that cycle ([EXEC-001] step 4) and emit `TransitionTimedOut` ([EVT-009]).

*When* a firing or an injected token writes one of a reaped transition's arc places (an input, read, inhibitor or reset place) and the transition is enabled afterwards, the transition *shall* be newly armed with a fresh clock ([TIME-010]).
A firing writes a place when it consumes from it, deposits into it or drains it through a reset arc; draining a reset place that is already empty counts as a write.
A reaped transition keeps its input tokens and is not armed again until one of its arc places is written, so an executor that fell behind can come to rest at a marking that still enables it.
assumes: A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic. Reapable, Expired, Reaped, Armed, Elapsed time, Arc place and Write are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean); Reaped is the state reading, enabled at the marking and not armed.

Line 1 reads the section's first paragraph as the definition of a reap step: it is taken only from an expired transition (reapable, armed, elapsed time strictly greater than its latest bound plus the tolerance, ruling D4), so the tolerance is applied, and it disarms that transition and nothing else, without firing it: the marking ("keeps its input tokens"), the clock reading and every other stamp stay. Several reaps in one deadline step are several reap steps.

Line 9 is the 'shall' sentence on reaping, and the first quoted sentence's 'the executor reaps it', as far as one atomic step can state them: from every state in which a transition of the net is expired, a reap of it is a step (the same condition as CoversReap, for this block; TIME-003 and TIME-005 state it for their timings). The step relation has no cycles and no events, so that the reap is taken, in the deadline step of the very cycle ([EXEC-001] step 4), and emits TransitionTimedOut ([EVT-009]) are deferred to Phase 2 and EVT. The atomic relation also lets another transition fire while u is expired (RefTStep does), and that firing may restart u's clock under [TIME-012], which a real cycle cannot do because its deadline step reaps before its firing pass; ClashesTime records this as a Phase 2 obligation (clash013_refresh_rescue).

The tolerance is the field TimedNet.tol, any natural number of milliseconds; the statement holds for every tolerance. Its default of 5 ms, the value 0 for strict enforcement and its exposure as a per-executor option (AC2) are configuration (kind N) and are not encoded.

Line 5 ties the state reading Reaped to the act of reaping: an armed transition becomes enabled and unarmed only by a reap of it, so a delay or a firing that silently drops the clock of an enabled transition is not a reap. Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10, InNet): the section assumes pairwise distinct names (NamesDistinct), and the reap of line 5 is of a transition of u's name.

Lines 1 and 8 make the transition of a reap or a firing label one of the net's. Without them a label outside the net that shares a name with a net transition but has another timing could reap or fire under that name, and lines 1 to 4 would check the label's timing, not the net's. Under distinct names a label of the net with u's name is u itself (time013_label_eq), so lines 1 to 5 speak of the net's transition (TIME_013_reap_is_of_u). Nets with two transitions of one name are outside ruling D10: the reference step itself then shares one stamp between them, so the statement does not speak to them.
Line 3 follows from line 1, as Expired includes Reapable (time013_line3_of_line1); it is kept so the quoted sentence on not reaping a non-reapable transition maps to one line.

Lines 6 and 7 are TIME-010's lines 1 and 3 read for a reaped transition (with line 1's fresh stamp in line 7), and are proven from the same policy-generic lemmas. A write is the glossary's Write (ruling D6): any arc place, not only an input place, and draining an empty reset place counts. The injected-token case of the last quoted 'shall' sentence is outside the step relation: injection is not a step of the Phase 1 relation, which has no environment places.

AC1 (a Deadline(5s) transition still armed past 5 s plus the tolerance does not fire after that bound; if it is still armed on the first cycle whose elapsed time is strictly greater than the bound, it is reaped in that cycle and TransitionTimedOut is emitted) is the nonvacuous example TIME_013_nonvacuous in milliseconds with tolerance 5: not reaped at elapsed 5005, reaped at 5006, and not fireable then. That the reap falls in the first such cycle is the cycle loop of Phase 2 (RefExec, [EXEC-001] step 4), and the TransitionTimedOut event is [EVT-009], deferred with it. AC3 (an Exact transition past its target is not disabled) is the same example: the Exact(3) transition, at elapsed 5006, cannot be reaped and fires. AC4 (a reaped transition does not fire until an arc place is written, then is armed again with a fresh clock and may fire) is the same example after the reap, ending with a firing of the re-armed transition; the backends (Bitmap, Precompiled) are Phase 2.

The paragraph on verification (quiescence reads a marking whose enabled transitions are all reapable as quiescent, Route B drops the latest bounds, assumeNoReaping) belongs to [VER-002], [VER-004] and [VER-012]; it is cited by ReapAware.rest_sound, not encoded here.

requirements.title: Deadline Enforcement (executor cycle)
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    (∀ (ns : List String),
        ∀ u ∈ C.X.net.transitions,
          on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.deadline ns) s', shall fun s s' ↦
            Expired C.X (viewAt s s'.cyc) u → s'.st u.core.name = Status.reaped) ∧
      (∀ (ns : List String) (n : String),
          on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.deadline ns) s', shall fun s s' ↦
            s'.M = s.M ∧
              (s'.st n ≠ s.st n →
                s'.st n = Status.reaped ∧
                  ∃ u ∈ C.X.net.transitions,
                    u.core.name = n ∧ Expired C.X (viewAt s s'.cyc) u)) ∧
        (∀ (n : String) (u : Reference.Trans N),
            findT C n = some u →
              on fun s s' ↦ R C s XLbl.update s', shall fun s s' ↦
                s.st n = Status.reaped → s'.st n = Status.reaped) ∧
          (∀ (l : XLbl N T) (n : String) (u : Reference.Trans N),
              findT C n = some u →
                on fun s s' ↦ R C s l s', shall fun s s' ↦
                  s.st n = Status.reaped →
                    s'.st n ≠ Status.reaped →
                      l = XLbl.lose n ∨ ∃ p ∈ arcPlaces u, p ∈ cycWrites s l) ∧
            ∀ (l : XLbl N T) (n : String) (u : Reference.Trans N),
              findT C n = some u →
                on fun s s' ↦ R C s l s', shall fun s s' ↦
                  s.st n = Status.reaped →
                    (∃ p ∈ arcPlaces u, p ∈ cycWrites s l) → s'.st n = Status.off
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C:
a deadline step from s to s' leaves reaped every transition of the net that is expired in s at the reading of the deadline step (the cycle reading of s');

a deadline step from s to s' leaves the marking as it was and changes the status of a name only to reaped, and only of a name of a transition of the net that is expired in s at the reading of the deadline step;
an update step leaves reaped every name of a transition of the net that is reaped before it;
a step that takes a name of a transition u of the net out of the reaped status writes one of u's arc places, or is a lose step of that name;
a step that writes one of the arc places of a transition u of the net, from a state in which u's name is reaped, leaves that name off.
quotes: When a reapable transition is expired, that is, armed with an elapsed time strictly greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance, the executor reaps it: it disarms the transition without firing it and emits a `TransitionTimedOut` event.

*If* a reapable transition is armed and its elapsed time is greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance, *then* the executor *shall* reap it in the deadline step of that cycle ([EXEC-001] step 4) and emit `TransitionTimedOut` ([EVT-009]).
The executor *shall not* reap a transition that is not reapable.

*When* a firing or an injected token writes one of a reaped transition's arc places (an input, read, inhibitor or reset place) and the transition is enabled afterwards, the transition *shall* be newly armed with a fresh clock ([TIME-010]).
*While* a transition is reaped, an enablement update *shall* leave it reaped, and only a firing or an injected token that writes one of its arc places *shall* end its reaped state.
The deadline step *shall* judge expiry at its reading of the firing clock ([TIME-010]), and it *shall not* reap a transition that is not expired at that reading or change the marking.
A firing writes a place when it consumes from it, deposits into it or drains it through a reset arc; draining a reset place that is already empty counts as a write.
A reaped transition keeps its input tokens and is not armed again until one of its arc places is written, so an executor that fell behind can come to rest at a marking that still enables it.
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A name's clock status is off, armed with a stamp and a restart flag, or reaped (glossary: ReapedE). Expired is the glossary term, read on the timed view of the state at the reading of the deadline step (viewAt s s'.cyc: the marking and the stamps before the step, the reading the step judges at, which is the update's reading or a later one, TIME-010's companion lines 3 to 5, ruling D61 (c)): reapable, armed, elapsed time strictly greater than the latest bound plus the tolerance (ruling D4). Write is the glossary term at the grain of the executor, cycWrites: a start writes the input and reset places of its transition, a commit or a timeout deposit the places of its emission, a publication the places of its batch, an injection the place of its token. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean).

This is the companion of the Phase 1 block TIME_013 (ruling D33 (a), design NR-1), which encodes the reap as far as one atomic step can (a reap is available from every expired transition, and only from one) and defers to the cycle relation that the reap is taken, in the deadline step of the very cycle, and the injected-token clause. Line 1 is the 'shall reap it in the deadline step of that cycle' sentence: the deadline step reaps every transition expired at its reading, which is the reading the update of that cycle took or a later one (TIME-010's companion, ruling D61 (c)); so a transition still armed in the first cycle whose reading puts it strictly past its bound is reaped in that cycle (AC1's second sentence, TIME-015 AC6). An executor that reaps one cycle late breaks it (TIME_013_cycle_forbids_reapLate). That the transition does not fire in the pass of that cycle is EXEC-001 line 6 with EXEC-003 line 1 (a start needs a stamp, a reaped name has none), and that the pass comes after the deadline step is EXEC-001 line 2, which excludes the refresh rescue of ClashesTime (clash013_refresh_rescue).

Line 2 is the first quoted sentence ('it disarms the transition without firing it'), the new sentence that the deadline step judges at its reading, reaps nothing that is not expired at it and does not change the marking, and the shall sentence on not reaping a transition that is not reapable: the deadline step reaps only expired transitions, so only reapable ones (Exact, Immediate and Delayed transitions are never expired, TIME-006), keeps their tokens ('keeps its input tokens') and changes no other status. An executor that reaps at the bound instead of strictly past it breaks it (TIME_013_cycle_forbids_reapAtBound). That the deadline step emits TransitionTimedOut is EVT-009's, on the event model (W7).

Lines 3 and 4 are the new shall sentence (design R9) and the last quoted sentence: an update leaves a reaped transition reaped (an executor that re-evaluates every transition re-arms it, re-reaps it and emits a TransitionTimedOut storm: TIME_013_cycle_forbids_reEvaluateAll), and only a write of one of its arc places ends the reaped state (TIME_013_cycle_forbids_injectWritesAll: an injection into another place unreaps it). Line 4 also allows a lose step of the name: a firing pass drops only names of its ready order (EXEC-003 line 3), which holds only ready, hence armed, transitions (TIME-014 line 1), so in a run from an initial state a reaped name is never dropped; the line speaks of every state of R, and a state whose pass order holds a reaped name is not reachable. The reference drop turns the dropped name off whatever its status (loseStep, Reference/Exec.lean), so the line keeps that case instead of the quoted sentence naming it; the sentence's 'only a firing or an injected token' speaks of the runs an executor takes.

Line 5 is the shall sentence on a write, at the grain of the executor: a firing that writes an arc place (its start consumes or drains it, its settle deposits into it, a publication deposits into it) or an injected token that lands in one ends the reaped state, and the next update arms the transition with its reading if it is enabled (TIME-010's companion line 1 and EXEC-001 line 8). This is the glossary's injection clause of Write, which the Phase 1 relation leaves out (GlossaryTime.lean, Writes). An executor whose injection does not count as a write keeps the transition reaped for ever (TIME_013_cycle_forbids_injectNoWrite). AC4 (a reaped transition does not fire while none of its arc places is written; once one is written it is armed again with a fresh clock and may fire) is lines 3 to 5 with TIME-010's companion: TIME_013_cycle_nonvacuous reaps u, keeps it reaped through an update and through an injection into another place, ends the reaped state by an injection into its input place, arms it at the next update and starts it three ms later. AC4's two backends are CONC-020's and the precompiled link (ExecLink).

The sentence 'While a transition is reaped, the transition shall not fire' is EXEC-003 line 1: a start needs a stamp, which a reaped name does not hold. The sentence 'If a reapable transition's elapsed time is greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance, then the transition shall not fire' is line 1 with EXEC-001 line 2 and TIME-014 line 1: the deadline step reaps the transition before the pass, and the pass's order holds only ready transitions, which are not expired. Both stay quoted by the Phase 1 block. AC2 (the tolerance is configurable, 5 ms by default) and AC3 (an Exact transition past its target is not disabled) are the Phase 1 block's; AC3 follows here from line 2. The tolerance is TimedNet.tol; the examples take 0 (strict enforcement), which TIME-015 asks for under an injected clock.

Transition names are taken to be pairwise distinct (ruling D10, Cfg.WF.names, which the statement does not assume): the status is kept per name, and lines 3 to 5 judge the transition the net holds under the name (findT).

requirements.title: Competitive Scheduling with Timing
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  (∀ (C : Cfg N T) (s s' : XSt N T) (tr : List (XStep N T)),
      XRun R C s ((s, XLbl.begin, s') :: tr) →
        time014_offers (time014_pass tr) <+: time014_orderNames C s ∧
          ∀ (w : List (XStep N T)) (st : XStep N T),
            time014_close tr = (w, some st) →
              time014_isTerminal st = false → time014_offers w = time014_orderNames C s) ∧
    (∀ (C : Cfg N T) (s s' : XSt N T) (tr : List (XStep N T)),
        XRun R C s ((s, XLbl.update, s') :: tr) →
          ∀ (mid : List (XStep N T)) (c d : XSt N T)
            (rest : List (XSt N T × XLbl N T × XSt N T)),
            tr = mid ++ (c, XLbl.begin, d) :: rest →
              (∀ x ∈ mid, x.2.1 ≠ XLbl.update) → s.now ≤ c.cyc) ∧
      ∀ (C : Cfg N T) (s : XSt N T) (ns : List String) (s' : XSt N T)
        (tr : List (XStep N T)),
        XRun R C s ((s, XLbl.deadline ns, s') :: tr) →
          ∀ (mid : List (XStep N T)) (c d : XSt N T)
            (rest : List (XSt N T × XLbl N T × XSt N T)),
            tr = mid ++ (c, XLbl.begin, d) :: rest →
              (∀ x ∈ mid, time014_rereads x.2.1 = false) → c.cyc = s'.cyc
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C:

in every run of R that opens with a begin step from state s, read up to the next begin step, the names of its start and lose steps, in order, are a prefix of the names of the ready order of EXEC-002 at the cycle reading of s (readyOrder C s);

in every such run, if the pass closes, at the first step whose label a pass cannot hold (anything but a start, a lose, a settle of a synchronous firing, or an outside step), and that step is not a terminal finish, the start and lose steps before it name the whole of that order;

in every run of R that opens with an update step from state s, the cycle reading at the next begin step, with no other update step between, is not earlier than the host reading of s, the update's reading; and in every run of R that opens with a deadline step to state s', the cycle reading at the next begin step, with no update or deadline step between, is the cycle reading of s', the deadline step's reading.
quotes: When multiple transitions compete for the same tokens, timing interacts with priority:
Higher priority transitions are preferred.

*While* several ready transitions compete for the same tokens, the executor *shall* fire them in the order of [EXEC-002], so the transition with the highest priority takes the tokens first ([EXEC-003]).

*While* a `Delayed` transition is armed and its elapsed time is less than its earliest bound, it *shall not* fire, so a ready transition competing for the same tokens takes them first whatever their priorities ([TIME-004]).
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A firing pass opens with a begin step, which fixes the pass's order, then takes the head of that order once per step: start, the head starts, or lose, it cannot start and its clock is lost; endPass ends the pass. 'Fire' is read as 'start': a firing starts in the pass and settles in a later step (EXEC-001). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), whose Phase 5 follows the Rust executor (executor_core/executor.rs, Phase 5: the ready list is walked, a transition that fails its recheck is disabled).

readyOrder C s is the reference order of EXEC-002 over the timed view of s at its cycle reading (viewAt s s.cyc), the reading the deadline step of the cycle took, which the pass and the park decision judge at (ruling D61 (c)): the ready transitions sorted by priority descending, stamp ascending and declaration order ascending, and on the all-immediate fast path in declaration order (ruling D14 (a)). Ready is the glossary term: armed, elapsed time at least the earliest bound, not expired. Line 1 fixes the order to that function, so this block is also EXEC-002's executor line: the pass starts its firings in that order.

Transitions are read by name throughout, under ruling D10 (NamesDistinct, part of Cfg.WF): line 1 compares the names a pass offers with the names of the order, so with two transitions of one name a start of the one that is not ready would pass for the one that is. Nets with duplicate names are outside the block, as they are outside TIME-013.

The first shall sentence is lines 1 and 2: the pass offers the ready transitions in the order of EXEC-002, one start or lose for each in turn (line 1), and does not close before it has offered every one of them (line 2), so no ready transition is passed over. A pass closes at its first step whose label it cannot hold: endPass, a park or a wake, a step of steps 1 to 4, a termination test, or the next begin. It can hold start and lose, the settle (commit, fail, tdeposit) of a synchronous firing inside its own pass (ruling D70 (a)), and the outside steps, which come at any time (CONC-001). Line 1 alone does not exclude a pass that stops early; an executor whose gate is one tick late ends the pass at the bound of the fallback transition without offering it and breaks only line 2 (TIME_014_forbids_lateGate), and so does an executor whose pass breaks at its first lose and goes on to step 1 without an endPass (the break-for-continue slip in the Phase 5 loop, TIME_014_forbids_breakOnLose). An executor that offers the lower priority first breaks line 1 (TIME_014_forbids_lowFirst).

Scope of the window: line 1 reads a pass up to the next begin step, so a run that starts inside a pass says nothing about that pass (EXEC-003 says a start takes the head of the pass's order). Because line 1 runs to the next begin and line 2 makes the pass offer the whole order before it closes, no start or lose may come between the close of a pass and the next begin; this is EXEC-001's step order (start and lose are step 5), not an addition to it. A pass that a terminal place stops (EXEC-042: nothing later in the pass fires) closes with a terminal finish, so line 2 does not apply to it. A run cut before its pass closes says nothing under line 2: that the pass closes at all is liveness, which no line here states. Re-entrancy (ruling D8 (b)) changes nothing here: a transition in flight that may not start again is off after the update, so it is not ready and not in the order.

The consequence 'so the transition with the highest priority takes the tokens first ([EXEC-003])' is line 1 together with EXEC-003, whose statement holds both halves over the same model: its line 3 lets a lose happen only for a head that is not armed or not enabled on the pass-visible marking, and its line 2 fixes what a start consumes. So an executor that offers the right order and turns every offer into a lose satisfies this block and breaks EXEC-003. TIME_014_nonvacuous shows two Immediate transitions on one token: the one of priority 10 starts, the one of priority -10 loses.

The second shall sentence follows from line 1: the ready order holds only ready transitions (EXEC-002 line 1), so a transition started in the pass was ready at the cycle reading of the pass, its elapsed time at least its earliest bound (TIME_014_started_ready); under distinct names (ruling D10) a transition armed below its earliest bound at that reading is not started in that pass (TIME_014_not_before_earliest). Its clause 'so a ready transition competing for the same tokens takes them first whatever their priorities' is line 2 with EXEC-003: the ready competitor is in the order and is offered, the Delayed one is not. TIME_014_nonvacuous shows it with a Delayed transition of priority 10 and an Immediate one of priority -10 on one token: only the Immediate one is in the order, and it starts. An executor that offers every transition of the net by priority, ready or not (as clash014_allOrder orders them), starts the Delayed one first and breaks line 1 (TIME_014_forbids_allOrder). The Phase 1 form of the gate is TIME-010 line 4 (time010_gate).

Line 3 is ruling D61 (c) as far as the pass needs it, in two halves. The reading the pass judges at is the deadline step's reading: no step between the deadline step and the begin step moves it. And it is not earlier than the host reading the update of its cycle took, the reading that stamps what the update newly arms (TIME-010's companion, line 1), so the elapsed time of the second shall sentence and the Ready of the first are measured at the present cycle and not at an older reading. Without that half lines 1 and 2 hold of an executor that never renews its reading (the clock reading hoisted out of the loop): a Delayed transition then never reaches its earliest bound at the cycle reading and never fires, and line 3 rejects it (TIME_014_forbids_staleReading). The reference stamps at the update's reading and takes a reading of its own at the deadline step, never an earlier one (atDeadline), which the pass and the park decision share. A run with no delay between the update and the deadline step is an executor that takes one reading per cycle, as Rust does (executor_core/executor.rs, cycle_now); a run with a delay between them is an executor that takes a second reading after its update, as TypeScript does (updateDirtyTransitions stamps at its own reading, and cycleNowMs, taken after it, is shared by the deadline step and the pass, typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts). TIME_014_twoReadings shows the reference start a Delayed(3000) transition in the cycle whose update armed it at reading 0 and whose deadline step ran at 3000. A pass that takes a reading of its own when it begins and judges readiness there breaks line 1 at the reading line 3 fixes (TIME_014_forbids_passReread). Java's fireReadyGeneral takes such a third reading (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java, and the same in PrecompiledNetExecutor.java), a recorded executor defect, RD-16 in spec/runtime-defects.md. How the deadline step and the park decision use the reading is TIME-013's companion and CONC-010's, not this block's.

The first quoted sentence introduces the bullets; the bullet 'Higher priority transitions are preferred.' is EXEC-002's priority sort, which line 1 applies to the pass. The second bullet is read as ruling D9 (b) restricts it, to a Delayed transition before its earliest bound, whatever the priorities; once both are ready the order of EXEC-002 applies, stamp included. Read as an ordering rule, Immediate before Delayed whenever priorities are equal, it contradicts EXEC-002 (TIME_014_bullet2_order_conflicts_EXEC_002, ClashesTime.lean), and an executor that offers Immediate first breaks line 1 when the Delayed transition was armed first (TIME_014_forbids_immediateFirst). The third bullet, the fallback, is AC2: the fallback starts in the first pass whose cycle reading is at or after its earliest bound, if it is still armed (its clock not restarted, TIME-012) and the high-priority transition is not also ready in that pass.

AC1 (T1 with priority 10 and Immediate, also taking an event token from a second input place that holds one, and T2 with priority -10 and Delayed(3s), on one shared input; T1 fires first) is checked on the reference: in the first pass T2 is armed but not in the order, and T1 starts (TIME_014_nonvacuous). AC2 is read with the scenario of ruling D9 (b) and R-EXEC-5 (b), the requirement's own test derivation (the primary action waits for an event): T1's event place stays empty, so T1 is not enabled, T2 is armed at 0, the pass at reading 0 offers nothing, the executor waits with a timer of 3000 ms, and at cycle reading 3000 the order is T2 alone and T2 starts. The reading where T1 is in flight when a new token arrives holds on Java and TypeScript only (on Rust T1 starts again), so it is not used.

AC2's 'becomes ready and fires' is these lines together with two requirements outside the block. Line 3 makes a cycle whose update runs at or after 3000 judge at a reading not earlier, lines 1 and 2 put T2 in the order of its pass and offer it, and EXEC-003 line 3 forbids a lose of T2 while it is armed and enabled, so it starts. That a cycle runs at all once 3000 ms have passed, that is, that the wait wakes on its timer, is CONC-010's (step 6): an executor that parks for ever has only finite runs that stop before the bound, and every line holds of them. TIME_014_nonvacuous shows the reference doing it, and the update step at host reading 3000 that line 3 reads.
The test derivation (PrimaryAction with priority 10 and Immediate against FallbackAction with priority -10 and a delay of 3s) is the net of the AC1 and AC2 examples, transitions primary and fallback.

requirements.title: Injectable Clock
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (X : TimedNet N),
    (∀ (l : TLbl N),
        on fun s s' ↦ R X s l s', shall fun s s' ↦ ClockReading s ≤ ClockReading s') ∧
      (∀ (δ : ℕ),
          on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.delay δ) s', shall fun s s' ↦
            ClockReading s' = ClockReading s + δ) ∧
        (∀ (δ : ℕ) (u : Reference.Trans N),
            on fun s₀ s ↦ R X s₀ (TLbl.delay δ) s, shall fun s₀ s ↦
              Armed (AfterWait s₀ s) u →
                Elapsed (AfterWait s₀ s) u < (TimingOf X u).earliest →
                  ∀ (d : List N) (s' : TSt N), ¬R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧
          ∀ (δ : ℕ) (u : Reference.Trans N),
            on fun s₀ s ↦ R X s₀ (TLbl.delay δ) s, shall fun s₀ s ↦
              Expired X (AfterWait s₀ s) u →
                ∀ (d : List N) (s' : TSt N), ¬R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s'
requirements.scope: all executors, on the default or an injected firing clock
reading: For every timed net X:
no step lowers the reading of the firing clock;
a delay of δ advances the reading by exactly δ;
no transition fires from the state a delay of any length reached if, read with the stamps held before the delay, it is armed there and its elapsed time is below its earliest bound;
no transition fires from the state a delay of any length reached if, read with the stamps held before the delay, it is expired there.
quotes: *While* an executor runs on an injected clock, successive readings of its firing clock *shall* be non-decreasing.

*When* the executor's wait completes, the executor *shall* re-check its boundary conditions before it fires any transition, so an armed transition *shall not* fire before its earliest bound because a wait completed early ([TIME-010]).
assumes: A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock (ClockReading) and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). The relation has one firing clock and does not say where its readings come from, so the block holds of the default clock as of an injected one. The epoch clock (token creation times, [CORE-011]) is not modelled: the Phase 1 marking is token counts. Injected tokens are not steps of the Phase 1 relation.

Line 1 of the formula is the first 'shall' sentence, over every step. A host reading that goes backwards cannot be written as a delay, since a delay's length is a natural number: across a wait, the sentence is carried by that type together with line 2, and a clock that rewinds on a delay breaks lines 1 and 2 at once (TIME_015_forbids_rewind). Line 1 on its own constrains firings and reaps: one that lowers the reading breaks it alone (TIME_015_mutant_waitOnly_killed).

Line 2 says a delay moves the clock by its length; it is the only statement of that fact, and TIME-003 to TIME-006 rely on it through ConsistencyTime for the elapsed time of their transitions to grow with the clock (their clock frame keeps the stamp across a delay, GlossaryTime ClockFrame). That a firing and a reap take no time (an atomic step happens at one reading) is a convention of the Phase 1 relation, not a sentence of this section, so it is not a line of this block; its firing half is time012_FramesClock, which ConsistencyTime conjoins, and its reap half is [TIME-013] line 1 (a reap leaves the clock reading as it is). Which reading stamps a transition armed by a firing is not fixed by the spec text and is open: the model takes the firing step's own reading (refPolicy.fresh), while a runtime that samples the clock once per cycle stamps it with the reading of the next cycle's enablement update, and an asynchronous action's outputs arm at its completion reading ([TIME-012] AC5, deferred).

Contract 1's other half (the clock is not assumed to advance between two reads) is not a line of this block. A repeated reading is a delay of 0; that one is offered is CoversDelay, and that it changes nothing else is TIME-010's framing of stamps across a delay together with FramesMarking. The reference meets it (time015_stutter).

Lines 3 and 4 are the second 'shall' sentence. A completed wait is a delay step of any length: the executor cannot tell an early or spurious completion from a due one, so both lines quantify over every delay. The boundary conditions are read in AfterWait: the marking and reading after the wait with the stamps held before it, so that a wait that rewrites or drops stamps cannot hide an early firing (TIME_015_mutant_inState_killed, TIME_015_forbids_dropStamps). For a relation that keeps stamps across a delay, as TIME-010 line 2 asks, AfterWait is the state the wait reached.

Line 3 is the earliest side, which the sentence names. Line 4 is the latest side of 'its boundary conditions': a transition that is expired (glossary: reapable, armed, elapsed time strictly greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance; rulings D2 and D4) does not fire after a wait that overshot. Exact transitions are not reapable and are never expired [TIME-006]. With TIME-010 and FramesMarking, line 3 holds of every relation (time015_ac4_of_time010, cited for AC4).

AC6: the reap test, that with tolerance 0 a Deadline transition can be reaped exactly when it is armed and its elapsed time is strictly greater than its bound, is the cited theorem time015_ac6_reap_strict (the strict test of TIME-013, ruling D4). That the reap happens on the first such cycle is a property of the executor loop and is deferred to Phase 2.

AC10 is not encoded: its ruling (D12) is open. The clash is recorded, and cited for TIME-015, with the other TIME clashes (ClashesTime.lean): if its 'same outcome' quantifies over strictly increasing clocks that may skip a window, the reference refutes it (time015_ac10_coarse_jump: a Window(3, 5) transition with tolerance 0 fires under a clock advancing 1 ms per reading, and is reaped, its token stranded, under the readings 0 then 10); repeated readings alone change nothing (refTStepW_delay_zero: a delay of 0 is an identity step; time015_stutter here is the converse, that such a step exists).

AC1, AC2, AC3, AC9, AC12, AC14 and AC15 are properties of the seam, its default path, its documentation and its identifiers (configuration, N kind), not of a step relation. AC5, AC7, AC8 and AC11 are properties of the executor loop (abort, the boundary short-circuit, wake-up, reentrant admission) and AC13 of token stamping through the epoch clock; they are deferred to Phase 2.

requirements.title: Injectable Clock (executor cycle)
requirements.statement:
fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦
  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),
    (∀ (l : XLbl N T), on fun s s' ↦ R C s l s', shall fun s s' ↦ s.now ≤ s'.now) ∧
      ∀ (s0 : XSt N T) (tr : List (XStep N T)),
        XRun R C s0 tr → (after tcIsWake, until isUpdate, never isStart) tr
requirements.scope: all executors, on the default or an injected firing clock
reading: For every executor R and every configuration C:
no step lowers the host's reading of the firing clock;
in every run of R, after a step that completes the wait (a wake), no start happens before the next update.
quotes: *While* an executor runs on an injected clock, successive readings of its firing clock *shall* be non-decreasing.

*When* the executor's wait completes, the executor *shall* re-check its boundary conditions before it fires any transition, so an armed transition *shall not* fire before its earliest bound because a wait completed early ([TIME-010]).
The executor MUST re-check its boundary conditions and MUST NOT treat "the wait completed" as "the boundary is reached".
assumes: The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The state holds two readings of the one firing clock: now, the host's present reading, which only the outside delay step advances, and cyc, the cycle reading, which the enablement update sets and the deadline step may move to a later reading, and at which the deadline step, the ready order of the pass and the park decision judge (TIME-010's companion lines 3 to 5, ruling D61 (c)). The model does not say where the readings come from, so line 1 holds of the default clock as of an injected one: the quoted sentence opens with 'While an executor runs on an injected clock' because an injected clock is the one the host can get wrong; the default firing clocks are monotonic sources (System.nanoTime, performance.now, a monotonic Instant), so the line asks nothing of them they do not do. The wait of step 6 is park and wake; a wake is offered at any time in the wait, so a timer that fires early and a spurious completion are both a wake. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean).

This is the companion of the Phase 1 block TIME_015 (ruling D33 (a), design NR-1), which states the readings and the re-check on the atomic timed step and defers the executor loop to the cycle relation. Line 1 is the first shall sentence on the host's reading: a clock that goes back breaks it (TIME_015_cycle_forbids_rewind). Which reading each step of a cycle judges at (ruling D61 (c)) is an executor rule for every executor on any clock, so it is stated by TIME-010 (a MUST) and its companion, lines 3 to 5, not here: the SHOULD priority of TIME-015 does not carry it. With line 1 those lines make the readings of successive cycles non-decreasing.

Line 2 is the second shall sentence and contract 3 (spurious completion): after the wait completes the loop runs steps 1 to 4 again, so the enablement update re-reads the clock and the deadline step and the ready order of the next pass are judged at that reading, and a transition whose earliest bound a wait that completed early did not reach is not ready in that pass (TIME-014 line 1). An executor that trusts the wait and goes straight to its firing pass breaks it (TIME_015_cycle_forbids_wakeToPass). That the update comes before the deadline step and the deadline step before the pass is EXEC-001 lines 1 and 2, whose trigger includes the wake.

AC4 (a wait that completes early fires nothing early) is TIME_015_cycle_nonvacuous: t, Delayed(5) and armed at 0, parks with a timer of 5, the wait completes at 2, the update takes reading 2 and the pass offers nothing, the next wait completes at 5 and t starts. AC6 (with tolerance 0, a Deadline transition is reaped on the first cycle strictly past its bound, not on one that observes exactly its bound) is TIME-013's companion line 1 at the reading of the deadline step (TIME-010's companion lines 3 and 4), and TIME_013_cycle_nonvacuous shows both cycles. AC7 (a boundary already due advances on the next cycle) is CONC-010's park guard: the executor does not wait while a transition is Ready or Expired at the cycle reading, and its timer is at most the next boundary plus the timer resolution. AC8 (a completing action, an injected event, a drain and a close wake the wait) is CONC-010's wake line. AC11 (an injection or a completion from inside the wait only enqueues, and is taken in by a later step 1 or step 2) is CONC-001 line 1 (an outside step changes neither the marking nor a clock status) with ENV-003 and EXEC-001; ruling D70 (a) lets the wait itself take the queued item and go on to step 1. AC13 (executor-stamped tokens carry the injected epoch clock) is the CORE-011 epoch slice (W11). AC5 (abort on shutdown), AC9 (no cost on the default path), AC15 (an absent boundary suspends) and the seam's shape (both halves of the wait, the readiness predicate, the two time bases) are properties of the host interface, not of a step relation; the wait without a timer is park none, which CONC-010 allows only when no boundary is ahead. AC1, AC2, AC3, AC10, AC12 and AC14 are the Phase 1 block's.

requirements.title: SMT Verification Pipeline
requirements.statement:
fun {N} [DecidableEq N] V X ↦
  (∀ (net : Reference.Net N) (m0 : Novel.Seam.NMarking N),
      (V net m0).places =
        net.places ++ List.filter (fun p ↦ decide (p ∉ net.places)) m0.places) ∧
    (∀ (net : Reference.Net N) (m0 : Novel.Seam.NMarking N),
        (V net m0).transitions = net.transitions) ∧
      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),
          ¬DrainedForward t →
            ∃ rows,
              X t = some rows ∧
                ∃ acts tos,
                  List.Forall₂ SamePerPlace (List.map Prod.snd rows) (acts ++ tos) ∧
                    (∀ (i : ℕ),
                        acts[i]? =
                          deposit (timeoutRequired t) t.out
                            (Novel.ForwardDeposit.Choice.action i)) ∧
                      ((tos = [] ∧
                          ∀ (d : List N),
                            deposit (timeoutRequired t) t.out
                                  (Novel.ForwardDeposit.Choice.timedOut 0) =
                                some d →
                              ∃ b ∈ acts, SamePerPlace b d) ∨
                        ∃ d,
                          tos = [d] ∧
                            deposit (timeoutRequired t) t.out
                                  (Novel.ForwardDeposit.Choice.timedOut 0) =
                                some d ∧
                              ∀ b ∈ acts, ¬SamePerPlace b d)) ∧
        (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (rows : List (VirtualRow N)),
            X t = some rows →
              List.map Prod.fst rows =
                List.map (virtualName t.core.name rows.length) (List.range rows.length)) ∧
          ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N), DrainedForward t → X t = none
reading: For every verified-net function V and expansion X, where X is the expansion every route reads:
the places of V net m0 are the places of net followed by the places m0 marks that net does not hold, in m0's order;
